    for b, d in ((2, 2), (3, 2), (3, 3), (5, 4)):
        nodes, leaves = tree_counts(b, d)
        print(f"branching {b}, depth {d}: {nodes} nodes in total, {leaves} leaves")
    print("branching 3 at depth 2 gives 13 nodes and 9 leaves, matching the hand count, and the totals grow fast enough that exploring every branch is its own cost problem")

    section("2. Genuinely measuring: restart from scratch against checkpoints, 60 steps at 97 percent per step")
    p, n = 0.97, 60
    rr = random.Random(11)
    a = [run_with_restart(rr, p, n, 5) for _ in range(4000)]
    rr = random.Random(11)
    b = [run_with_checkpoints(rr, p, n, 10, 5) for _ in range(4000)]
    print(f"restart (5 attempts):          success {mean(x[0] for x in a):.3f} | mean steps executed {mean(x[1] for x in a):.1f}")
    print(f"checkpoint every 10 (5 retries each): success {mean(x[0] for x in b):.3f} | mean steps executed {mean(x[1] for x in b):.1f}")
    print("with the same per-step reliability, checkpoints finished far more tasks and spent fewer executed steps in total, because a failure only repeats at most ten steps; the probabilities are invented and the two runs share a seed but not a random stream, so treat the gap as indicative")

    section("3. Genuinely measuring: checkpoint spacing")
    for every in (2, 5, 10, 20, 60):
        rr = random.Random(21)
        res = [run_with_checkpoints(rr, p, n, every, 5) for _ in range(3000)]
        print(f"checkpoint every {every:2d} steps: success {mean(x[0] for x in res):.3f} | mean steps executed {mean(x[1] for x in res):.1f}")
    print("very sparse checkpoints behave like restarting, and very dense ones save more work but, in a real system, each checkpoint costs time and storage that this lab does not charge for")

    section("4. Genuinely computing and simulating: best-of-N retries")
    rr = random.Random(5)
    for pp in (0.3, 0.6):

            sim = mean(best_of_n(rr, pp, k) for _ in range(20000))

    print("trying several times helps a lot when the tries are independent and a checker can tell which one worked; if the checker is wrong or the failures are correlated, the formula overstates the benefit")

    rr = random.Random(9)

    hits = 0

        task_is_hard = rr.random() < 0.5
        p_local = 0.05 if task_is_hard else 0.95
        hits += best_of_n(rr, p_local, 4)

Part 2 of 3: branching trees of attempts, restarting from scratch compared with checkpoints, checkpoint spacing, best-of-N retries checked against a simulation and correlated failures that break the independence assumption. Every output below was genuinely produced by the lab file on Python 3.14.5. This is our own stdlib model of the ideas behind long-horizon agents (METR-style time horizons, compounding per-step reliability, checkpoints, retries, memory compaction and trajectory monitors), not the real software, and the success probabilities, step counts and the scripted agent are made up by the lab and no language model is involved, so no real LLM behaviour is measured. ಪ್ರಯತ್ನಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def tree_counts(branching, depth):
    nodes = sum(branching ** d for d in range(depth + 1))
    leaves = branching ** depth
    return nodes, leaves


def run_with_restart(r, p_step, n_steps, max_attempts):
    """A failure anywhere sends the whole task back to step 0. Returns (success, steps_executed)."""
    executed = 0
    for _ in range(max_attempts):
        done = True
        for _s in range(n_steps):
            executed += 1
            if r.random() >= p_step:
                done = False
                break
        if done:
            return True, executed
    return False, executed


def run_with_checkpoints(r, p_step, n_steps, checkpoint_every, max_retries_per_segment):
    """A failure only rewinds to the last checkpoint. Returns (success, steps_executed)."""
    executed = 0
    pos = 0
    while pos < n_steps:
        seg_end = min(pos + checkpoint_every, n_steps)
        for _ in range(max_retries_per_segment):
            ok = True
            for _s in range(pos, seg_end):
                executed += 1
                if r.random() >= p_step:
                    ok = False
                    break
            if ok:
                break
        else:
            return False, executed
        pos = seg_end
    return True, executed


def best_of_n(r, p, n):
    return any(r.random() < p for _ in range(n))"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"lh_2.py","headingEn":"main(): experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() counts tree nodes, compares restart and checkpoints, varies checkpoint spacing, checks best-of-N and shows correlated failures.","descKn":"main() ಮರದ ನೋಡ್ ಎಣಿಸಿ, ಮರುಪ್ರಾರಂಭ ಮತ್ತು checkpoints ಹೋಲಿಸಿ, checkpoint ಅಂತರ ಬದಲಿಸಿ, best-of-N ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ಸಹಸಂಬಂಧಿತ ವೈಫಲ್ಯಗಳನ್ನು ತೋರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    section("1. Genuinely computing: size of a branching tree of attempts")
    for b, d in ((2, 2), (3, 2), (3, 3), (5, 4)):
        nodes, leaves = tree_counts(b, d)
        print(f"branching {b}, depth {d}: {nodes} nodes in total, {leaves} leaves")
    print("branching 3 at depth 2 gives 13 nodes and 9 leaves, matching the hand count, and the totals grow fast enough that exploring every branch is its own cost problem")

    section("2. Genuinely measuring: restart from scratch against checkpoints, 60 steps at 97 percent per step")
    p, n = 0.97, 60
    rr = random.Random(11)
    a = [run_with_restart(rr, p, n, 5) for _ in range(4000)]
    rr = random.Random(11)
    b = [run_with_checkpoints(rr, p, n, 10, 5) for _ in range(4000)]
    print(f"restart (5 attempts):          success {mean(x[0] for x in a):.3f} | mean steps executed {mean(x[1] for x in a):.1f}")
    print(f"checkpoint every 10 (5 retries each): success {mean(x[0] for x in b):.3f} | mean steps executed {mean(x[1] for x in b):.1f}")
    print("with the same per-step reliability, checkpoints finished far more tasks and spent fewer executed steps in total, because a failure only repeats at most ten steps; the probabilities are invented and the two runs share a seed but not a random stream, so treat the gap as indicative")

    section("3. Genuinely measuring: checkpoint spacing")
    for every in (2, 5, 10, 20, 60):
        rr = random.Random(21)
        res = [run_with_checkpoints(rr, p, n, every, 5) for _ in range(3000)]
        print(f"checkpoint every {every:2d} steps: success {mean(x[0] for x in res):.3f} | mean steps executed {mean(x[1] for x in res):.1f}")
    print("very sparse checkpoints behave like restarting, and very dense ones save more work but, in a real system, each checkpoint costs time and storage that this lab does not charge for")

    section("4. Genuinely computing and simulating: best-of-N retries")
    rr = random.Random(5)
    for pp in (0.3, 0.6):
        for k in (1, 3, 5):
            sim = mean(best_of_n(rr, pp, k) for _ in range(20000))
            print(f"single-try success {pp}, {k} tries: formula {1 - (1 - pp) ** k:.3f} | simulated {sim:.3f}")
    print("trying several times helps a lot when the tries are independent and a checker can tell which one worked; if the checker is wrong or the failures are correlated, the formula overstates the benefit")

    section("5. Genuinely running: correlated failures break the independence assumption")
    rr = random.Random(9)
    trials = 20000
    hit_independent = mean(best_of_n(rr, 0.5, 4) for _ in range(trials))
    hits = 0
    for _ in range(trials):
        task_is_hard = rr.random() < 0.5
        p_local = 0.05 if task_is_hard else 0.95
        hits += best_of_n(rr, p_local, 4)
    print(f"independent tries at 0.5 each, 4 tries: {hit_independent:.3f}")
    print(f"same average (0.5) but half the tasks are hard (5 percent) and half easy (95 percent), 4 tries: {hits / trials:.3f}")
    print("both setups average 50 percent per try, yet four tries succeed far less often when the failures are concentrated on the hard tasks, so retries cannot rescue tasks the agent systematically cannot do; the 5 and 95 percent split is invented")"}},{"type":"output","data":{"output":"

compact ಹಳೆಯ ಇತಿಹಾಸವನ್ನು ಸಾರಾಂಶವಾಗಿ ಮಡಚುತ್ತದೆ ಮತ್ತು monitor ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ ಹಾಗೂ ಅತಿ ಉದ್ದ trajectory ಗುರುತಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"class ScriptedAgent:
    """Stand-in agent: works through a fixed list of steps; the 'tool' just appends to a result list."""

    def __init__(self, steps):
        self.steps = steps

    def act(self, i):
        return {"tool": "work", "arg": self.steps[i]}


def run(steps, ckpt_path, crash_at=None, max_steps=100, start_fresh=False):
    ckpt = Path(ckpt_path)
    state = {"next": 0, "done": []}
    if ckpt.exists() and not start_fresh:
        state = json.loads(ckpt.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    agent = ScriptedAgent(steps)
    executed = []
    taken = 0
    while state["next"] < len(steps):
        if taken >= max_steps:
            return state, executed, "step budget"
        i = state["next"]
        if crash_at is not None and i == crash_at:
            return state, executed, "crashed"
        action = agent.act(i)
        executed.append(i)
        state["done"].append(action["arg"])
        state["next"] = i + 1
        ckpt.write_text(json.dumps(state), encoding="utf-8")
        taken += 1
    return state, executed, "finished"


def compact(history, keep_recent):
    if len(history) <= keep_recent:
        return history, 0
    old, recent = history[:-keep_recent], history[-keep_recent:]
    summary = {"summary_of": len(old), "first": old[0], "last": old[-1]}
    return [summary] + recent, len(old)


def monitor(trajectory, repeat_limit=3, step_limit=12):
    """Return the first problem found in a list of (tool, arg) pairs, or None."""
    run_len = 1
    for i in range(1, len(trajectory)):
        run_len = run_len + 1 if trajectory[i] == trajectory[i - 1] else 1
        if run_len >= repeat_limit:
            return f"repeat of {trajectory[i]} {run_len} times at step {i + 1}"
    if len(trajectory) > step_limit:
        return f"step count {len(trajectory)} exceeds limit {step_limit}"
    return None"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"lh_3.py","headingEn":"main(): experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() crashes and resumes, repeats the crash without a checkpoint, enforces a step budget, compacts a history and runs the monitor.","descKn":"main() crash ಮಾಡಿ ಮುಂದುವರಿಸಿ, checkpoint ಇಲ್ಲದೆ crash ಪುನರಾವರ್ತಿಸಿ, ಹಂತ ಬಜೆಟ್ ಜಾರಿಗೊಳಿಸಿ, ಇತಿಹಾಸ ಸಂಕ್ಷೇಪಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ಮಾನಿಟರ್ ಓಡಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():

    """Stand-in agent: works through a fixed list of steps; the 'tool' just appends to a result list."""

    def __init__(self, steps):
        self.steps = steps

    def act(self, i):
        return {"tool": "work", "arg": self.steps[i]}


def run(steps, ckpt_path, crash_at=None, max_steps=100, start_fresh=False):
    ckpt = Path(ckpt_path)
    state = {"next": 0, "done": []}
    if ckpt.exists() and not start_fresh:
        state = json.loads(ckpt.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    agent = ScriptedAgent(steps)
    executed = []
    taken = 0
    while state["next"] < len(steps):
        if taken >= max_steps:
            return state, executed, "step budget"
        i = state["next"]
        if crash_at is not None and i == crash_at:
            return state, executed, "crashed"
        action = agent.act(i)
        executed.append(i)
        state["done"].append(action["arg"])
        state["next"] = i + 1
        ckpt.write_text(json.dumps(state), encoding="utf-8")
        taken += 1
    return state, executed, "finished"


def compact(history, keep_recent):
    if len(history) <= keep_recent:
        return history, 0
    old, recent = history[:-keep_recent], history[-keep_recent:]
    summary = {"summary_of": len(old), "first": old[0], "last": old[-1]}
    return [summary] + recent, len(old)

    run_len = 1

        if run_len >= repeat_limit:
            return f"repeat of {trajectory[i]} {run_len} times at step {i + 1}"
    if len(trajectory) > step_limit:

ಏರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def make_problems(r, tier, n):
    lo, hi = TIERS[tier]
    return [(r.randint(lo, hi), r.randint(lo, hi)) for _ in range(n)]


def generate(r, comp, tier, a, b):
    """Returns (answer, good_reasoning). A wrong path still lands on the right answer one time in three (offset 0 is 2 of the 6 choices), which is the shortcut."""
    if r.random() < comp[tier]:
        return a + b, True
    off = r.choice([-2, -1, 0, 0, 1, 2])
    return a + b + off, False


def rationalize(r, tier, a, b, hint_success=0.6):
    """Given the correct answer as a hint, the model writes a rationale that reaches it; assumed to be good reasoning only some of the time."""
    return (r.random() < hint_success)


def star_round(r, comp, n, use_rationalization, lr=0.6):
    stats = {}
    for tier in TIERS:
        probs = make_problems(r, tier, n)
        kept_good = kept_short = rat_good = 0
        for a, b in probs:
            ans, good = generate(r, comp, tier, a, b)
            if ans == a + b:
                if good:
                    kept_good += 1
                else:
                    kept_short += 1
            elif use_rationalization and rationalize(r, tier, a, b):
                rat_good += 1
        stats[tier] = (kept_good, kept_short, rat_good)
    for tier, (g, s, rg) in stats.items():
        rate = (g + rg) / n
        comp[tier] = min(0.99, comp[tier] + lr * rate * (1 - comp[tier]))
    return stats


def accuracy(r, comp, tier, n=400):
    probs = make_problems(r, tier, n)
    return mean(generate(r, comp, tier, a, b)[0] == a + b for a, b in probs)"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"st_1.py","headingEn":"main(): experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() shows what the filter keeps, runs five rounds with and without rationalization, repeats over ten seeds and reports the shortcut share of the kept data.","descKn":"main() ಶೋಧಕ ಏನು ಇಡುತ್ತದೆ ತೋರಿಸಿ, rationalization ಇಲ್ಲದೆ ಮತ್ತು ಇರುವಂತೆ ಐದು ಸುತ್ತು ಓಡಿಸಿ, ಹತ್ತು seeds ಮೇಲೆ ಪುನರಾವರ್ತಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ಇಟ್ಟ ದತ್ತಾಂಶದ ಶಾರ್ಟ್‌ಕಟ್ ಪಾಲು ವರದಿ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    section("1. Genuinely running: what the answer filter keeps in round 0 (200 problems per tier)")
    r = random.Random(1)
    comp = dict(START)
    st = {}
    for tier in TIERS:
        probs = make_problems(r, tier, 200)
        g = s = 0
        for a, b in probs:
            ans, good = generate(r, comp, tier, a, b)
            if ans == a + b:
                g, s = (g + 1, s) if good else (g, s + 1)
        st[tier] = (g, s)
        print(f"{tier:6} competence {comp[tier]:.2f}: kept {g + s:3d} of 200 | genuine {g:3d} | shortcut {s:3d}")
    print("the filter keeps every rationale whose final answer is right, including wrong-path rationales that landed on the right answer by luck, so the kept set is a little contaminated and the hard tier gives the least training data; competence values are invented starting points")

    section("2. Genuinely running: five STaR rounds without and with rationalization (seed 3)")
    for flag in (False, True):
        r = random.Random(3)
        comp = dict(START)
        print(f"rationalization = {flag}")
        for rnd in range(1, 6):
            star_round(r, comp, 200, flag)
            acc = {t: accuracy(r, comp, t) for t in TIERS}
            print(f"  round {rnd}: accuracy easy {acc['easy']:.2f} medium {acc['medium']:.2f} hard {acc['hard']:.2f}")
    print("each round trains only on kept rationales, so the easy tier saturates first and the hard tier moves slowly; adding hint-based rationalization gives the hard tier extra training examples from problems the model got wrong, and the numbers come from invented update rules")

    section("3. Genuinely measuring: ten seeds, hard-tier accuracy after five rounds")
    res = {False: [], True: []}
    for flag in (False, True):
        for seed in range(1, 11):
            r = random.Random(seed)
            comp = dict(START)
            for _ in range(5):
                star_round(r, comp, 200, flag)
            res[flag].append(comp["hard"])
    for flag in (False, True):
        print(f"rationalization = {flag}: mean hard competence {mean(res[flag]):.3f} | min {min(res[flag]):.3f} | max {max(res[flag]):.3f}")
    print("both settings were run on the same ten seeds; the difference comes straight from the update rule and the assumed 60 percent hint success, so it shows how rationalization could help and is not evidence about any real STaR run")

    section("4. Genuinely running: the shortcut fraction of the kept data by tier")
    r = random.Random(5)
    comp = dict(START)
    for tier in TIERS:
        g = s = 0
        for a, b in make_problems(r, tier, 5000):
            ans, good = generate(r, comp, tier, a, b)
            if ans == a + b:
                g, s = (g + 1, s) if good else (g, s + 1)
        print(f"{tier:6} kept {g + s:4d} of 5000 | shortcut share of kept: {s / (g + s):.3f}")
    print("the weaker the model is on a tier, the larger the share of its kept rationales that reached the right answer by a wrong path, because those are the only kept examples; an answer-only filter therefore gets less trustworthy exactly where the model is weakest")"}},{"type":"output","data":{"output":"

ಏರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def make_problems(r, tier, n):
    lo, hi = TIERS[tier]
    return [(r.randint(lo, hi), r.randint(lo, hi)) for _ in range(n)]


def generate(r, comp, tier, a, b):
    """Returns (answer, good_reasoning). A wrong path still lands on the right answer one time in three (offset 0 is 2 of the 6 choices), which is the shortcut."""
    if r.random() < comp[tier]:
        return a + b, True
    off = r.choice([-2, -1, 0, 0, 1, 2])
    return a + b + off, False


def rationalize(r, tier, a, b, hint_success=0.6):
    """Given the correct answer as a hint, the model writes a rationale that reaches it; assumed to be good reasoning only some of the time."""
    return (r.random() < hint_success)


def star_round(r, comp, n, use_rationalization, lr=0.6):
    stats = {}
    for tier in TIERS:
        probs = make_problems(r, tier, n)
        kept_good = kept_short = rat_good = 0
        for a, b in probs:
            ans, good = generate(r, comp, tier, a, b)
            if ans == a + b:
                if good:
                    kept_good += 1
                else:
                    kept_short += 1
            elif use_rationalization and rationalize(r, tier, a, b):
                rat_good += 1
        stats[tier] = (kept_good, kept_short, rat_good)
    for tier, (g, s, rg) in stats.items():
        rate = (g + rg) / n
        comp[tier] = min(0.99, comp[tier] + lr * rate * (1 - comp[tier]))
    return stats


def accuracy(r, comp, tier, n=400):
    probs = make_problems(r, tier, n)
    return mean(generate(r, comp, tier, a, b)[0] == a + b for a, b in probs)"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"st_1.py","headingEn":"main(): experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() shows what the filter keeps, runs five rounds with and without rationalization, repeats over ten seeds and reports the shortcut share of the kept data.","descKn":"main() ಶೋಧಕ ಏನು ಇಡುತ್ತದೆ ತೋರಿಸಿ, rationalization ಇಲ್ಲದೆ ಮತ್ತು ಇರುವಂತೆ ಐದು ಸುತ್ತು ಓಡಿಸಿ, ಹತ್ತು seeds ಮೇಲೆ ಪುನರಾವರ್ತಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ಇಟ್ಟ ದತ್ತಾಂಶದ ಶಾರ್ಟ್‌ಕಟ್ ಪಾಲು ವರದಿ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    section("1. Genuinely running: what the answer filter keeps in round 0 (200 problems per tier)")
    r = random.Random(1)
    comp = dict(START)
    st = {}
    for tier in TIERS:
        probs = make_problems(r, tier, 200)
        g = s = 0
        for a, b in probs:
            ans, good = generate(r, comp, tier, a, b)
            if ans == a + b:
                g, s = (g + 1, s) if good else (g, s + 1)
        st[tier] = (g, s)
        print(f"{tier:6} competence {comp[tier]:.2f}: kept {g + s:3d} of 200 | genuine {g:3d} | shortcut {s:3d}")
    print("the filter keeps every rationale whose final answer is right, including wrong-path rationales that landed on the right answer by luck, so the kept set is a little contaminated and the hard tier gives the least training data; competence values are invented starting points")

    section("2. Genuinely running: five STaR rounds without and with rationalization (seed 3)")
    for flag in (False, True):
        r = random.Random(3)
        comp = dict(START)
        print(f"rationalization = {flag}")
        for rnd in range(1, 6):
            star_round(r, comp, 200, flag)
            acc = {t: accuracy(r, comp, t) for t in TIERS}
            print(f"  round {rnd}: accuracy easy {acc['easy']:.2f} medium {acc['medium']:.2f} hard {acc['hard']:.2f}")
    print("each round trains only on kept rationales, so the easy tier saturates first and the hard tier moves slowly; adding hint-based rationalization gives the hard tier extra training examples from problems the model got wrong, and the numbers come from invented update rules")

    section("3. Genuinely measuring: ten seeds, hard-tier accuracy after five rounds")
    res = {False: [], True: []}
    for flag in (False, True):
        for seed in range(1, 11):
            r = random.Random(seed)
            comp = dict(START)
            for _ in range(5):
                star_round(r, comp, 200, flag)
            res[flag].append(comp["hard"])
    for flag in (False, True):
        print(f"rationalization = {flag}: mean hard competence {mean(res[flag]):.3f} | min {min(res[flag]):.3f} | max {max(res[flag]):.3f}")
    print("both settings were run on the same ten seeds; the difference comes straight from the update rule and the assumed 60 percent hint success, so it shows how rationalization could help and is not evidence about any real STaR run")

    section("4. Genuinely running: the shortcut fraction of the kept data by tier")
    r = random.Random(5)
    comp = dict(START)
    for tier in TIERS:
        g = s = 0
        for a, b in make_problems(r, tier, 5000):
            ans, good = generate(r, comp, tier, a, b)
            if ans == a + b:
                g, s = (g + 1, s) if good else (g, s + 1)
        print(f"{tier:6} kept {g + s:4d} of 5000 | shortcut share of kept: {s / (g + s):.3f}")
    print("the weaker the model is on a tier, the larger the share of its kept rationales that reached the right answer by a wrong path, because those are the only kept examples; an answer-only filter therefore gets less trustworthy exactly where the model is weakest")"}},{"type":"output","data":{"output":"

answers, pick_random, pick_majority and pick_verified choose one, and rate repeats the draw to estimate how often the choice is right.","descKn":"candidates N ಉತ್ತರ ಎಳೆಯುತ್ತದೆ, pick_random, pick_majority ಮತ್ತು pick_verified ಒಂದನ್ನು ಆರಿಸುತ್ತವೆ, ಮತ್ತು rate ಆಯ್ಕೆ ಎಷ್ಟು ಬಾರಿ ಸರಿ ಎಂದು ಅಂದಾಜಿಸಲು ಎಳೆಯುವುದನ್ನು ಪುನರಾವರ್ತಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def candidates(r, p, n, wrong_pool=7):
    """n candidate answers; each is the right answer 0 with probability p, else one of wrong_pool wrong answers (1..wrong_pool)."""
    return [0 if r.random() < p else r.randint(1, wrong_pool) for _ in range(n)]


def pick_random(r, c):
    return r.choice(c)


def pick_majority(r, c):
    cnt = Counter(c)
    top = max(cnt.values())
    return r.choice([k for k, v in cnt.items() if v == top])


def pick_verified(r, c, tpr, fpr):
    """Verifier accepts a right candidate with probability tpr and a wrong one with probability fpr; pick randomly among accepted, else fall back to random."""
    accepted = [x for x in c if r.random() < (tpr if x == 0 else fpr)]
    return r.choice(accepted) if accepted else r.choice(c)


def rate(fn, p, n, trials, seed, **kw):
    r = random.Random(seed)
    return mean(fn(r, candidates(r, p, n), **kw) == 0 for _ in range(trials))"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"st_2.py","headingEn":"main(): experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() compares the rules with the formula, varies verifier error rates, adds correlated failures and trains a threshold verifier.","descKn":"main() ನಿಯಮಗಳನ್ನು ಸೂತ್ರದೊಂದಿಗೆ ಹೋಲಿಸಿ, ಪರಿಶೀಲಕ ದೋಷ ದರ ಬದಲಿಸಿ, ಸಹಸಂಬಂಧಿತ ವೈಫಲ್ಯ ಸೇರಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ಮಿತಿ ಪರಿಶೀಲಕಕ್ಕೆ ತರಬೇತಿ ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    T = 20000
    section("1. Genuinely measuring: random pick, majority vote and a perfect checker against the formula (p = 0.3)")
    for n in (1, 4, 16):
        ideal = 1 - (1 - 0.3) ** n
        rnd = rate(pick_random, 0.3, n, T, 1)
        maj = rate(pick_majority, 0.3, n, T, 1)

        print(f"N={n:2d}: formula {ideal:.3f} | perfect verifier {ver:.3f} | majority {maj:.3f} | random {rnd:.3f}")

    section("2. Genuinely measuring: verifier errors cap the gain (p = 0.3, N = 16)")

        v = rate(pick_verified, 0.3, 16, T, 2, tpr=tpr, fpr=fpr)
        print(f"verifier true-positive {tpr:.1f}, false-positive {fpr:.1f}: success {v:.3f}")
    print("success falls as the false-positive rate rises and equals the base rate 0.300 when the verifier accepts right and wrong answers equally often, so a weak verifier can make extra samples worthless; the rates are invented")

    section("3. Genuinely measuring: when failures are correlated, more samples help less (N = 16)")

    print("a perfect verifier cannot select an answer that was never sampled, so the gain is bounded by how often the right answer appears at all; the 0.02 and 0.58 split is invented")

    """n candidate answers; each is the right answer 0 with probability p, else one of wrong_pool wrong answers (1..wrong_pool)."""
    return [0 if r.random() < p else r.randint(1, wrong_pool) for _ in range(n)]


def pick_random(r, c):
    return r.choice(c)


def pick_majority(r, c):
    cnt = Counter(c)
    top = max(cnt.values())
    return r.choice([k for k, v in cnt.items() if v == top])


def pick_verified(r, c, tpr, fpr):
    """Verifier accepts a right candidate with probability tpr and a wrong one with probability fpr; pick randomly among accepted, else fall back to random."""
    accepted = [x for x in c if r.random() < (tpr if x == 0 else fpr)]
    return r.choice(accepted) if accepted else r.choice(c)


def rate(fn, p, n, trials, seed, **kw):
    r = random.Random(seed)
    return mean(fn(r, candidates(r, p, n), **kw) == 0 for _ in range(trials))"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"st_2.py","headingEn":"main(): experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() compares the rules with the formula, varies verifier error rates, adds correlated failures and trains a threshold verifier.","descKn":"main() ನಿಯಮಗಳನ್ನು ಸೂತ್ರದೊಂದಿಗೆ ಹೋಲಿಸಿ, ಪರಿಶೀಲಕ ದೋಷ ದರ ಬದಲಿಸಿ, ಸಹಸಂಬಂಧಿತ ವೈಫಲ್ಯ ಸೇರಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ಮಿತಿ ಪರಿಶೀಲಕಕ್ಕೆ ತರಬೇತಿ ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    T = 20000
    section("1. Genuinely measuring: random pick, majority vote and a perfect checker against the formula (p = 0.3)")
    for n in (1, 4, 16):
        ideal = 1 - (1 - 0.3) ** n
        rnd = rate(pick_random, 0.3, n, T, 1)
        maj = rate(pick_majority, 0.3, n, T, 1)
        ver = rate(pick_verified, 0.3, n, T, 1, tpr=1.0, fpr=0.0)
        print(f"N={n:2d}: formula {ideal:.3f} | perfect verifier {ver:.3f} | majority {maj:.3f} | random {rnd:.3f}")
    print("a perfect checker matches 1 - (1 - p)^N, random choice never improves on p, and majority vote helps here only because wrong answers are spread over seven values while the right one is a single value; if wrong answers agreed with each other majority vote would fail")

    section("2. Genuinely measuring: verifier errors cap the gain (p = 0.3, N = 16)")
    for tpr, fpr in ((1.0, 0.0), (0.9, 0.1), (0.9, 0.3), (0.7, 0.3), (0.5, 0.5)):
        v = rate(pick_verified, 0.3, 16, T, 2, tpr=tpr, fpr=fpr)
        print(f"verifier true-positive {tpr:.1f}, false-positive {fpr:.1f}: success {v:.3f}")
    print("success falls as the false-positive rate rises and equals the base rate 0.300 when the verifier accepts right and wrong answers equally often, so a weak verifier can make extra samples worthless; the rates are invented")

    section("3. Genuinely measuring: when failures are correlated, more samples help less (N = 16)")
    r = random.Random(4)
    hits = 0
    for _ in range(T):
        hard = r.random() < 0.5
        p = 0.02 if hard else 0.58
        c = candidates(r, p, 16)
        hits += pick_verified(r, c, 1.0, 0.0) == 0
    print(f"average p is 0.30 but half the problems are hard (0.02) and half easy (0.58): perfect-verifier success {hits / T:.3f} against the independent formula {1 - 0.7 ** 16:.3f}")
    print("a perfect verifier cannot select an answer that was never sampled, so the gain is bounded by how often the right answer appears at all; the 0.02 and 0.58 split is invented")

    section("4. Genuinely running: training a verifier on both correct and incorrect samples")
    r = random.Random(7)
    data = []
    for _ in range(4000):
        correct = r.random() < 0.3
        score = r.gauss(1.0 if correct else 0.0, 1.0)
        data.append((score, correct))
    best_t, best_acc = None, 0
    for t in [x / 10 for x in range(-10, 21)]:
        acc = mean((s > t) == c for s, c in data)
        if acc > best_acc:
            best_t, best_acc = t, acc
    test = []
    for _ in range(4000):
        correct = r.random() < 0.3
        test.append((r.gauss(1.0 if correct else 0.0, 1.0), correct))
    tacc = mean((s > best_t) == c for s, c in test)
    tpr = mean(s > best_t for s, c in test if c)
    fpr = mean(s > best_t for s, c in test if not c)
    print(f"threshold {best_t} chosen on training data | held-out accuracy {tacc:.3f} | true-positive {tpr:.3f} | false-positive {fpr:.3f}")
    print("the scripted scores overlap, so the threshold that maximises accuracy on this 30 percent correct mix rejects most right answers (low true-positive rate) in order to keep false positives low; V-STaR trains a verifier on the model's own wrong samples as well as right ones to learn that boundary, but a real verifier is a trained model and this one is a threshold on invented Gaussian scores")

Every output below was genuinely produced by the lab file on Python 3.14.5. This is our own stdlib model of the ideas behind self-taught reasoning (STaR rationale filtering and rationalization, V-STaR verifiers and best-of-N, process versus outcome supervision, out-of-distribution testing and Quiet-STaR style thinking gates), not the real software, and the model is a table of invented competence values or a threshold on invented scores, and no language model is involved, so no real LLM behaviour is measured. builds a chain of steps with a lucky-answer chance, outcome_reward and process_reward score it two different ways.","descKn":"make_chain ಅದೃಷ್ಟ-ಉತ್ತರ ಸಾಧ್ಯತೆಯೊಂದಿಗೆ ಹಂತಗಳ ಸರಪಳಿ ರಚಿಸುತ್ತದೆ, outcome_reward ಮತ್ತು process_reward ಅದಕ್ಕೆ ಎರಡು ವಿಭಿನ್ನ ರೀತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುತ್ತವೆ.","code":"def make_chain(r, n_steps=4, p_step=0.8, lucky=0.2):
    """A reasoning chain: each step is right with p_step. If any step is wrong the final answer is still right with probability lucky."""
    steps = [r.random() < p_step for _ in range(n_steps)]
    if all(steps):
        return steps, True
    return steps, r.random() < lucky


def outcome_reward(chain):
    return 1.0 if chain[1] else 0.0


def process_reward(chain):
    return mean(chain[0])"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"st_3.py","headingEn":"main(): experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() measures outcome rewards, compares the two filters, degrades the step checker, tests a memorizer and an algorithm out of distribution and tries thinking gates.","descKn":"main() outcome ಬಹುಮಾನ ಅಳೆದು, ಎರಡು ಶೋಧಕ ಹೋಲಿಸಿ, ಹಂತ ಪರಿಶೀಲಕ ಹದಗೆಡಿಸಿ, ವಿತರಣೆ-ಹೊರಗೆ memorizer ಮತ್ತು algorithm ಪರೀಕ್ಷಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ಯೋಚನೆ ಗೇಟ್ ಪ್ರಯತ್ನಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    section("1. Genuinely measuring: what outcome rewards reward (20000 chains of 4 steps, per-step 0.8)")
    r = random.Random(1)
    chains = [make_chain(r) for _ in range(20000)]
    right = [c for c in chains if c[1]]
    clean = [c for c in right if all(c[0])]
    print(f"answer right: {len(right) / len(chains):.3f} | all steps right: {sum(all(c[0]) for c in chains) / len(chains):.3f}")
    print(f"of the chains an outcome reward scores 1.0, the share with at least one wrong step: {1 - len(clean) / len(right):.3f}")
    print("an outcome-only reward treats a chain with wrong steps and a lucky right answer exactly like a clean chain, so a notable share of rewarded chains reasoned badly; the 0.8 per-step rate and 20 percent luck are invented")

    section("2. Genuinely measuring: filtering by outcome against filtering by process")
    keep_out = [c for c in chains if outcome_reward(c) == 1.0]
    keep_proc = [c for c in chains if process_reward(c) == 1.0]
    print(f"outcome filter keeps {len(keep_out)} chains; fraction fully correct {mean(all(c[0]) for c in keep_out):.3f}")
    print(f"process filter keeps {len(keep_proc)} chains; fraction fully correct {mean(all(c[0]) for c in keep_proc):.3f}")
    print("requiring every step to be checked removes the lucky chains and keeps fewer examples, which is the trade of process supervision: cleaner data at the price of needing a per-step checker, and here the checker is perfect because the lab knows the truth")

    section("3. Genuinely measuring: an imperfect step checker")
    r = random.Random(2)
    for miss in (0.0, 0.1, 0.3):
        kept = []
        for steps, ans in chains[:8000]:
            flagged = any((not s) and r.random() >= miss for s in steps)
            if not flagged:
                kept.append((steps, ans))
        print(f"checker misses {miss:.1f} of wrong steps: kept {len(kept):4d} | fully correct share {mean(all(s) for s, _ in kept):.3f}")
    print("as the checker misses more wrong steps, bad chains slip into the training set again; a process checker is only as good as its coverage, and the miss rates are invented")

    section("4. Genuinely running: a memorizer and an algorithm, tested in and out of distribution")
    train = {(a, b): a + b for a in range(10, 100, 3) for b in range(10, 100, 3)}
    memorizer = lambda a, b: train.get((a, b), 0)
    algorithm = lambda a, b: a + b
    r = random.Random(3)
    in_dist = [(r.choice(range(10, 100, 3)), r.choice(range(10, 100, 3))) for _ in range(500)]
    unseen = [(a + 1, b + 1) for a, b in in_dist]
    big = [(r.randint(1000, 9999), r.randint(1000, 9999)) for _ in range(500)]
    for name, f in (("memorizer", memorizer), ("algorithm", algorithm)):
        acc = [mean(f(a, b) == a + b for a, b in s) for s in (in_dist, unseen, big)]
        print(f"{name:10} in-distribution {acc[0]:.2f} | unseen two-digit {acc[1]:.2f} | four-digit {acc[2]:.2f}")
    print("both look perfect on training-style inputs, and only the one that learned the procedure survives inputs it has not seen; a test set drawn from the training distribution cannot tell them apart, and the memorizer is a plain lookup table used as a stand-in")

    section("5. Genuinely measuring: a thinking gate that thinks only when a position looks hard")
    r = random.Random(4)
    positions = [r.random() for _ in range(20000)]
    accuracy = lambda d, think: 0.97 if think else max(0.2, 1.0 - 0.9 * d)
    for name, gate in (("never think", lambda d: False), ("always think", lambda d: True), ("think if difficulty > 0.5", lambda d: d > 0.5), ("think if difficulty > 0.8", lambda d: d > 0.8)):
        thought = [gate(d) for d in positions]
        acc = mean(accuracy(d, t) for d, t in zip(positions, thought))
        print(f"{name:27} accuracy {acc:.3f} | thinking tokens per position {mean(thought) * 50:5.1f}")
    print("thinking only where difficulty exceeds 0.5 recovers about 76 percent of the accuracy gain of always thinking (0.556 to 0.870 against 0.970) for about half the tokens, because thinking only helps where the position is hard; the difficulty scores and the accuracy curve are invented, and a real model has to learn when to think")"}},{"type":"output","data":{"output":"

builds a chain of steps with a lucky-answer chance, outcome_reward and process_reward score it two different ways.","descKn":"make_chain ಅದೃಷ್ಟ-ಉತ್ತರ ಸಾಧ್ಯತೆಯೊಂದಿಗೆ ಹಂತಗಳ ಸರಪಳಿ ರಚಿಸುತ್ತದೆ, outcome_reward ಮತ್ತು process_reward ಅದಕ್ಕೆ ಎರಡು ವಿಭಿನ್ನ ರೀತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡುತ್ತವೆ.","code":"def make_chain(r, n_steps=4, p_step=0.8, lucky=0.2):
    """A reasoning chain: each step is right with p_step. If any step is wrong the final answer is still right with probability lucky."""
    steps = [r.random() < p_step for _ in range(n_steps)]
    if all(steps):
        return steps, True
    return steps, r.random() < lucky


def outcome_reward(chain):
    return 1.0 if chain[1] else 0.0


def process_reward(chain):
    return mean(chain[0])"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"st_3.py","headingEn":"main(): experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() measures outcome rewards, compares the two filters, degrades the step checker, tests a memorizer and an algorithm out of distribution and tries thinking gates.","descKn":"main() outcome ಬಹುಮಾನ ಅಳೆದು, ಎರಡು ಶೋಧಕ ಹೋಲಿಸಿ, ಹಂತ ಪರಿಶೀಲಕ ಹದಗೆಡಿಸಿ, ವಿತರಣೆ-ಹೊರಗೆ memorizer ಮತ್ತು algorithm ಪರೀಕ್ಷಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ಯೋಚನೆ ಗೇಟ್ ಪ್ರಯತ್ನಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    section("1. Genuinely measuring: what outcome rewards reward (20000 chains of 4 steps, per-step 0.8)")
    r = random.Random(1)
    chains = [make_chain(r) for _ in range(20000)]
    right = [c for c in chains if c[1]]
    clean = [c for c in right if all(c[0])]
    print(f"answer right: {len(right) / len(chains):.3f} | all steps right: {sum(all(c[0]) for c in chains) / len(chains):.3f}")
    print(f"of the chains an outcome reward scores 1.0, the share with at least one wrong step: {1 - len(clean) / len(right):.3f}")
    print("an outcome-only reward treats a chain with wrong steps and a lucky right answer exactly like a clean chain, so a notable share of rewarded chains reasoned badly; the 0.8 per-step rate and 20 percent luck are invented")

    section("2. Genuinely measuring: filtering by outcome against filtering by process")
    keep_out = [c for c in chains if outcome_reward(c) == 1.0]
    keep_proc = [c for c in chains if process_reward(c) == 1.0]
    print(f"outcome filter keeps {len(keep_out)} chains; fraction fully correct {mean(all(c[0]) for c in keep_out):.3f}")
    print(f"process filter keeps {len(keep_proc)} chains; fraction fully correct {mean(all(c[0]) for c in keep_proc):.3f}")
    print("requiring every step to be checked removes the lucky chains and keeps fewer examples, which is the trade of process supervision: cleaner data at the price of needing a per-step checker, and here the checker is perfect because the lab knows the truth")

    section("3. Genuinely measuring: an imperfect step checker")
    r = random.Random(2)
    for miss in (0.0, 0.1, 0.3):
        kept = []
        for steps, ans in chains[:8000]:
            flagged = any((not s) and r.random() >= miss for s in steps)
            if not flagged:
                kept.append((steps, ans))
        print(f"checker misses {miss:.1f} of wrong steps: kept {len(kept):4d} | fully correct share {mean(all(s) for s, _ in kept):.3f}")
    print("as the checker misses more wrong steps, bad chains slip into the training set again; a process checker is only as good as its coverage, and the miss rates are invented")

    section("4. Genuinely running: a memorizer and an algorithm, tested in and out of distribution")
    train = {(a, b): a + b for a in range(10, 100, 3) for b in range(10, 100, 3)}
    memorizer = lambda a, b: train.get((a, b), 0)
    algorithm = lambda a, b: a + b
    r = random.Random(3)
    in_dist = [(r.choice(range(10, 100, 3)), r.choice(range(10, 100, 3))) for _ in range(500)]
    unseen = [(a + 1, b + 1) for a, b in in_dist]
    big = [(r.randint(1000, 9999), r.randint(1000, 9999)) for _ in range(500)]
    for name, f in (("memorizer", memorizer), ("algorithm", algorithm)):
        acc = [mean(f(a, b) == a + b for a, b in s) for s in (in_dist, unseen, big)]
        print(f"{name:10} in-distribution {acc[0]:.2f} | unseen two-digit {acc[1]:.2f} | four-digit {acc[2]:.2f}")
    print("both look perfect on training-style inputs, and only the one that learned the procedure survives inputs it has not seen; a test set drawn from the training distribution cannot tell them apart, and the memorizer is a plain lookup table used as a stand-in")

    section("5. Genuinely measuring: a thinking gate that thinks only when a position looks hard")
    r = random.Random(4)
    positions = [r.random() for _ in range(20000)]
    accuracy = lambda d, think: 0.97 if think else max(0.2, 1.0 - 0.9 * d)
    for name, gate in (("never think", lambda d: False), ("always think", lambda d: True), ("think if difficulty > 0.5", lambda d: d > 0.5), ("think if difficulty > 0.8", lambda d: d > 0.8)):
        thought = [gate(d) for d in positions]
        acc = mean(accuracy(d, t) for d, t in zip(positions, thought))
        print(f"{name:27} accuracy {acc:.3f} | thinking tokens per position {mean(thought) * 50:5.1f}")
    print("thinking only where difficulty exceeds 0.5 recovers about 76 percent of the accuracy gain of always thinking (0.556 to 0.870 against 0.970) for about half the tokens, because thinking only helps where the position is hard; the difficulty scores and the accuracy curve are invented, and a real model has to learn when to think")"}},{"type":"output","data":{"output":"

class Program:
    a: int
    b: int
    c: int

    def predict(self, x):
        return self.a * x * x + self.b * x + self.c

    def expression(self):
        return f"{self.a}*x*x + {self.b}*x + {self.c}"


def target(x):
    return x * x + 3 * x + 2


def mse(p, points):
    return sum((p.predict(x) - target(x)) ** 2 for x in points) / len(points)


def descriptor(p):
    degree = 2 if p.a != 0 else (1 if p.b != 0 else 0)
    return degree, sum(v != 0 for v in (p.a, p.b, p.c))


def mutate(p, rng):
    v = [p.a, p.b, p.c]
    v[rng.randrange(3)] += rng.choice([-2, -1, 1, 2])
    return Program(*v)


class Archive:
    def __init__(self, points):
        self.points, self.cells = points, {}

    def insert(self, p):
        cell = descriptor(p)
        inc = self.cells.get(cell)
        if inc is None or mse(p, self.points) < mse(inc, self.points):
            self.cells[cell] = p
            return True
        return False

ಪ್ರೋಗ್ರಾಂ ಇಡುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Program:
    a: int
    b: int
    c: int

    def predict(self, x):
        return self.a * x * x + self.b * x + self.c

    def expression(self):
        return f"{self.a}*x*x + {self.b}*x + {self.c}"


def target(x):
    return x * x + 3 * x + 2


def mse(p, points):
    return sum((p.predict(x) - target(x)) ** 2 for x in points) / len(points)


def descriptor(p):
    degree = 2 if p.a != 0 else (1 if p.b != 0 else 0)
    return degree, sum(v != 0 for v in (p.a, p.b, p.c))


def mutate(p, rng):
    v = [p.a, p.b, p.c]
    v[rng.randrange(3)] += rng.choice([-2, -1, 1, 2])
    return Program(*v)


class Archive:
    def __init__(self, points):
        self.points, self.cells = points, {}

    def insert(self, p):
        cell = descriptor(p)
        inc = self.cells.get(cell)
        if inc is None or mse(p, self.points) < mse(inc, self.points):
            self.cells[cell] = p
            return True
        return False


TRAIN = list(range(-5, 6))
HELD = [-9, -7, 7, 8, 12]"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"ae_1.py","headingEn":"main(): experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() scores three programs, runs one search, compares two parent-selection rules over ten seeds, varies the generation budget and prints what the archive keeps.","descKn":"main() ಮೂರು ಪ್ರೋಗ್ರಾಂಗಳಿಗೆ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡಿ, ಒಂದು ಹುಡುಕಾಟ ಓಡಿಸಿ, ಹತ್ತು seeds ಮೇಲೆ ಎರಡು ಪೋಷಕ-ಆಯ್ಕೆ ನಿಯಮ ಹೋಲಿಸಿ, ಜನರೇಶನ್ ಬಜೆಟ್ ಬದಲಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ಆರ್ಕೈವ್ ಏನು ಇಡುತ್ತದೆ ಮುದ್ರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    section("1. Genuinely running: the target, the seed program and the evaluator")
    pts = [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2]
    for p in (Program(0, 1, 0), Program(1, 1, 0), Program(1, 3, 2)):
        print(f"{p.expression():22} MSE on -2..2 = {mse(p, pts)}")
    print("the seed program x has a mean squared error of 26.8, x*x + x has 12.0 and the exact target has 0.0; the evaluator is deterministic, so the same program on the same points always gets the same score")

    section("2. Genuinely running: one search, 200 generations, seed 42, archive parents")
    best, bs, hs, cells, hit = evolve(42, 200, "archive")
    print("best:", best.expression(), "| training MSE:", bs, "| held-out MSE:", hs, "| archive cells:", cells, "| generation of first exact match:", hit)
    print("a single seeded run shows what the loop does and says little about how often it works, which is why the next two sections repeat it")

    section("3. Genuinely measuring: ten seeds, 200 generations, two parent-selection rules")
    for mode in ("archive", "global best"):
        runs = [evolve(s, 200, "archive" if mode == "archive" else "best") for s in range(1, 11)]
        exact = sum(1 for r in runs if r[1] == 0)
        hits = [r[4] for r in runs if r[4] is not None]
        print(f"{mode:12} exact in {exact}/10 runs | median training MSE {median(r[1] for r in runs)} | worst training MSE {max(r[1] for r in runs)} | median generation of first hit {median(hits) if hits else None} | mean archive cells {mean(r[3] for r in runs):.1f}")
    print("both rules were run on the same ten seeds with the same budget and the counts above are what they produced; ten seeds is a small sample, so a difference of one or two runs is not evidence that one rule is better")

    section("4. Genuinely measuring: more generations")
    for gens in (50, 200, 1000):
        runs = [evolve(s, gens, "archive") for s in range(1, 11)]
        print(f"generations={gens:4} exact in {sum(1 for r in runs if r[1] == 0)}/10 | median training MSE {median(r[1] for r in runs)} | median held-out MSE {median(r[2] for r in runs)}")
    print("more generations gave the search more chances and the table shows how many runs reached the exact target at each budget; a run that has stopped improving is not proof the target is out of reach, only that these mutations have not found it yet")

    section("5. Genuinely running: what the archive keeps")
    rng = random.Random(7)
    arch = Archive(TRAIN)
    arch.insert(Program(0, 1, 0))
    for _ in range(60):
        arch.insert(mutate(rng.choice(list(arch.cells.values())), rng))
    for cell, p in sorted(arch.cells.items()):
        print(f"cell (degree, nonzero) = {cell}  elite {p.expression():20} MSE {mse(p, TRAIN):9.1f}")
    print("each occupied cell holds the lowest-error program found for that degree and number of nonzero terms, so structurally different programs survive even when one of them is much better overall")"}},{"type":"output","data":{"output":"

ಇಡುತ್ತದೆ ಮತ್ತು cubic_search ಆರಿಸಿದ training ಬಿಂದುಗಳ ವಿರುದ್ಧ ನಾಲ್ಕು ಗುಣಾಂಕ ವಿಕಸಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def small(p, r):
    v = [p.a, p.b, p.c]
    v[r.randrange(3)] += r.choice([-1, 1])
    return P(*v)


def large(p, r):
    v = [p.a, p.b, p.c]
    v[r.randrange(3)] += r.choice([-5, -3, 3, 5])
    return P(*v)


def reset(p, r):
    v = [p.a, p.b, p.c]
    v[r.randrange(3)] = r.randint(-6, 6)
    return P(*v)


def hill(seed, gens, op):
    r = random.Random(seed)
    best = P(0, 1, 0)
    bs = mse(best, TRAIN)
    for _ in range(gens):
        c = op(best, r)
        s = mse(c, TRAIN)
        if s < bs:
            best, bs = c, s
    return bs


def island_run(seed, gens, islands, migrate_every=10):
    r = random.Random(seed)
    pops = [[P(r.randint(-3, 3), r.randint(-3, 3), r.randint(-3, 3)) for _ in range(4)] for _ in range(islands)]
    for g in range(1, gens + 1):
        for pop in pops:
            parent = min(r.sample(pop, 2), key=lambda p: mse(p, TRAIN))
            child = small(parent, r) if r.random() < 0.7 else reset(parent, r)
            worst = max(range(len(pop)), key=lambda i: mse(pop[i], TRAIN))
            if mse(child, TRAIN) <= mse(pop[worst], TRAIN):
                pop[worst] = child
        if islands > 1 and g % migrate_every == 0:
            bests = [min(pop, key=lambda p: mse(p, TRAIN)) for pop in pops]
            for i, pop in enumerate(pops):
                w = max(range(len(pop)), key=lambda j: mse(pop[j], TRAIN))
                pop[w] = bests[(i - 1) % islands]
    return min(mse(p, TRAIN) for pop in pops for p in pop)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Cubic:
    a: int
    b: int
    c: int
    d: int

    def predict(self, x):
        return self.a * x ** 3 + self.b * x * x + self.c * x + self.d


def cubic_search(seed, pts, gens=1500):
    r = random.Random(seed)
    best = Cubic(0, 0, 1, 0)
    err = lambda p, q: sum((p.predict(x) - target(x)) ** 2 for x in q) / len(q)
    bs = err(best, pts)
    for _ in range(gens):
        v = [best.a, best.b, best.c, best.d]
        v[r.randrange(4)] += r.choice([-2, -1, 1, 2])
        c = Cubic(*v)
        s = err(c, pts)
        if s < bs or (s == bs and r.random() < 0.5):
            best, bs = c, s
    return best, bs, err(best, [-7, -4, 4, 6, 9])"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"ae_2.py","headingEn":"main(): experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() compares operators, checks tournament pressure, compares one population with four islands, computes the overfitting example, runs the cubic search and shows the speed-only evaluator.","descKn":"main() ಆಪರೇಟರ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು ಹೋಲಿಸಿ, tournament ಒತ್ತಡ ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಿ, ಒಂದು ಜನಸಂಖ್ಯೆ ಮತ್ತು ನಾಲ್ಕು islands ಹೋಲಿಸಿ, overfitting ಉದಾಹರಣೆ ಲೆಕ್ಕ ಹಾಕಿ, cubic ಹುಡುಕಾಟ ಓಡಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ವೇಗ-ಮಾತ್ರ ಮೌಲ್ಯಮಾಪಕ ತೋರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    section("1. Genuinely measuring: three mutation operators, 200 generations, seeds 1 to 10")
    for name, op in (("small (+-1)", small), ("large (+-3/5)", large), ("reset (-6..6)", reset)):
        res = [hill(s, 200, op) for s in range(1, 11)]
        print(f"{name:14} exact in {sum(1 for x in res if x == 0)}/10 | median final MSE {median(res)} | worst {max(res)}")
    print("the table shows which operator reached the exact target most often with this budget on these ten seeds; the operators were run with the same loop and the same seeds, and with ten runs a gap of one or two is within what a different set of seeds could change")

    section("2. Genuinely computing: tournament pressure, formula against simulation")
    rng = random.Random(1)
    pop = [rng.random() for _ in range(100000)]
    cut = sorted(pop)[int(0.2 * len(pop))]
    for k in (1, 3, 5, 10):
        formula = 1 - 0.8 ** k
        hits = sum(1 for _ in range(20000) if min(rng.sample(pop, k)) <= cut) / 20000
        print(f"tournament size {k:2}: formula {formula:.3f} | simulated {hits:.3f}")
    print("the chance that a tournament contains at least one top-20 percent member is 1 - 0.8^k, which is 0.488 at k = 3, and the simulated column agrees to about two decimal places; a larger tournament raises that chance and so raises selection pressure")

    section("3. Genuinely measuring: one population against four islands (same total budget of mutations)")
    for islands, gens in ((1, 400), (4, 100)):
        res = [island_run(s, gens, islands) for s in range(1, 11)]
        print(f"{islands} island(s) x {gens} generations: exact in {sum(1 for x in res if x == 0)}/10 | median final MSE {median(res)} | worst {max(res)}")
    print("both setups made 400 mutations in total per run and the table reports what each reached; the lab's islands are small lists of four programs with ring migration every ten generations, and this is a toy comparison on a problem easy enough that diversity may not matter")

    section("4. Genuinely computing: the overfitting example from the lesson")
    over = lambda x: target(x) + 10 * x * (x - 1) * (x - 2)
    m = lambda f, pts: sum((f(x) - target(x)) ** 2 for x in pts) / len(pts)
    print("training MSE on 0, 1, 2:", m(over, [0, 1, 2]), "| held-out MSE on -1, 3, 4:", m(over, [-1, 3, 4]))
    print("the held-out squared errors are 3600, 3600 and 57600, so the mean is 21600; part 2 of the lesson printed 6240.0 for this and part 3 corrected it, and the run agrees with the correction")

    section("5. Genuinely measuring: a cubic search with only three training points")
    pts3 = [0, 1, 2]
    zero_train = bad_held = 0
    for s in range(1, 21):
        best, tr, ho = cubic_search(s, pts3)
        if tr == 0:
            zero_train += 1
            if ho > 0:
                bad_held += 1
    print(f"20 seeds: training error reached 0 in {zero_train}; of those, held-out error stayed above 0 in {bad_held}")
    print("with three training points many cubics fit exactly, and the count above is how many of the runs that fit the training points still disagreed with the target elsewhere; this is overfitting of the evaluator's inputs and not a bug in the search")

    section("6. Genuinely running: a speed-only evaluator rewards doing nothing")
    import time
    data = list(range(20000))
    correct = lambda xs: [v * 2 for v in xs]
    empty = lambda xs: []

    def timed(f):
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        out = f(data)
        return time.perf_counter() - t0, out

    tc, oc = timed(correct)
    te, oe = timed(empty)
    print("empty answer faster than correct answer:", te < tc)
    print("correctness gate: correct passes =", oc == [v * 2 for v in data], "| empty passes =", oe == [v * 2 for v in data])
    print("a score that only measures time prefers the empty answer, and putting a correctness check in front of the timing rejects it; the timings themselves are single measurements on this machine and are not stable enough to quote")"}},{"type":"output","data":{"output":"

ಇಡುತ್ತದೆ ಮತ್ತು cubic_search ಆರಿಸಿದ training ಬಿಂದುಗಳ ವಿರುದ್ಧ ನಾಲ್ಕು ಗುಣಾಂಕ ವಿಕಸಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def small(p, r):
    v = [p.a, p.b, p.c]
    v[r.randrange(3)] += r.choice([-1, 1])
    return P(*v)


def large(p, r):
    v = [p.a, p.b, p.c]
    v[r.randrange(3)] += r.choice([-5, -3, 3, 5])
    return P(*v)


def reset(p, r):
    v = [p.a, p.b, p.c]
    v[r.randrange(3)] = r.randint(-6, 6)
    return P(*v)


def hill(seed, gens, op):
    r = random.Random(seed)
    best = P(0, 1, 0)
    bs = mse(best, TRAIN)
    for _ in range(gens):
        c = op(best, r)
        s = mse(c, TRAIN)
        if s < bs:
            best, bs = c, s
    return bs


def island_run(seed, gens, islands, migrate_every=10):
    r = random.Random(seed)
    pops = [[P(r.randint(-3, 3), r.randint(-3, 3), r.randint(-3, 3)) for _ in range(4)] for _ in range(islands)]
    for g in range(1, gens + 1):
        for pop in pops:
            parent = min(r.sample(pop, 2), key=lambda p: mse(p, TRAIN))
            child = small(parent, r) if r.random() < 0.7 else reset(parent, r)
            worst = max(range(len(pop)), key=lambda i: mse(pop[i], TRAIN))
            if mse(child, TRAIN) <= mse(pop[worst], TRAIN):
                pop[worst] = child
        if islands > 1 and g % migrate_every == 0:
            bests = [min(pop, key=lambda p: mse(p, TRAIN)) for pop in pops]
            for i, pop in enumerate(pops):
                w = max(range(len(pop)), key=lambda j: mse(pop[j], TRAIN))
                pop[w] = bests[(i - 1) % islands]
    return min(mse(p, TRAIN) for pop in pops for p in pop)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Cubic:
    a: int
    b: int
    c: int
    d: int

    def predict(self, x):
        return self.a * x ** 3 + self.b * x * x + self.c * x + self.d


def cubic_search(seed, pts, gens=1500):
    r = random.Random(seed)
    best = Cubic(0, 0, 1, 0)
    err = lambda p, q: sum((p.predict(x) - target(x)) ** 2 for x in q) / len(q)
    bs = err(best, pts)
    for _ in range(gens):
        v = [best.a, best.b, best.c, best.d]
        v[r.randrange(4)] += r.choice([-2, -1, 1, 2])
        c = Cubic(*v)
        s = err(c, pts)
        if s < bs or (s == bs and r.random() < 0.5):
            best, bs = c, s
    return best, bs, err(best, [-7, -4, 4, 6, 9])"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"ae_2.py","headingEn":"main(): experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() compares operators, checks tournament pressure, compares one population with four islands, computes the overfitting example, runs the cubic search and shows the speed-only evaluator.","descKn":"main() ಆಪರೇಟರ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು ಹೋಲಿಸಿ, tournament ಒತ್ತಡ ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಿ, ಒಂದು ಜನಸಂಖ್ಯೆ ಮತ್ತು ನಾಲ್ಕು islands ಹೋಲಿಸಿ, overfitting ಉದಾಹರಣೆ ಲೆಕ್ಕ ಹಾಕಿ, cubic ಹುಡುಕಾಟ ಓಡಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ವೇಗ-ಮಾತ್ರ ಮೌಲ್ಯಮಾಪಕ ತೋರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    section("1. Genuinely measuring: three mutation operators, 200 generations, seeds 1 to 10")
    for name, op in (("small (+-1)", small), ("large (+-3/5)", large), ("reset (-6..6)", reset)):
        res = [hill(s, 200, op) for s in range(1, 11)]
        print(f"{name:14} exact in {sum(1 for x in res if x == 0)}/10 | median final MSE {median(res)} | worst {max(res)}")
    print("the table shows which operator reached the exact target most often with this budget on these ten seeds; the operators were run with the same loop and the same seeds, and with ten runs a gap of one or two is within what a different set of seeds could change")

    section("2. Genuinely computing: tournament pressure, formula against simulation")
    rng = random.Random(1)
    pop = [rng.random() for _ in range(100000)]
    cut = sorted(pop)[int(0.2 * len(pop))]
    for k in (1, 3, 5, 10):
        formula = 1 - 0.8 ** k
        hits = sum(1 for _ in range(20000) if min(rng.sample(pop, k)) <= cut) / 20000
        print(f"tournament size {k:2}: formula {formula:.3f} | simulated {hits:.3f}")
    print("the chance that a tournament contains at least one top-20 percent member is 1 - 0.8^k, which is 0.488 at k = 3, and the simulated column agrees to about two decimal places; a larger tournament raises that chance and so raises selection pressure")

    section("3. Genuinely measuring: one population against four islands (same total budget of mutations)")
    for islands, gens in ((1, 400), (4, 100)):
        res = [island_run(s, gens, islands) for s in range(1, 11)]
        print(f"{islands} island(s) x {gens} generations: exact in {sum(1 for x in res if x == 0)}/10 | median final MSE {median(res)} | worst {max(res)}")
    print("both setups made 400 mutations in total per run and the table reports what each reached; the lab's islands are small lists of four programs with ring migration every ten generations, and this is a toy comparison on a problem easy enough that diversity may not matter")

    section("4. Genuinely computing: the overfitting example from the lesson")
    over = lambda x: target(x) + 10 * x * (x - 1) * (x - 2)
    m = lambda f, pts: sum((f(x) - target(x)) ** 2 for x in pts) / len(pts)
    print("training MSE on 0, 1, 2:", m(over, [0, 1, 2]), "| held-out MSE on -1, 3, 4:", m(over, [-1, 3, 4]))
    print("the held-out squared errors are 3600, 3600 and 57600, so the mean is 21600; part 2 of the lesson printed 6240.0 for this and part 3 corrected it, and the run agrees with the correction")

    section("5. Genuinely measuring: a cubic search with only three training points")
    pts3 = [0, 1, 2]
    zero_train = bad_held = 0
    for s in range(1, 21):
        best, tr, ho = cubic_search(s, pts3)
        if tr == 0:
            zero_train += 1
            if ho > 0:
                bad_held += 1
    print(f"20 seeds: training error reached 0 in {zero_train}; of those, held-out error stayed above 0 in {bad_held}")
    print("with three training points many cubics fit exactly, and the count above is how many of the runs that fit the training points still disagreed with the target elsewhere; this is overfitting of the evaluator's inputs and not a bug in the search")

    section("6. Genuinely running: a speed-only evaluator rewards doing nothing")
    import time
    data = list(range(20000))
    correct = lambda xs: [v * 2 for v in xs]
    empty = lambda xs: []

    def timed(f):
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        out = f(data)
        return time.perf_counter() - t0, out

    tc, oc = timed(correct)
    te, oe = timed(empty)
    print("empty answer faster than correct answer:", te < tc)
    print("correctness gate: correct passes =", oc == [v * 2 for v in data], "| empty passes =", oe == [v * 2 for v in data])
    print("a score that only measures time prefers the empty answer, and putting a correctness check in front of the timing rejects it; the timings themselves are single measurements on this machine and are not stable enough to quote")"}},{"type":"output","data":{"output":"

ಕಳುಹಿಸುವ ಕೆಲಸದ ಘಟಕ.","code":"def pool_eval(p):
    return p, mse(p)


def sha(text):
    return hashlib.sha256(text.encode()).hexdigest()[:12]


class ProgramDB:
    def __init__(self):
        self.db = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
        self.db.execute("CREATE TABLE c (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, parent TEXT, gen INTEGER, src TEXT, status TEXT, score REAL, evaluator TEXT)")

    def add(self, p, parent, gen, status, score, evaluator="v1"):
        cid = sha(p.source())
        try:
            self.db.execute("INSERT INTO c VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?)", (cid, parent, gen, p.source(), status, score, evaluator))
            return cid, True
        except sqlite3.IntegrityError:
            return cid, False

    def lineage(self, cid):
        out = []
        while cid:
            row = self.db.execute("SELECT id, parent, gen, src, score FROM c WHERE id=?", (cid,)).fetchone()
            out.append(row)
            cid = row[1]
        return out[::-1]


def staged(p):
    if not all(isinstance(v, int) and not isinstance(v, bool) and abs(v) <= 100 for v in (p.a, p.b, p.c)):
        return "INVALID", None
    e = mse(p)
    return ("PASS", e) if e == 0 else ("INCORRECT", e)"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"ae_3.py","headingEn":"main(): experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() fills a database and prints a lineage, runs the staged evaluator, tallies stop reasons over 20 seeds, times parallel against sequential evaluation, runs a child process that reads a file, and applies a deployment gate.","descKn":"main() ಡೇಟಾಬೇಸ್ ತುಂಬಿ ವಂಶಾವಳಿ ಮುದ್ರಿಸಿ, ಹಂತಹಂತದ ಮೌಲ್ಯಮಾಪಕ ಓಡಿಸಿ, 20 seeds ಮೇಲೆ ನಿಲುಗಡೆ ಕಾರಣ ಎಣಿಸಿ, ಸಮಾನಾಂತರ ಮತ್ತು ಅನುಕ್ರಮ ಮೌಲ್ಯಮಾಪನ ಸಮಯ ಅಳೆದು, ಫೈಲ್ ಓದುವ child process ಓಡಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು deployment gate ಅನ್ವಯಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    section("1. Genuinely running: a SQLite program database with lineage and duplicate detection")
    db = ProgramDB()
    rng = random.Random(5)
    cur, cid = Program(0, 1, 0), None
    cid, _ = db.add(cur, None, 0, "evaluated", mse(cur))
    dup = 0
    for g in range(1, 60):
        v = [cur.a, cur.b, cur.c]
        v[rng.randrange(3)] += rng.choice([-2, -1, 1, 2])
        child = Program(*v)
        s = mse(child)
        new_id, fresh = db.add(child, cid, g, "evaluated", s)
        dup += 0 if fresh else 1
        if s < mse(cur):
            cur, cid = child, new_id
    print("rows:", db.db.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM c").fetchone()[0], "| duplicates refused:", dup, "| best:", cur.source(), "| MSE:", mse(cur))
    for row in db.lineage(cid):
        print("  lineage", row[2], row[3], "score", row[4])
    print("every stored program has a content-hash id, a parent and a generation, and the same source text was refused the second time it appeared; the lineage is the chain of parents that led to the current best")

    section("2. Genuinely running: a staged evaluator separates invalid, incorrect and passing")
    for p in (Program(1000, 1, 0), Program(0, 1, 0), Program(1, 3, 2)):
        print(f"{p.source():28} -> {staged(p)}")
    print("a candidate outside the allowed coefficient range never reaches scoring, a wrong one gets its error and the exact one passes; keeping the stages apart tells you why a candidate was rejected")

    section("3. Genuinely running: a search budget with stagnation stopping")
    def run(seed, max_evals, stag):
        r = random.Random(seed)
        best, bs, last, n = Program(0, 1, 0), mse(Program(0, 1, 0)), 0, 0
        while n < max_evals:
            v = [best.a, best.b, best.c]
            v[r.randrange(3)] += r.choice([-1, 1])
            c = Program(*v)
            n += 1
            s = mse(c)
            if s < bs:
                best, bs, last = c, s, n
            if bs == 0:
                return n, "target reached", bs
            if n - last >= stag:
                return n, "stagnation", bs
        return n, "evaluation budget", bs
    tally = {}
    for seed in range(1, 21):
        n, why, bs = run(seed, 300, 6)
        tally[why] = tally.get(why, 0) + 1
        if seed <= 4:
            print(f"seed {seed}: stopped after {n:3} evaluations because of {why!r}, best MSE {bs}")
    print("over 20 seeds with a stagnation window of 6:", tally)
    n2 = {}
    for seed in range(1, 21):
        n, why, bs = run(seed, 300, 40)
        n2[why] = n2.get(why, 0) + 1
    print("over the same 20 seeds with a window of 40:", n2)
    print("the counts above are how often each stop reason occurred; a short stagnation window ended runs before the target was found, and a longer one let more of them finish, so the window is a choice with a cost, and the seeds and limits are invented")

    section("4. Genuinely measuring: parallel versus sequential evaluation of tiny jobs")
    progs = [Program(rng.randint(-5, 5), rng.randint(-5, 5), rng.randint(-5, 5)) for _ in range(400)]
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    seq = [pool_eval(p) for p in progs]
    t_seq = time.perf_counter() - t0
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=4) as ex:
        par = list(ex.map(pool_eval, progs))
    t_par = time.perf_counter() - t0
    print("same results from both:", [round(e, 6) for _, e in seq] == [round(e, 6) for _, e in par], "| parallel slower than sequential on this machine:", t_par > t_seq)
    print("each evaluation is a few microseconds of arithmetic, so starting processes and sending objects between them costs more than the work; parallelism pays when each evaluation takes long enough to dwarf that overhead, and the timings are single runs that were not repeated")

    section("5. Genuinely running: a child process is not a sandbox")
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        secret = Path(d) / "made_up_secret.txt"
        secret.write_text("made-up-secret-value", encoding="utf-8")
        script = Path(d) / "candidate.py"
        script.write_text(f"print(open(r'{secret}').read())", encoding="utf-8")
        out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-I", str(script)], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
        print("child with -I and a timeout read the file it was never given:", out.stdout.strip())
        loop = Path(d) / "loop.py"
        loop.write_text("while True: pass", encoding="utf-8")
        try:
            subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(loop)], timeout=1)
            print("loop finished")
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            print("an infinite loop was stopped by the timeout after 1 second")
    print("isolated mode and a timeout stop a runaway loop and do nothing about file access, because the child runs with the same operating-system permissions as its parent; real isolation has to be enforced outside Python with a container or a virtual machine, and this lab only shows the gap")

    section("6. Genuinely running: a deployment gate and an evidence report")
    def gate(ev):
        failed = [k for k, v in ev.items() if not v]
        return {"approved": not failed, "failed_checks": failed}
    ev = dict(correctness=True, security=True, performance=True, independent_review=True, human_approval=False, rollback_ready=True)
    print(gate(ev))
    report = {"candidate": sha(cur.source()), "training_mse": mse(cur), "held_out_mse": mse(cur, [-30, -20, 20, 40]), "gate": gate(ev)}
    print(json.dumps(report, sort_keys=True))
    print("a candidate with a perfect score was still not approved because a human approval was missing, and in this lab approval is a boolean field, which a real system must replace with an authenticated decision the candidate cannot set; the report is printed and not written to a file")"}},{"type":"output","data":{"output":"

ಕಳುಹಿಸುವ ಕೆಲಸದ ಘಟಕ.","code":"def pool_eval(p):
    return p, mse(p)


def sha(text):
    return hashlib.sha256(text.encode()).hexdigest()[:12]


class ProgramDB:
    def __init__(self):
        self.db = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
        self.db.execute("CREATE TABLE c (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, parent TEXT, gen INTEGER, src TEXT, status TEXT, score REAL, evaluator TEXT)")

    def add(self, p, parent, gen, status, score, evaluator="v1"):
        cid = sha(p.source())
        try:
            self.db.execute("INSERT INTO c VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?)", (cid, parent, gen, p.source(), status, score, evaluator))
            return cid, True
        except sqlite3.IntegrityError:
            return cid, False

    def lineage(self, cid):
        out = []
        while cid:
            row = self.db.execute("SELECT id, parent, gen, src, score FROM c WHERE id=?", (cid,)).fetchone()
            out.append(row)
            cid = row[1]
        return out[::-1]


def staged(p):
    if not all(isinstance(v, int) and not isinstance(v, bool) and abs(v) <= 100 for v in (p.a, p.b, p.c)):
        return "INVALID", None
    e = mse(p)
    return ("PASS", e) if e == 0 else ("INCORRECT", e)"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"ae_3.py","headingEn":"main(): experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() fills a database and prints a lineage, runs the staged evaluator, tallies stop reasons over 20 seeds, times parallel against sequential evaluation, runs a child process that reads a file, and applies a deployment gate.","descKn":"main() ಡೇಟಾಬೇಸ್ ತುಂಬಿ ವಂಶಾವಳಿ ಮುದ್ರಿಸಿ, ಹಂತಹಂತದ ಮೌಲ್ಯಮಾಪಕ ಓಡಿಸಿ, 20 seeds ಮೇಲೆ ನಿಲುಗಡೆ ಕಾರಣ ಎಣಿಸಿ, ಸಮಾನಾಂತರ ಮತ್ತು ಅನುಕ್ರಮ ಮೌಲ್ಯಮಾಪನ ಸಮಯ ಅಳೆದು, ಫೈಲ್ ಓದುವ child process ಓಡಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು deployment gate ಅನ್ವಯಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    section("1. Genuinely running: a SQLite program database with lineage and duplicate detection")
    db = ProgramDB()
    rng = random.Random(5)
    cur, cid = Program(0, 1, 0), None
    cid, _ = db.add(cur, None, 0, "evaluated", mse(cur))
    dup = 0
    for g in range(1, 60):
        v = [cur.a, cur.b, cur.c]
        v[rng.randrange(3)] += rng.choice([-2, -1, 1, 2])
        child = Program(*v)
        s = mse(child)
        new_id, fresh = db.add(child, cid, g, "evaluated", s)
        dup += 0 if fresh else 1
        if s < mse(cur):
            cur, cid = child, new_id
    print("rows:", db.db.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM c").fetchone()[0], "| duplicates refused:", dup, "| best:", cur.source(), "| MSE:", mse(cur))
    for row in db.lineage(cid):
        print("  lineage", row[2], row[3], "score", row[4])
    print("every stored program has a content-hash id, a parent and a generation, and the same source text was refused the second time it appeared; the lineage is the chain of parents that led to the current best")

    section("2. Genuinely running: a staged evaluator separates invalid, incorrect and passing")
    for p in (Program(1000, 1, 0), Program(0, 1, 0), Program(1, 3, 2)):
        print(f"{p.source():28} -> {staged(p)}")
    print("a candidate outside the allowed coefficient range never reaches scoring, a wrong one gets its error and the exact one passes; keeping the stages apart tells you why a candidate was rejected")

    section("3. Genuinely running: a search budget with stagnation stopping")
    def run(seed, max_evals, stag):
        r = random.Random(seed)
        best, bs, last, n = Program(0, 1, 0), mse(Program(0, 1, 0)), 0, 0
        while n < max_evals:
            v = [best.a, best.b, best.c]
            v[r.randrange(3)] += r.choice([-1, 1])
            c = Program(*v)
            n += 1
            s = mse(c)
            if s < bs:
                best, bs, last = c, s, n
            if bs == 0:
                return n, "target reached", bs
            if n - last >= stag:
                return n, "stagnation", bs
        return n, "evaluation budget", bs
    tally = {}
    for seed in range(1, 21):
        n, why, bs = run(seed, 300, 6)
        tally[why] = tally.get(why, 0) + 1
        if seed <= 4:
            print(f"seed {seed}: stopped after {n:3} evaluations because of {why!r}, best MSE {bs}")
    print("over 20 seeds with a stagnation window of 6:", tally)
    n2 = {}
    for seed in range(1, 21):
        n, why, bs = run(seed, 300, 40)
        n2[why] = n2.get(why, 0) + 1
    print("over the same 20 seeds with a window of 40:", n2)
    print("the counts above are how often each stop reason occurred; a short stagnation window ended runs before the target was found, and a longer one let more of them finish, so the window is a choice with a cost, and the seeds and limits are invented")

    section("4. Genuinely measuring: parallel versus sequential evaluation of tiny jobs")
    progs = [Program(rng.randint(-5, 5), rng.randint(-5, 5), rng.randint(-5, 5)) for _ in range(400)]
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    seq = [pool_eval(p) for p in progs]
    t_seq = time.perf_counter() - t0
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=4) as ex:
        par = list(ex.map(pool_eval, progs))
    t_par = time.perf_counter() - t0
    print("same results from both:", [round(e, 6) for _, e in seq] == [round(e, 6) for _, e in par], "| parallel slower than sequential on this machine:", t_par > t_seq)
    print("each evaluation is a few microseconds of arithmetic, so starting processes and sending objects between them costs more than the work; parallelism pays when each evaluation takes long enough to dwarf that overhead, and the timings are single runs that were not repeated")

    section("5. Genuinely running: a child process is not a sandbox")
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        secret = Path(d) / "made_up_secret.txt"
        secret.write_text("made-up-secret-value", encoding="utf-8")
        script = Path(d) / "candidate.py"
        script.write_text(f"print(open(r'{secret}').read())", encoding="utf-8")
        out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-I", str(script)], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5)
        print("child with -I and a timeout read the file it was never given:", out.stdout.strip())
        loop = Path(d) / "loop.py"
        loop.write_text("while True: pass", encoding="utf-8")
        try:
            subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(loop)], timeout=1)
            print("loop finished")
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            print("an infinite loop was stopped by the timeout after 1 second")
    print("isolated mode and a timeout stop a runaway loop and do nothing about file access, because the child runs with the same operating-system permissions as its parent; real isolation has to be enforced outside Python with a container or a virtual machine, and this lab only shows the gap")

    section("6. Genuinely running: a deployment gate and an evidence report")
    def gate(ev):
        failed = [k for k, v in ev.items() if not v]
        return {"approved": not failed, "failed_checks": failed}
    ev = dict(correctness=True, security=True, performance=True, independent_review=True, human_approval=False, rollback_ready=True)
    print(gate(ev))
    report = {"candidate": sha(cur.source()), "training_mse": mse(cur), "held_out_mse": mse(cur, [-30, -20, 20, 40]), "gate": gate(ev)}
    print(json.dumps(report, sort_keys=True))
    print("a candidate with a perfect score was still not approved because a human approval was missing, and in this lab approval is a boolean field, which a real system must replace with an authenticated decision the candidate cannot set; the report is printed and not written to a file")"}},{"type":"output","data":{"output":"
