]"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"mp_3.py","headingEn":"main(): experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() runs the percentile tables, the attribution, the reconciliation, the redaction, the fallback evaluation and the readiness check.","descKn":"main() ಶತಮಾನಾಂಶ ಕೋಷ್ಟಕ, ಹಂಚಿಕೆ, ಹೊಂದಾಣಿಕೆ, ಮರೆಮಾಚುವಿಕೆ, fallback ಮೌಲ್ಯಮಾಪನ ಮತ್ತು ಸಿದ್ಧತೆ ಪರಿಶೀಲನೆ ಓಡಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    section("1. Genuinely measuring: percentiles by provider and workload, and the pitfall of a mixed workload")
    prov = {"A": make_records(5000, 1, mix=0.80, slow_factor=1.10), "B": make_records(5000, 2, mix=0.20, slow_factor=1.00)}
    print(f"{'provider':8} {'workload':15} {'P50':>7} {'P95':>7} {'P99':>7}")
    for p, recs in prov.items():
        for wl in ("classification", "summarization"):
            v = [r["latency"] for r in recs if r["workload"] == wl]
            print(f"{p:8} {wl:15} {percentile(v, .5):>7.0f} {percentile(v, .95):>7.0f} {percentile(v, .99):>7.0f}")
    for p, recs in prov.items():
        v = [r["latency"] for r in recs]
        print(f"{p:8} {'all requests':15} {percentile(v, .5):>7.0f} {percentile(v, .95):>7.0f} {percentile(v, .99):>7.0f}")
    print("provider A was built to be 10 percent slower than B on both workloads, yet on the combined numbers A looks much faster, because 80 percent of A's requests are short classifications and only 20 percent of B's are; a ranking has to compare the same workload, and the lognormal latencies are simulated and not measured")

    section("2. Genuinely computing: attribution by request against an equal split")
    db = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
    db.execute("CREATE TABLE usage (request_id INTEGER, team TEXT, product TEXT, input_tokens INTEGER, output_tokens INTEGER)")
    rng = random.Random(3)
    rows = []
    profile = {"support": (400, 100, 6000), "engineering": (2500, 700, 1500), "finance": (6000, 1500, 500)}
    rid = 0
    for team, (tin, tout, count) in profile.items():
        for _ in range(count):
            rid += 1
            rows.append((rid, team, team + "-assistant", int(rng.gauss(tin, tin * .1)), int(rng.gauss(tout, tout * .1))))
    db.executemany("INSERT INTO usage VALUES (?,?,?,?,?)", rows)
    P_IN, P_OUT = 3.0, 15.0
    q = "SELECT team, COUNT(*) AS requests, SUM(input_tokens / 1e6 * ? + output_tokens / 1e6 * ?) AS cost FROM usage GROUP BY team ORDER BY cost DESC"
    res = db.execute(q, (P_IN, P_OUT)).fetchall()
    total = sum(r[2] for r in res)
    print(f"{'team':12} {'requests':>9} {'cost by request':>16} {'share':>7} {'equal split share':>18}")
    for team, cnt, cost in res:
        print(f"{team:12} {cnt:>9} {cost:>16.2f} {cost / total:>7.1%} {1 / 3:>18.1%}")
    counts = {t: c for t, c, _ in res}
    print("split by request count instead:", {t: f"{c / sum(counts.values()):.1%}" for t, c in counts.items()})
    print("the same shared bill allocated by the tokens each request used puts 42.5 percent on engineering, 32.0 on finance and 25.5 on support, an equal split would charge each team 33.3 percent, and a split by request count would charge support 75 percent for 25.5 percent of the use and finance 6.2 percent for 32.0; the query is a GROUP BY like the lesson's illustration run on a toy table, and a real billing export has its own schema")

    section("3. Genuinely computing: reconciling an estimate with a bill")
    billed = total * 1.03 + total * 0.04
    print(f"estimated from tokens {total:.2f} | billed {billed:.2f} | difference {billed - total:.2f} = {(billed - total) / billed:.1%} of the bill")
    print("the estimate was 93.5 percent of a bill that carried a 3 percent price difference and a further 4 percent line that no request could be tied to, so an estimate is a way to attribute cost and the provider's bill stays the authority; the percentages are invented")

    section("4. Genuinely running: redacting prompts before they reach logs")
    samples = ["Contact me at jane.doe@example.com about the refund", "Call +91 98765 43210 tomorrow", "Card 4111 1111 1111 1111 was charged twice", "My name is Jane Doe and I live at 12 Park Street", "Order 77 shipped on Monday"]
    for s in samples:
        print(f"{s!r:58} -> {redact(s)!r}")
    print("the email address, the phone number and the card number were replaced, while the name and the street address in the fourth line went through untouched and the order number was left alone, so pattern redaction catches structured identifiers and misses free-text personal data; it reduces what reaches a log and does not make a log safe")

    section("5. Genuinely computing: when is a fallback good enough")
    for name, k in (("primary", 95), ("fallback", 82), ("fallback B", 90), ("fallback C", 93)):
        lo, hi = wilson(k, 100)
        print(f"{name:11} {k}/100 correct | 95% interval [{lo:.3f}, {hi:.3f}]")
    print("tasks needed per model to tell 95 from 90 percent with about 80 percent power:", math.ceil(needed_n(.95, .90)), "| 95 from 93:", math.ceil(needed_n(.95, .93)), "| 95 from 82:", math.ceil(needed_n(.95, .82)))
    print("with 100 items the interval of the 90 percent fallback overlaps the primary's and the 82 percent one does not, and telling 95 from 90 reliably would take roughly 434 items per model while telling 95 from 93 would take about 2210 and 95 from 82 only 94, so a small evaluation set can show a clearly worse fallback and cannot certify a close one; the outcomes are invented counts")

    section("6. Genuinely running: a production-readiness check on a sample configuration")
    cfg = {"providers": [{"name": "primary", "tested_last_30_days": True}, {"name": "secondary", "tested_last_30_days": False}], "hardcoded_keys": False, "roles_scoped": True,
           "sensitivity_policy": True, "fallback_eval_passed": False, "max_attempts": 3, "deadline_ms": 5000, "breaker": True, "idempotency_keys": True,
           "redaction": True, "percentile_dashboards": True, "request_level_attribution": False, "quota_alarms": True}
    results = [(n, f(cfg)) for n, f in CHECKLIST]
    for n, ok in results:
        print(f"{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}  {n}")
    print(f"{sum(ok for _, ok in results)} of {len(results)} checks pass")
    print("nine of the twelve checks pass, and the three failures are a secondary provider that was not exercised in the last 30 days, a fallback that has not passed a quality evaluation and cost that is attributed per resource and not per request; the checklist is a teaching list and a passing configuration is not a finding of compliance")"}},{"type":"output","data":{"output":"

ಗುರುತುಗಳನ್ನು ಬದಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ ಮತ್ತು CHECKLIST ಸಂರಚನೆ ನಿಘಂಟಿನ ಮೇಲೆ ಹನ್ನೆರಡು ಪರಿಶೀಲನೆ ಹೊಂದಿದೆ.","code":"def percentile(values, f):
    o = sorted(values)
    pos = f * (len(o) - 1)
    lo, hi = math.floor(pos), math.ceil(pos)
    return o[lo] * (1 - (pos - lo)) + o[hi] * (pos - lo)


BASE_MS = {"classification": 350, "summarization": 900}


def make_records(n, seed, mix, slow_factor):
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    out = []
    for i in range(n):
        wl = "classification" if rng.random() < mix else "summarization"
        provider = "A"
        out.append({"provider": provider, "workload": wl, "team": rng.choice(["support", "engineering", "finance"]),
                    "latency": rng.lognormvariate(math.log(BASE_MS[wl] * slow_factor), 0.35)})
    return out


def wilson(k, n, z=1.96):
    p = k / n
    d = 1 + z * z / n
    c = (p + z * z / (2 * n)) / d
    h = z * math.sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + z * z / (4 * n * n)) / d
    return c - h, c + h


def needed_n(p1, p2, z_a=1.96, z_b=0.84):
    pbar = (p1 + p2) / 2
    return ((z_a * math.sqrt(2 * pbar * (1 - pbar)) + z_b * math.sqrt(p1 * (1 - p1) + p2 * (1 - p2))) / (p1 - p2)) ** 2


PATTERNS = {"email": re.compile(r"[\w.+-]+@[\w-]+\.[\w.]+"), "card": re.compile(r"\b(?:\d[ -]*?){13,16}\b"), "phone": re.compile(r"\+?\d[\d\s-]{8,}\d")}


def redact(text):
    for name, pat in PATTERNS.items():
        text = pat.sub(f"[{name}]", text)
    return text


CHECKLIST = [
    ("two usable provider paths", lambda c: len(c["providers"]) >= 2 and all(p["tested_last_30_days"] for p in c["providers"])),

]"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"mp_3.py","headingEn":"main(): experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() runs the percentile tables, the attribution, the reconciliation, the redaction, the fallback evaluation and the readiness check.","descKn":"main() ಶತಮಾನಾಂಶ ಕೋಷ್ಟಕ, ಹಂಚಿಕೆ, ಹೊಂದಾಣಿಕೆ, ಮರೆಮಾಚುವಿಕೆ, fallback ಮೌಲ್ಯಮಾಪನ ಮತ್ತು ಸಿದ್ಧತೆ ಪರಿಶೀಲನೆ ಓಡಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    section("1. Genuinely measuring: percentiles by provider and workload, and the pitfall of a mixed workload")

    print(f"{'provider':8} {'workload':15} {'P50':>7} {'P95':>7} {'P99':>7}")
    for p, recs in prov.items():
        for wl in ("classification", "summarization"):

    for p, recs in prov.items():
        v = [r["latency"] for r in recs]
        print(f"{p:8} {'all requests':15} {percentile(v, .5):>7.0f} {percentile(v, .95):>7.0f} {percentile(v, .99):>7.0f}")
    print("provider A was built to be 10 percent slower than B on both workloads, yet on the combined numbers A looks much faster, because 80 percent of A's requests are short classifications and only 20 percent of B's are; a ranking has to compare the same workload, and the lognormal latencies are simulated and not measured")

    section("2. Genuinely computing: attribution by request against an equal split")
    db = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
    db.execute("CREATE TABLE usage (request_id INTEGER, team TEXT, product TEXT, input_tokens INTEGER, output_tokens INTEGER)")
    rng = random.Random(3)
    rows = []
    profile = {"support": (400, 100, 6000), "engineering": (2500, 700, 1500), "finance": (6000, 1500, 500)}
    rid = 0
    for team, (tin, tout, count) in profile.items():
        for _ in range(count):
            rid += 1
            rows.append((rid, team, team + "-assistant", int(rng.gauss(tin, tin * .1)), int(rng.gauss(tout, tout * .1))))
    db.executemany("INSERT INTO usage VALUES (?,?,?,?,?)", rows)
    P_IN, P_OUT = 3.0, 15.0
    q = "SELECT team, COUNT(*) AS requests, SUM(input_tokens / 1e6 * ? + output_tokens / 1e6 * ?) AS cost FROM usage GROUP BY team ORDER BY cost DESC"
    res = db.execute(q, (P_IN, P_OUT)).fetchall()
    total = sum(r[2] for r in res)
    print(f"{'team':12} {'requests':>9} {'cost by request':>16} {'share':>7} {'equal split share':>18}")
    for team, cnt, cost in res:
        print(f"{team:12} {cnt:>9} {cost:>16.2f} {cost / total:>7.1%} {1 / 3:>18.1%}")
    counts = {t: c for t, c, _ in res}
    print("split by request count instead:", {t: f"{c / sum(counts.values()):.1%}" for t, c in counts.items()})
    print("the same shared bill allocated by the tokens each request used puts 42.5 percent on engineering, 32.0 on finance and 25.5 on support, an equal split would charge each team 33.3 percent, and a split by request count would charge support 75 percent for 25.5 percent of the use and finance 6.2 percent for 32.0; the query is a GROUP BY like the lesson's illustration run on a toy table, and a real billing export has its own schema")

    section("3. Genuinely computing: reconciling an estimate with a bill")

    print("the estimate was 93.5 percent of a bill that carried a 3 percent price difference and a further 4 percent line that no request could be tied to, so an estimate is a way to attribute cost and the provider's bill stays the authority; the percentages are invented")

    section("4. Genuinely running: redacting prompts before they reach logs")
    samples = ["Contact me at jane.doe@example.com about the refund", "Call +91 98765 43210 tomorrow", "Card 4111 1111 1111 1111 was charged twice", "My name is Jane Doe and I live at 12 Park Street", "Order 77 shipped on Monday"]
    for s in samples:
        print(f"{s!r:58} -> {redact(s)!r}")
    print("the email address, the phone number and the card number were replaced, while the name and the street address in the fourth line went through untouched and the order number was left alone, so pattern redaction catches structured identifiers and misses free-text personal data; it reduces what reaches a log and does not make a log safe")

    section("5. Genuinely computing: when is a fallback good enough")
    for name, k in (("primary", 95), ("fallback", 82), ("fallback B", 90), ("fallback C", 93)):
        lo, hi = wilson(k, 100)
        print(f"{name:11} {k}/100 correct | 95% interval [{lo:.3f}, {hi:.3f}]")
    print("tasks needed per model to tell 95 from 90 percent with about 80 percent power:", math.ceil(needed_n(.95, .90)), "| 95 from 93:", math.ceil(needed_n(.95, .93)), "| 95 from 82:", math.ceil(needed_n(.95, .82)))
    print("with 100 items the interval of the 90 percent fallback overlaps the primary's and the 82 percent one does not, and telling 95 from 90 reliably would take roughly 434 items per model while telling 95 from 93 would take about 2210 and 95 from 82 only 94, so a small evaluation set can show a clearly worse fallback and cannot certify a close one; the outcomes are invented counts")

    section("6. Genuinely running: a production-readiness check on a sample configuration")
    cfg = {"providers": [{"name": "primary", "tested_last_30_days": True}, {"name": "secondary", "tested_last_30_days": False}], "hardcoded_keys": False, "roles_scoped": True,
           "sensitivity_policy": True, "fallback_eval_passed": False, "max_attempts": 3, "deadline_ms": 5000, "breaker": True, "idempotency_keys": True,
           "redaction": True, "percentile_dashboards": True, "request_level_attribution": False, "quota_alarms": True}

    print(f"{sum(ok for _, ok in results)} of {len(results)} checks pass")

ಸಮಸ್ಯೆಗೆ ದೋಷ ಸೇರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ ಮತ್ತು ಅತಿಕ್ರಮಣವನ್ನು ಎರಡೂ ದಿಕ್ಕಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def is_nonempty(value):
    return isinstance(value, str) and bool(value.strip())


def normalize_path(value):
    raw = value.strip().replace(chr(92), "/")
    path = PurePosixPath(raw)
    if path.is_absolute():
        raise ValueError("absolute paths are not allowed")
    parts = []
    for part in path.parts:
        if part in ("", "."):
            continue
        if part == "..":
            raise ValueError("parent traversal is not allowed")
        parts.append(part)
    return "/".join(parts)


def path_covers(parent, child):
    return child == parent or child.startswith(parent + "/")


def validate_task_frame(frame):
    errors = []
    if not is_nonempty(frame.goal):
        errors.append("Goal is required.")
    for i, fact in enumerate(frame.repository_facts, start=1):
        if not is_nonempty(fact.claim):
            errors.append(f"Repository fact {i} has no claim.")
        if not is_nonempty(fact.evidence):
            errors.append(f"Repository fact {i} has no evidence receipt.")
    if not frame.allowed_paths:
        errors.append("At least one allowed path is required.")
    allowed, forbidden = [], []
    for label, raw_list, out in (("allowed", frame.allowed_paths, allowed), ("forbidden", frame.forbidden_paths, forbidden)):
        for raw in raw_list:
            try:
                n = normalize_path(raw)
                if not n:
                    errors.append(f"A {label} path cannot be empty.")
                else:
                    out.append(n)
            except ValueError as exc:
                errors.append(f"Invalid {label} path {raw!r}: {exc}.")
    for a in allowed:
        for f in forbidden:
            if path_covers(a, f) or path_covers(f, a):
                errors.append(f"Allowed and forbidden paths overlap: {a!r} vs {f!r}.")
    if not [c for c in frame.acceptance_commands if is_nonempty(c)]:
        errors.append("At least one acceptance command is required.")
    for i, u in enumerate(frame.unknowns, start=1):
        if not is_nonempty(u.question):
            errors.append(f"Unknown {i} has no question.")
        if u.category not in VALID_CATEGORIES:
            errors.append(f"Unknown {i} has invalid category {u.category!r}.")
        if not is_nonempty(u.action):
            errors.append(f"Unknown {i} has no planned action.")
    return errors"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"tf_1.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() runs the four required breakages, collects errors from a multiply-broken frame, compares directory-aware coverage with a naive prefix test, normalises nine paths and shows three weak frames that still pass.","descKn":"main() ನಾಲ್ಕು ಅಗತ್ಯ ಮುರಿತಗಳನ್ನು ಓಡಿಸಿ, ಬಹು-ಮುರಿದ frame ನಿಂದ ದೋಷ ಸಂಗ್ರಹಿಸಿ, ಡೈರೆಕ್ಟರಿ-ಅರಿವಿನ ವ್ಯಾಪ್ತಿಯನ್ನು ಸರಳ ಪೂರ್ವಪದ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆಗೆ ಹೋಲಿಸಿ, ಒಂಬತ್ತು paths ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯೀಕರಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ಇನ್ನೂ ಪಾಸ್ ಆಗುವ ಮೂರು ದುರ್ಬಲ frames ತೋರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    section("1. Genuinely running: the example frame and the four required breakages")
    base = example_task_frame()
    print("valid frame errors:", validate_task_frame(base))
    cases = []
    f = copy.deepcopy(base); f.goal = ""; cases.append(("remove the goal", f))
    f = copy.deepcopy(base); f.repository_facts[0].evidence = ""; cases.append(("remove a fact receipt", f))
    f = copy.deepcopy(base); f.allowed_paths = ["src/accounts/"]; f.forbidden_paths = ["src/accounts/service.py"]; cases.append(("overlap the paths", f))
    f = copy.deepcopy(base); f.acceptance_commands = []; cases.append(("remove acceptance command", f))
    for label, fr in cases:
        print(f"{label:26} -> {validate_task_frame(fr)}")
    print("each breakage produced its own specific message and nothing else, so the four failures are distinguishable and a generic 'invalid task' is never needed")

    section("2. Genuinely running: errors are collected, not stopped at the first")
    f = copy.deepcopy(base); f.goal = "   "; f.acceptance_commands = [""]; f.allowed_paths = []
    errs = validate_task_frame(f)
    print(len(errs), "errors in one run:", errs)
    print("a whitespace-only goal, a blank command and a missing allowed path were all reported together, which lets the author fix several problems in one pass; the tests should assert the specific message rather than the whole list for this reason")

    section("3. Genuinely measuring: directory-aware coverage versus a naive prefix test")
    for parent, child in (("src/accounts", "src/accounts/service.py"), ("src/accounts", "src/accounts_old/service.py"), ("src/accounts", "src/accounts"), ("src/accounts/service.py", "src/accounts")):
        print(f"{parent:26} covers {child:30} directory-aware={path_covers(parent, child)!s:5} naive startswith={child.startswith(parent)}")
    print("the naive startswith test said src/accounts covers src/accounts_old, which is a different directory, while the directory-aware test did not; and the last row is False in this direction, which is why the validator checks coverage both ways")

    section("4. Genuinely running: lexical path normalisation")
    for p in ("src/accounts/", "src/./accounts", "src\\accounts", "  src/accounts  ", "/etc/config", "../secrets", "src/../secrets", "", "."):
        try:
            print(f"{p!r:22} -> {normalize_path(p)!r}")
        except ValueError as e:
            print(f"{p!r:22} rejected: {e}")
    print("trailing slashes, dot segments, backslashes and padding all collapsed to one form, and absolute or parent-traversal paths were rejected; an empty string and a single dot normalised to an empty path, which the validator reports separately; this is lexical only and says nothing about symlinks or the real filesystem")

    section("5. Genuinely measuring: what the nonempty checks do not catch")
    f = copy.deepcopy(base); f.acceptance_commands = ["", "echo all tests passed"]
    print("acceptance commands ['', 'echo all tests passed']:", validate_task_frame(f))
    f = copy.deepcopy(base); f.goal = "Improve everything"
    print("goal 'Improve everything':", validate_task_frame(f))
    f = copy.deepcopy(base); f.repository_facts[0].evidence = "somewhere in the tests"
    print("evidence 'somewhere in the tests':", validate_task_frame(f))
    print("all three passed: a blank entry beside one real command is tolerated, an echo is accepted as an acceptance command, a vague goal is accepted and an evidence receipt with no file or line is accepted; the validator checks that things exist, and judging whether they are good still needs review")"}},{"type":"output","data":{"output":"

ಸಮಸ್ಯೆಗೆ ದೋಷ ಸೇರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ ಮತ್ತು ಅತಿಕ್ರಮಣವನ್ನು ಎರಡೂ ದಿಕ್ಕಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def is_nonempty(value):
    return isinstance(value, str) and bool(value.strip())


def normalize_path(value):
    raw = value.strip().replace(chr(92), "/")
    path = PurePosixPath(raw)
    if path.is_absolute():
        raise ValueError("absolute paths are not allowed")
    parts = []
    for part in path.parts:
        if part in ("", "."):
            continue
        if part == "..":
            raise ValueError("parent traversal is not allowed")
        parts.append(part)
    return "/".join(parts)


def path_covers(parent, child):
    return child == parent or child.startswith(parent + "/")


def validate_task_frame(frame):
    errors = []
    if not is_nonempty(frame.goal):
        errors.append("Goal is required.")
    for i, fact in enumerate(frame.repository_facts, start=1):
        if not is_nonempty(fact.claim):
            errors.append(f"Repository fact {i} has no claim.")
        if not is_nonempty(fact.evidence):
            errors.append(f"Repository fact {i} has no evidence receipt.")
    if not frame.allowed_paths:
        errors.append("At least one allowed path is required.")
    allowed, forbidden = [], []
    for label, raw_list, out in (("allowed", frame.allowed_paths, allowed), ("forbidden", frame.forbidden_paths, forbidden)):
        for raw in raw_list:
            try:
                n = normalize_path(raw)
                if not n:
                    errors.append(f"A {label} path cannot be empty.")
                else:
                    out.append(n)
            except ValueError as exc:
                errors.append(f"Invalid {label} path {raw!r}: {exc}.")
    for a in allowed:
        for f in forbidden:
            if path_covers(a, f) or path_covers(f, a):
                errors.append(f"Allowed and forbidden paths overlap: {a!r} vs {f!r}.")
    if not [c for c in frame.acceptance_commands if is_nonempty(c)]:
        errors.append("At least one acceptance command is required.")
    for i, u in enumerate(frame.unknowns, start=1):
        if not is_nonempty(u.question):
            errors.append(f"Unknown {i} has no question.")
        if u.category not in VALID_CATEGORIES:
            errors.append(f"Unknown {i} has invalid category {u.category!r}.")
        if not is_nonempty(u.action):
            errors.append(f"Unknown {i} has no planned action.")
    return errors"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"tf_1.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() runs the four required breakages, collects errors from a multiply-broken frame, compares directory-aware coverage with a naive prefix test, normalises nine paths and shows three weak frames that still pass.","descKn":"main() ನಾಲ್ಕು ಅಗತ್ಯ ಮುರಿತಗಳನ್ನು ಓಡಿಸಿ, ಬಹು-ಮುರಿದ frame ನಿಂದ ದೋಷ ಸಂಗ್ರಹಿಸಿ, ಡೈರೆಕ್ಟರಿ-ಅರಿವಿನ ವ್ಯಾಪ್ತಿಯನ್ನು ಸರಳ ಪೂರ್ವಪದ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆಗೆ ಹೋಲಿಸಿ, ಒಂಬತ್ತು paths ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯೀಕರಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ಇನ್ನೂ ಪಾಸ್ ಆಗುವ ಮೂರು ದುರ್ಬಲ frames ತೋರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    section("1. Genuinely running: the example frame and the four required breakages")
    base = example_task_frame()
    print("valid frame errors:", validate_task_frame(base))
    cases = []
    f = copy.deepcopy(base); f.goal = ""; cases.append(("remove the goal", f))
    f = copy.deepcopy(base); f.repository_facts[0].evidence = ""; cases.append(("remove a fact receipt", f))
    f = copy.deepcopy(base); f.allowed_paths = ["src/accounts/"]; f.forbidden_paths = ["src/accounts/service.py"]; cases.append(("overlap the paths", f))
    f = copy.deepcopy(base); f.acceptance_commands = []; cases.append(("remove acceptance command", f))
    for label, fr in cases:
        print(f"{label:26} -> {validate_task_frame(fr)}")
    print("each breakage produced its own specific message and nothing else, so the four failures are distinguishable and a generic 'invalid task' is never needed")

    section("2. Genuinely running: errors are collected, not stopped at the first")
    f = copy.deepcopy(base); f.goal = "   "; f.acceptance_commands = [""]; f.allowed_paths = []
    errs = validate_task_frame(f)
    print(len(errs), "errors in one run:", errs)
    print("a whitespace-only goal, a blank command and a missing allowed path were all reported together, which lets the author fix several problems in one pass; the tests should assert the specific message rather than the whole list for this reason")

    section("3. Genuinely measuring: directory-aware coverage versus a naive prefix test")
    for parent, child in (("src/accounts", "src/accounts/service.py"), ("src/accounts", "src/accounts_old/service.py"), ("src/accounts", "src/accounts"), ("src/accounts/service.py", "src/accounts")):
        print(f"{parent:26} covers {child:30} directory-aware={path_covers(parent, child)!s:5} naive startswith={child.startswith(parent)}")
    print("the naive startswith test said src/accounts covers src/accounts_old, which is a different directory, while the directory-aware test did not; and the last row is False in this direction, which is why the validator checks coverage both ways")

    section("4. Genuinely running: lexical path normalisation")
    for p in ("src/accounts/", "src/./accounts", "src\\accounts", "  src/accounts  ", "/etc/config", "../secrets", "src/../secrets", "", "."):
        try:
            print(f"{p!r:22} -> {normalize_path(p)!r}")
        except ValueError as e:
            print(f"{p!r:22} rejected: {e}")
    print("trailing slashes, dot segments, backslashes and padding all collapsed to one form, and absolute or parent-traversal paths were rejected; an empty string and a single dot normalised to an empty path, which the validator reports separately; this is lexical only and says nothing about symlinks or the real filesystem")

    section("5. Genuinely measuring: what the nonempty checks do not catch")
    f = copy.deepcopy(base); f.acceptance_commands = ["", "echo all tests passed"]
    print("acceptance commands ['', 'echo all tests passed']:", validate_task_frame(f))
    f = copy.deepcopy(base); f.goal = "Improve everything"
    print("goal 'Improve everything':", validate_task_frame(f))
    f = copy.deepcopy(base); f.repository_facts[0].evidence = "somewhere in the tests"
    print("evidence 'somewhere in the tests':", validate_task_frame(f))

def render(goal, facts, allowed, forbidden, commands, unknowns):
    lines = ["# Task Frame", "", "## Goal", "", goal.strip(), "", "## Repository Facts", ""]
    lines += [f"- **Claim:** {c}" + chr(10) + f"  - **Evidence:** `{e}`" for c, e in facts] or ["- No repository facts recorded."]
    lines += ["", "## Allowed Paths", ""] + [f"- {p}" for p in allowed]
    lines += ["", "## Forbidden Paths", ""] + [f"- {p}" for p in forbidden]
    lines += ["", "## Acceptance Commands", ""] + [f"- `{c}`" for c in commands]
    lines += ["", "## Unknowns", ""] + [f"- {cat}: {q}" for q, cat in unknowns]
    return chr(10).join(lines) + chr(10)

def render(goal, facts, allowed, forbidden, commands, unknowns):
    lines = ["# Task Frame", "", "## Goal", "", goal.strip(), "", "## Repository Facts", ""]
    lines += [f"- **Claim:** {c}" + chr(10) + f"  - **Evidence:** `{e}`" for c, e in facts] or ["- No repository facts recorded."]
    lines += ["", "## Allowed Paths", ""] + [f"- {p}" for p in allowed]
    lines += ["", "## Forbidden Paths", ""] + [f"- {p}" for p in forbidden]
    lines += ["", "## Acceptance Commands", ""] + [f"- `{c}`" for c in commands]
    lines += ["", "## Unknowns", ""] + [f"- {cat}: {q}" for q, cat in unknowns]
    return chr(10).join(lines) + chr(10)

    return [ln for ln in md.splitlines() if ln.startswith("## ")]

ಹೋಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def check_receipt(repo, claim_keyword, receipt):
    m = re.fullmatch(r"([\w./-]+):(\d+)", receipt)
    if not m:
        return "malformed receipt"
    path, line = m.group(1), int(m.group(2))
    f = Path(repo) / path
    if not f.is_file():
        return "file not found"
    lines = f.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    if line > len(lines):
        return f"line {line} beyond end of file ({len(lines)} lines)"
    return "supported" if claim_keyword in lines[line - 1] else "line exists but does not support the claim"


POLICY = {"discoverable": "investigate", "decidable": "decide within delegated authority and record it", "human": "stop and ask", "deferred": "record as a non-goal"}


def next_step(unknowns):
    steps = [(q, POLICY[c]) for q, c in unknowns]
    blocked = [q for q, c in unknowns if c == "human"]
    return steps, blocked


def changed_files(repo, base):
    out = set(git(repo, "diff", "--name-only", "--no-renames", base).splitlines())
    out |= set(git(repo, "ls-files", "--others", "--exclude-standard").splitlines())
    return sorted(out)


def covered(path, prefix):
    prefix = prefix.rstrip("/")
    return path == prefix or path.startswith(prefix + "/")


def audit(files, allowed, forbidden):
    bad = []
    for f in files:
        if any(covered(f, p) for p in forbidden):
            bad.append((f, "forbidden"))
        elif not any(covered(f, p) for p in allowed):
            bad.append((f, "outside allowed paths"))
    return bad"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"tf_3.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() builds a git repository, resolves five receipts, maps four unknowns, audits an allowed edit then a forbidden migration and a README, runs three acceptance commands and checks a test that asserts nothing about registration.","descKn":"main() git repository ನಿರ್ಮಿಸಿ, ಐದು ರಸೀದಿ ಪರಿಹರಿಸಿ, ನಾಲ್ಕು ಅಜ್ಞಾತ ಮ್ಯಾಪ್ ಮಾಡಿ, ಅನುಮತಿಸಿದ ಸಂಪಾದನೆ ನಂತರ ನಿಷೇಧಿತ migration ಮತ್ತು README ಲೆಕ್ಕಪರಿಶೋಧಿಸಿ, ಮೂರು ಸ್ವೀಕಾರ ಆದೇಶ ಓಡಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ನೋಂದಣಿ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಏನನ್ನೂ ಪ್ರತಿಪಾದಿಸದ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():

        (repo / "migrations/001.sql").write_text("-- schema" + chr(10), encoding="utf-8")
        git(repo, "add", "-A")

        section("1. Genuinely running: resolving evidence receipts in the repository")

ಹೋಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def check_receipt(repo, claim_keyword, receipt):
    m = re.fullmatch(r"([\w./-]+):(\d+)", receipt)
    if not m:
        return "malformed receipt"
    path, line = m.group(1), int(m.group(2))
    f = Path(repo) / path
    if not f.is_file():
        return "file not found"
    lines = f.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    if line > len(lines):
        return f"line {line} beyond end of file ({len(lines)} lines)"
    return "supported" if claim_keyword in lines[line - 1] else "line exists but does not support the claim"


POLICY = {"discoverable": "investigate", "decidable": "decide within delegated authority and record it", "human": "stop and ask", "deferred": "record as a non-goal"}


def next_step(unknowns):
    steps = [(q, POLICY[c]) for q, c in unknowns]
    blocked = [q for q, c in unknowns if c == "human"]
    return steps, blocked


def changed_files(repo, base):
    out = set(git(repo, "diff", "--name-only", "--no-renames", base).splitlines())
    out |= set(git(repo, "ls-files", "--others", "--exclude-standard").splitlines())
    return sorted(out)


def covered(path, prefix):
    prefix = prefix.rstrip("/")
    return path == prefix or path.startswith(prefix + "/")


def audit(files, allowed, forbidden):
    bad = []
    for f in files:
        if any(covered(f, p) for p in forbidden):
            bad.append((f, "forbidden"))
        elif not any(covered(f, p) for p in allowed):
            bad.append((f, "outside allowed paths"))
    return bad"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"tf_3.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() builds a git repository, resolves five receipts, maps four unknowns, audits an allowed edit then a forbidden migration and a README, runs three acceptance commands and checks a test that asserts nothing about registration.","descKn":"main() git repository ನಿರ್ಮಿಸಿ, ಐದು ರಸೀದಿ ಪರಿಹರಿಸಿ, ನಾಲ್ಕು ಅಜ್ಞಾತ ಮ್ಯಾಪ್ ಮಾಡಿ, ಅನುಮತಿಸಿದ ಸಂಪಾದನೆ ನಂತರ ನಿಷೇಧಿತ migration ಮತ್ತು README ಲೆಕ್ಕಪರಿಶೋಧಿಸಿ, ಮೂರು ಸ್ವೀಕಾರ ಆದೇಶ ಓಡಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ನೋಂದಣಿ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಏನನ್ನೂ ಪ್ರತಿಪಾದಿಸದ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:

        (repo / "tests").mkdir()
        (repo / "migrations").mkdir()
        (repo / "src/accounts/normalization.py").write_text("def normalize(email):" + chr(10) + "    return email.strip().lower()" + chr(10), encoding="utf-8")
        (repo / "tests/test_accounts.py").write_text("import unittest" + chr(10) + "class T(unittest.TestCase):" + chr(10) + "    def test_duplicate(self):" + chr(10) + "        self.assertEqual(409, 409)" + chr(10), encoding="utf-8")
        (repo / "migrations/001.sql").write_text("-- schema" + chr(10), encoding="utf-8")
        git(repo, "add", "-A")
        git(repo, "commit", "-q", "-m", "base")
        base = git(repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD")

        section("1. Genuinely running: resolving evidence receipts in the repository")
        for label, kw, rec in (("real line, supports claim", "lower", "src/accounts/normalization.py:2"), ("real line, wrong claim", "409 conflict", "src/accounts/normalization.py:2"), ("line past the end", "lower", "src/accounts/normalization.py:99"),
                               ("file missing", "x", "src/accounts/nope.py:1"), ("no line number", "x", "tests/test_accounts.py")):
            print(f"{label:26} {rec:36} -> {check_receipt(repo, kw, rec)}")
        print("a receipt that looked fine in shape was caught when its line did not exist, when the file was missing and when the line did not contain what the claim says; only the first is actually supported, and even that shows the line says something, not that the claim is wholly true")

        section("2. Genuinely running: the four kinds of unknown and what each requires")
        unknowns = [("Does the database already enforce uniqueness?", "discoverable"), ("What should the private helper be called?", "decidable"), ("May the duplicate response change for existing clients?", "human"), ("Should the registration subsystem be refactored?", "deferred")]
        steps, blocked = next_step(unknowns)
        for q, s in steps:
            print(f"{s:48} <- {q}")
        print("dependent work blocked until a human answers:", blocked)
        print("only the human unknown stops dependent work; the discoverable one is a task for the agent and the deferred one leaves the scope alone, which is the difference between an unresolved question and a blocker")

        section("3. Genuinely running: a scope audit of the real diff")
        allowed, forbidden = ["src/accounts/", "tests/accounts/"], ["migrations/", "deploy/", "src/auth/"]
        (repo / "src/accounts/service.py").write_text("x = 1" + chr(10), encoding="utf-8")
        print("only an allowed file changed:", audit(changed_files(repo, base), allowed, forbidden))
        (repo / "migrations/002_unique_email.sql").write_text("ALTER TABLE ..." + chr(10), encoding="utf-8")
        (repo / "README.md").write_text("docs" + chr(10), encoding="utf-8")
        files = changed_files(repo, base)
        print("changed files:", files)
        print("audit:", audit(files, allowed, forbidden))
        print("the unique-index migration the agent thought cleanest was flagged as forbidden and the README as outside the allowed paths, though the tests might all pass; this is the moment the agent should stop and ask for the scope to be extended, not edit quietly")

        section("4. Genuinely running: did the acceptance command actually run a test?")

            p = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=repo, capture_output=True, text=True)
            m = re.search(r"Ran (\d+) test", p.stderr)

        print("the echo exited 0 and printed that tests passed while running none, and the missing module exited non-zero; an acceptance command is evidence only when the number of tests run is checked along with the exit code, and when the test named actually covers the claim")

class WorkItem:
    id: str
    change: str
    evidence: List[str]
    dependencies: List[str]
    proof: str


def validate_plan(items):
    if not items:
        raise ValueError("Plan cannot be empty")
    ids = [i.id for i in items]
    if len(ids) != len(set(ids)):
        raise ValueError("Duplicate work item identifier")
    known = set(ids)
    for it in items:
        if not it.id.strip():
            raise ValueError("Work item has no identifier")
        if not it.change.strip():
            raise ValueError(f"{it.id}: missing change description")
        if not it.evidence or not all(e.strip() for e in it.evidence):
            raise ValueError(f"{it.id}: missing evidence")
        if not it.proof.strip():
            raise ValueError(f"{it.id}: missing proof")
        if len(it.dependencies) != len(set(it.dependencies)):
            raise ValueError(f"{it.id}: duplicate dependency")
        for d in it.dependencies:
            if d == it.id:
                raise ValueError(f"{it.id}: depends on itself")
            if d not in known:
                raise ValueError(f"{it.id}: unknown dependency {d}")


def execution_waves(items):
    validate_plan(items)
    remaining = {i.id: set(i.dependencies) for i in items}
    done, waves = set(), []
    while remaining:

class WorkItem:
    id: str
    change: str
    evidence: List[str]
    dependencies: List[str]
    proof: str


def validate_plan(items):
    if not items:
        raise ValueError("Plan cannot be empty")
    ids = [i.id for i in items]
    if len(ids) != len(set(ids)):
        raise ValueError("Duplicate work item identifier")
    known = set(ids)
    for it in items:
        if not it.id.strip():
            raise ValueError("Work item has no identifier")
        if not it.change.strip():
            raise ValueError(f"{it.id}: missing change description")
        if not it.evidence or not all(e.strip() for e in it.evidence):
            raise ValueError(f"{it.id}: missing evidence")
        if not it.proof.strip():
            raise ValueError(f"{it.id}: missing proof")
        if len(it.dependencies) != len(set(it.dependencies)):
            raise ValueError(f"{it.id}: duplicate dependency")
        for d in it.dependencies:
            if d == it.id:
                raise ValueError(f"{it.id}: depends on itself")
            if d not in known:
                raise ValueError(f"{it.id}: unknown dependency {d}")


def execution_waves(items):
    validate_plan(items)
    remaining = {i.id: set(i.dependencies) for i in items}
    done, waves = set(), []
    while remaining:
        ready = sorted(k for k, deps in remaining.items() if deps <= done)
        if not ready:
            raise ValueError("Dependency cycle detected among: " + ", ".join(sorted(remaining)))
        waves.append(ready)
        for k in ready:
            del remaining[k]
        done.update(ready)
    return waves"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"ep_1.py","headingEn":"main(): six experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಆರು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() schedules the lesson plan, tries eight defective plans, runs a cycle and its repair, computes a critical path from invented durations, passes a plan with vague evidence and writes the plan as JSON.","descKn":"main() lesson ಯೋಜನೆ ವೇಳಾಪಟ್ಟಿ ಮಾಡಿ, ಎಂಟು ದೋಷಯುಕ್ತ ಯೋಜನೆ ಪ್ರಯತ್ನಿಸಿ, ಚಕ್ರ ಮತ್ತು ಅದರ ದುರಸ್ತಿ ಓಡಿಸಿ, ಕಾಲ್ಪನಿಕ ಅವಧಿಗಳಿಂದ critical path ಲೆಕ್ಕ ಹಾಕಿ, ಅಸ್ಪಷ್ಟ ಸಾಕ್ಷ್ಯ ಇರುವ ಯೋಜನೆ ಪಾಸ್ ಮಾಡಿ ಯೋಜನೆಯನ್ನು JSON ಆಗಿ ಬರೆಯುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():

    d = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(65536), b""):
            d.update(chunk)
    return d.hexdigest()


def inspect_file(root, rel):
    root = Path(root).resolve()
    target = (root / rel).resolve()
    if root != target and root not in target.parents:
        return {"source": rel, "status": "outside_root"}
    if not target.exists():
        return {"source": rel, "status": "missing"}
    if target.is_dir():
        return {"source": rel, "status": "directory"}
    return {"source": rel, "status": "found", "size": target.stat().st_size, "sha256": sha(target)[:12]}


def run_proof(command, cwd, timeout=20, expected=0):
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    try:
        p = subprocess.run(command, cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout, check=False)
        r = {"exit_code": p.returncode, "timed_out": False, "stdout": p.stdout.strip()[-120:], "stderr": p.stderr.strip()[-120:]}
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        r = {"exit_code": None, "timed_out": True, "stdout": "", "stderr": ""}
    r["seconds"] = round(time.monotonic() - t0, 2)
    r["passed"] = (not r["timed_out"]) and r["exit_code"] == expected
    return r


def tests_ran(stderr):
    import re
    m = re.search(r"Ran (\d+) test", stderr)
    return int(m.group(1)) if m else 0"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"ep_2.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() builds a temporary repository, collects five receipts, edits a file to make a receipt stale, replaces a planned item after finding an existing helper, runs four proof commands and three acceptance-style commands.","descKn":"main() ತಾತ್ಕಾಲಿಕ repository ನಿರ್ಮಿಸಿ, ಐದು ರಸೀದಿ ಸಂಗ್ರಹಿಸಿ, ರಸೀದಿ ಹಳೆಯದಾಗಲು ಫೈಲ್ ಸಂಪಾದಿಸಿ, ಇರುವ helper ಕಂಡ ನಂತರ ಯೋಜಿತ ಘಟಕ ಬದಲಿಸಿ, ನಾಲ್ಕು ಪುರಾವೆ ಆದೇಶ ಮತ್ತು ಮೂರು ಸ್ವೀಕಾರ-ಶೈಲಿ ಆದೇಶ ಓಡಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        root = Path(d) / "repo"
        (root / "app").mkdir(parents=True)
        (root / "tests").mkdir()
        (root / "app/endpoint.py").write_text("def products():" + chr(10) + "    return [1, 2, 3]" + chr(10), encoding="utf-8")
        (root / "app/helpers.py").write_text("def paginate(items, size=20):" + chr(10) + "    return items[:size]" + chr(10), encoding="utf-8")
        (root / "tests/test_endpoint.py").write_text("import unittest" + chr(10) + "from app.endpoint import products" + chr(10) + "class T(unittest.TestCase):" + chr(10) + "    def test_products(self):" + chr(10) + "        self.assertEqual(len(products()), 3)" + chr(10), encoding="utf-8")
        (root / "app/__init__.py").write_text("", encoding="utf-8")
        (root / "tests/__init__.py").write_text("", encoding="utf-8")

        section("1. Genuinely running: evidence receipts for five paths")
        for rel in ("app/endpoint.py", "app/missing.py", "app", "../outside.txt", "app/../../outside.txt"):
            print(f"{rel:24} {inspect_file(root, rel)}")
        print("a real file gave size and a SHA-256 prefix, a missing file and a directory were reported as such, and both paths that climbed above the root were refused; a receipt says the file existed with that content when inspected, and nothing about what the code means")

        section("2. Genuinely running: a receipt goes stale when the file changes")
        before = inspect_file(root, "app/endpoint.py")
        (root / "app/endpoint.py").write_text("def products(page_size=20):" + chr(10) + "    return [1, 2, 3][:page_size]" + chr(10), encoding="utf-8")
        after = inspect_file(root, "app/endpoint.py")
        print("before:", before["sha256"], "| after:", after["sha256"], "| same evidence:", before["sha256"] == after["sha256"])
        print("the hash changed, so an observation recorded against the first version no longer describes the file; evidence should name the content it saw, and a plan built on old receipts needs them refreshed")

        section("3. Genuinely running: evidence that changes the plan")
        planned = "W-002: create a new pagination utility in app/pagination.py"
        found = inspect_file(root, "app/helpers.py")
        revised = "W-002: extend the existing paginate helper in app/helpers.py" if found["status"] == "found" else planned
        print("planned:", planned)
        print("inspection of app/helpers.py:", found["status"], "| contains paginate:", "def paginate" in (root / "app/helpers.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        print("revised:", revised)
        print("the existing helper was found, so the item to build a new utility was replaced by one to extend it; evidence that never changes a decision is decoration, and this is a case where it did")

        section("4. Genuinely running: proof commands, run for real and recorded")
        cases = {"unittest that passes": [PY, "-B", "-m", "unittest", "tests.test_endpoint"], "command that fails": [PY, "-c", "import sys; sys.stderr.write('assertion failed'); sys.exit(1)"],
                 "command that hangs": [PY, "-c", "import time; time.sleep(30)"], "program that cannot start": ["no-such-program-xyz"]}
        for label, cmd in cases.items():
            try:
                r = run_proof(cmd, root, timeout=1.5)
                print(f"{label:26} exit={r['exit_code']!s:5} timed_out={r['timed_out']!s:5} passed={r['passed']!s:5} tests_ran={tests_ran(r['stderr'])}")
            except OSError as e:
                print(f"{label:26} could not launch: {type(e).__name__}")
        print("the passing, failing and hanging commands each produced a different record, and the program that could not start raised before any record existed, so a runner must catch that case too or the item would silently have no proof")

        section("5. Genuinely checking: exit 0 is not proof the right test ran")
        for label, cmd in (("echo instead of a test", [PY, "-c", "print('All tests passed')"]), ("wrong module name", [PY, "-B", "-m", "unittest", "tests.test_nothing"]), ("named test", [PY, "-B", "-m", "unittest", "tests.test_endpoint"])):
            r = run_proof(cmd, root)
            print(f"{label:24} exit={r['exit_code']} tests_ran={tests_ran(r['stderr'])} passed={r['passed']}")
        print("the echo passed with zero tests run and the misnamed module failed, which is why the gate checks the test count and the command against the planned proof, and why a planned proof is not an executed proof")"}},{"type":"output","data":{"output":"

ಆರ್ಗ್ಯುಮೆಂಟ್ ಪಟ್ಟಿಯನ್ನು timeout ಜೊತೆ ಓಡಿಸಿ exit code, ಔಟ್‌ಪುಟ್ ಮತ್ತು ಅವಧಿ ದಾಖಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. tests_ran unittest ಸಾರಾಂಶದಿಂದ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆಗಳ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆ ಓದುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def sha(path):
    d = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(65536), b""):
            d.update(chunk)
    return d.hexdigest()


def inspect_file(root, rel):
    root = Path(root).resolve()
    target = (root / rel).resolve()
    if root != target and root not in target.parents:
        return {"source": rel, "status": "outside_root"}
    if not target.exists():
        return {"source": rel, "status": "missing"}
    if target.is_dir():
        return {"source": rel, "status": "directory"}
    return {"source": rel, "status": "found", "size": target.stat().st_size, "sha256": sha(target)[:12]}


def run_proof(command, cwd, timeout=20, expected=0):
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    try:
        p = subprocess.run(command, cwd=cwd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout, check=False)
        r = {"exit_code": p.returncode, "timed_out": False, "stdout": p.stdout.strip()[-120:], "stderr": p.stderr.strip()[-120:]}
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        r = {"exit_code": None, "timed_out": True, "stdout": "", "stderr": ""}
    r["seconds"] = round(time.monotonic() - t0, 2)
    r["passed"] = (not r["timed_out"]) and r["exit_code"] == expected
    return r


def tests_ran(stderr):
    import re
    m = re.search(r"Ran (\d+) test", stderr)
    return int(m.group(1)) if m else 0"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"ep_2.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() builds a temporary repository, collects five receipts, edits a file to make a receipt stale, replaces a planned item after finding an existing helper, runs four proof commands and three acceptance-style commands.","descKn":"main() ತಾತ್ಕಾಲಿಕ repository ನಿರ್ಮಿಸಿ, ಐದು ರಸೀದಿ ಸಂಗ್ರಹಿಸಿ, ರಸೀದಿ ಹಳೆಯದಾಗಲು ಫೈಲ್ ಸಂಪಾದಿಸಿ, ಇರುವ helper ಕಂಡ ನಂತರ ಯೋಜಿತ ಘಟಕ ಬದಲಿಸಿ, ನಾಲ್ಕು ಪುರಾವೆ ಆದೇಶ ಮತ್ತು ಮೂರು ಸ್ವೀಕಾರ-ಶೈಲಿ ಆದೇಶ ಓಡಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        root = Path(d) / "repo"
        (root / "app").mkdir(parents=True)
        (root / "tests").mkdir()
        (root / "app/endpoint.py").write_text("def products():" + chr(10) + "    return [1, 2, 3]" + chr(10), encoding="utf-8")
        (root / "app/helpers.py").write_text("def paginate(items, size=20):" + chr(10) + "    return items[:size]" + chr(10), encoding="utf-8")
        (root / "tests/test_endpoint.py").write_text("import unittest" + chr(10) + "from app.endpoint import products" + chr(10) + "class T(unittest.TestCase):" + chr(10) + "    def test_products(self):" + chr(10) + "        self.assertEqual(len(products()), 3)" + chr(10), encoding="utf-8")
        (root / "app/__init__.py").write_text("", encoding="utf-8")
        (root / "tests/__init__.py").write_text("", encoding="utf-8")

        section("1. Genuinely running: evidence receipts for five paths")
        for rel in ("app/endpoint.py", "app/missing.py", "app", "../outside.txt", "app/../../outside.txt"):
            print(f"{rel:24} {inspect_file(root, rel)}")
        print("a real file gave size and a SHA-256 prefix, a missing file and a directory were reported as such, and both paths that climbed above the root were refused; a receipt says the file existed with that content when inspected, and nothing about what the code means")

        section("2. Genuinely running: a receipt goes stale when the file changes")
        before = inspect_file(root, "app/endpoint.py")
        (root / "app/endpoint.py").write_text("def products(page_size=20):" + chr(10) + "    return [1, 2, 3][:page_size]" + chr(10), encoding="utf-8")
        after = inspect_file(root, "app/endpoint.py")
        print("before:", before["sha256"], "| after:", after["sha256"], "| same evidence:", before["sha256"] == after["sha256"])
        print("the hash changed, so an observation recorded against the first version no longer describes the file; evidence should name the content it saw, and a plan built on old receipts needs them refreshed")

        section("3. Genuinely running: evidence that changes the plan")
        planned = "W-002: create a new pagination utility in app/pagination.py"
        found = inspect_file(root, "app/helpers.py")
        revised = "W-002: extend the existing paginate helper in app/helpers.py" if found["status"] == "found" else planned
        print("planned:", planned)
        print("inspection of app/helpers.py:", found["status"], "| contains paginate:", "def paginate" in (root / "app/helpers.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        print("revised:", revised)
        print("the existing helper was found, so the item to build a new utility was replaced by one to extend it; evidence that never changes a decision is decoration, and this is a case where it did")

        section("4. Genuinely running: proof commands, run for real and recorded")
        cases = {"unittest that passes": [PY, "-B", "-m", "unittest", "tests.test_endpoint"], "command that fails": [PY, "-c", "import sys; sys.stderr.write('assertion failed'); sys.exit(1)"],
                 "command that hangs": [PY, "-c", "import time; time.sleep(30)"], "program that cannot start": ["no-such-program-xyz"]}
        for label, cmd in cases.items():
            try:
                r = run_proof(cmd, root, timeout=1.5)
                print(f"{label:26} exit={r['exit_code']!s:5} timed_out={r['timed_out']!s:5} passed={r['passed']!s:5} tests_ran={tests_ran(r['stderr'])}")
            except OSError as e:
                print(f"{label:26} could not launch: {type(e).__name__}")
        print("the passing, failing and hanging commands each produced a different record, and the program that could not start raised before any record existed, so a runner must catch that case too or the item would silently have no proof")

        section("5. Genuinely checking: exit 0 is not proof the right test ran")
        for label, cmd in (("echo instead of a test", [PY, "-c", "print('All tests passed')"]), ("wrong module name", [PY, "-B", "-m", "unittest", "tests.test_nothing"]), ("named test", [PY, "-B", "-m", "unittest", "tests.test_endpoint"])):
            r = run_proof(cmd, root)
            print(f"{label:24} exit={r['exit_code']} tests_ran={tests_ran(r['stderr'])} passed={r['passed']}")
        print("the echo passed with zero tests run and the misnamed module failed, which is why the gate checks the test count and the command against the planned proof, and why a planned proof is not an executed proof")"}},{"type":"output","data":{"output":"

ಉಲ್ಲೇಖಗಳನ್ನು ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ, compute_waves ವೇಳಾಪಟ್ಟಿ ಮಾಡಿ ಚಕ್ರದಿಂದ ತಡೆಯಲ್ಪಟ್ಟ ಘಟಕಗಳನ್ನು ಹೆಸರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def normalize_path(path):
    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path.strip():
        raise ValueError("Expected a non-empty path")
    raw = path.replace(chr(92), "/")
    if raw.startswith("/") or (len(raw) > 1 and raw[1] == ":"):
        raise ValueError("Expected a relative path")
    if ".." in raw.split("/"):
        raise ValueError("Parent traversal is not allowed")
    parts = tuple(p for p in PurePosixPath(raw).parts if p != ".")
    if not parts:
        raise ValueError("Repository root ownership is not allowed")
    return parts


def paths_overlap(a, b):
    x, y = normalize_path(a), normalize_path(b)
    n = min(len(x), len(y))
    return x[:n] == y[:n]


def unit(uid, paths, deps=()):
    return WorkUnit(uid, f"Complete {uid}", f"{uid}-agent", tuple(paths), tuple(deps), ("Required proof",), ("Changed files and risks",))


def validate_ownership(units):
    for i, a in enumerate(units):
        for b in units[i + 1:]:
            for pa in a.paths:
                for pb in b.paths:
                    if paths_overlap(pa, pb):
                        raise ValueError(f"Overlapping ownership: {a.unit_id}:{pa} and {b.unit_id}:{pb}")


def validate_dependencies(units):
    ids = [u.unit_id for u in units]
    if len(ids) != len(set(ids)):
        raise ValueError("Duplicate work-unit IDs")
    for u in units:
        for d in u.dependencies:
            if d == u.unit_id:
                raise ValueError(f"{u.unit_id} depends on itself")
            if d not in ids:
                raise ValueError(f"{u.unit_id} has unknown dependency: {d}")


def compute_waves(units):
    validate_dependencies(units)
    pending = {u.unit_id: set(u.dependencies) for u in units}
    done, waves = set(), []
    while pending:
        ready = sorted(k for k, d in pending.items() if d <= done)
        if not ready:
            raise ValueError("No executable units remain; dependency graph is blocked by: " + ", ".join(sorted(pending)))
        waves.append(ready)
        for k in ready:
            del pending[k]
        done.update(ready)
    return waves


def build_plan(units):
    validate_dependencies(units)
    validate_ownership(units)
    return {"units": [u.unit_id for u in units], "execution_waves": compute_waves(units), "status": "planned"}"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"dg_1.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() plans four units and then makes docs own app/, compares component and text-prefix matching, tries seven unsafe paths, tries four dependency defects and computes three illustrative serial-versus-parallel totals.","descKn":"main() ನಾಲ್ಕು ಘಟಕಗಳನ್ನು ಯೋಜಿಸಿ ನಂತರ docs ಗೆ app/ ಮಾಲೀಕತ್ವ ನೀಡಿ, ಘಟಕ ಮತ್ತು ಪಠ್ಯ-ಪೂರ್ವಪದ ಹೊಂದಾಣಿಕೆ ಹೋಲಿಸಿ, ಏಳು ಅಸುರಕ್ಷಿತ paths ಪ್ರಯತ್ನಿಸಿ, ನಾಲ್ಕು ಅವಲಂಬನೆ ದೋಷ ಪ್ರಯತ್ನಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ಮೂರು ಕಾಲ್ಪನಿಕ ಅನುಕ್ರಮ-ವಿರುದ್ಧ-ಸಮಾನಾಂತರ ಒಟ್ಟು ಲೆಕ್ಕ ಹಾಕುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    section("1. Genuinely running: a valid plan and the lesson's app/ ownership experiment")
    api, docs = unit("api", ["app/accounts.py"]), unit("docs", ["docs/accounts.md"])
    review, integ = unit("review", ["reviews/accounts.json"], ["api"]), unit("integration", ["outputs/integration.json"], ["api", "docs", "review"])
    print("plan:", build_plan([api, docs, review, integ]))
    bad_docs = unit("docs", ["app/"])

    except ValueError as e:

    section("2. Genuinely measuring: component matching versus a text prefix")

        print(f"{a:18} vs {b:18} component overlap={paths_overlap(a, b)!s:5} naive startswith={b.startswith(a)}")
    print("the owner written as app without a trailing slash made the text prefix claim application/x.py as inside it (second row), while the component comparison did not and gave the same answer for app and app/; the last row shows case: this comparison is case-sensitive, so App/accounts.py and app/ do not overlap here even though they would be the same folder on a case-insensitive filesystem")

    section("3. Genuinely running: unsafe paths are rejected before they can own anything")

        except ValueError as e:

    print("traversal, absolute, drive-letter, empty and root paths were refused while backslashes and dot segments were cleaned; this is lexical only, and symlinks and the real filesystem are not consulted")

    section("4. Genuinely running: dependency defects and a blocked graph")
    for label, us in (("unknown dependency", [unit("a", ["a/"], ["zzz"])]), ("self dependency", [unit("a", ["a/"], ["a"])]), ("duplicate ids", [unit("a", ["a/"]), unit("a", ["b/"])]),

        except ValueError as e:
            print(f"{label:20} rejected: {e}")
    print("ownership and dependencies are separate checks: two units can own different files and still be unable to run, and the cycle was reported with the names of the units that blocked it")

    section("5. Genuinely computing: when parallel delegation is slower (ILLUSTRATIVE numbers)")

ತಿರಸ್ಕರಿಸಿ ಚುಕ್ಕೆ ಭಾಗಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ಬ್ಯಾಕ್‌ಸ್ಲ್ಯಾಶ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು ಶುದ್ಧೀಕರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. paths_overlap path ಘಟಕಗಳನ್ನು ಹೋಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. validate_ownership ಪ್ರತಿ ಘಟಕ ಜೋಡಿ ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ, validate_dependencies ids ಮತ್ತು ಉಲ್ಲೇಖಗಳನ್ನು ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ, compute_waves ವೇಳಾಪಟ್ಟಿ ಮಾಡಿ ಚಕ್ರದಿಂದ ತಡೆಯಲ್ಪಟ್ಟ ಘಟಕಗಳನ್ನು ಹೆಸರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def normalize_path(path):
    if not isinstance(path, str) or not path.strip():
        raise ValueError("Expected a non-empty path")
    raw = path.replace(chr(92), "/")
    if raw.startswith("/") or (len(raw) > 1 and raw[1] == ":"):
        raise ValueError("Expected a relative path")
    if ".." in raw.split("/"):
        raise ValueError("Parent traversal is not allowed")
    parts = tuple(p for p in PurePosixPath(raw).parts if p != ".")
    if not parts:
        raise ValueError("Repository root ownership is not allowed")
    return parts


def paths_overlap(a, b):
    x, y = normalize_path(a), normalize_path(b)
    n = min(len(x), len(y))
    return x[:n] == y[:n]


def unit(uid, paths, deps=()):
    return WorkUnit(uid, f"Complete {uid}", f"{uid}-agent", tuple(paths), tuple(deps), ("Required proof",), ("Changed files and risks",))


def validate_ownership(units):
    for i, a in enumerate(units):
        for b in units[i + 1:]:
            for pa in a.paths:
                for pb in b.paths:
                    if paths_overlap(pa, pb):
                        raise ValueError(f"Overlapping ownership: {a.unit_id}:{pa} and {b.unit_id}:{pb}")


def validate_dependencies(units):
    ids = [u.unit_id for u in units]
    if len(ids) != len(set(ids)):
        raise ValueError("Duplicate work-unit IDs")
    for u in units:
        for d in u.dependencies:
            if d == u.unit_id:
                raise ValueError(f"{u.unit_id} depends on itself")
            if d not in ids:
                raise ValueError(f"{u.unit_id} has unknown dependency: {d}")


def compute_waves(units):
    validate_dependencies(units)
    pending = {u.unit_id: set(u.dependencies) for u in units}
    done, waves = set(), []
    while pending:
        ready = sorted(k for k, d in pending.items() if d <= done)
        if not ready:
            raise ValueError("No executable units remain; dependency graph is blocked by: " + ", ".join(sorted(pending)))
        waves.append(ready)
        for k in ready:
            del pending[k]
        done.update(ready)
    return waves


def build_plan(units):
    validate_dependencies(units)
    validate_ownership(units)
    return {"units": [u.unit_id for u in units], "execution_waves": compute_waves(units), "status": "planned"}"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"dg_1.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() plans four units and then makes docs own app/, compares component and text-prefix matching, tries seven unsafe paths, tries four dependency defects and computes three illustrative serial-versus-parallel totals.","descKn":"main() ನಾಲ್ಕು ಘಟಕಗಳನ್ನು ಯೋಜಿಸಿ ನಂತರ docs ಗೆ app/ ಮಾಲೀಕತ್ವ ನೀಡಿ, ಘಟಕ ಮತ್ತು ಪಠ್ಯ-ಪೂರ್ವಪದ ಹೊಂದಾಣಿಕೆ ಹೋಲಿಸಿ, ಏಳು ಅಸುರಕ್ಷಿತ paths ಪ್ರಯತ್ನಿಸಿ, ನಾಲ್ಕು ಅವಲಂಬನೆ ದೋಷ ಪ್ರಯತ್ನಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ಮೂರು ಕಾಲ್ಪನಿಕ ಅನುಕ್ರಮ-ವಿರುದ್ಧ-ಸಮಾನಾಂತರ ಒಟ್ಟು ಲೆಕ್ಕ ಹಾಕುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    section("1. Genuinely running: a valid plan and the lesson's app/ ownership experiment")
    api, docs = unit("api", ["app/accounts.py"]), unit("docs", ["docs/accounts.md"])
    review, integ = unit("review", ["reviews/accounts.json"], ["api"]), unit("integration", ["outputs/integration.json"], ["api", "docs", "review"])
    print("plan:", build_plan([api, docs, review, integ]))
    bad_docs = unit("docs", ["app/"])
    try:
        build_plan([api, bad_docs, review, integ])
    except ValueError as e:
        print("docs owns app/:", e)
    print("owning the directory app/ also covers app/accounts.py, so the plan was refused before any worker started; the contract is checked as a plan, which is the only moment it is cheap to fix")

    section("2. Genuinely measuring: component matching versus a text prefix")

        print(f"{a:18} vs {b:18} component overlap={paths_overlap(a, b)!s:5} naive startswith={b.startswith(a)}")
    print("the owner written as app without a trailing slash made the text prefix claim application/x.py as inside it (second row), while the component comparison did not and gave the same answer for app and app/; the last row shows case: this comparison is case-sensitive, so App/accounts.py and app/ do not overlap here even though they would be the same folder on a case-insensitive filesystem")

    section("3. Genuinely running: unsafe paths are rejected before they can own anything")
    for p in ("../secrets.txt", "/etc/passwd", "C:\\Windows\\x", "", ".", "app\\accounts.py", "./app/./accounts.py"):
        try:
            print(f"{p!r:24} -> {normalize_path(p)}")
        except ValueError as e:
            print(f"{p!r:24} rejected: {e}")
    print("traversal, absolute, drive-letter, empty and root paths were refused while backslashes and dot segments were cleaned; this is lexical only, and symlinks and the real filesystem are not consulted")

    section("4. Genuinely running: dependency defects and a blocked graph")
    for label, us in (("unknown dependency", [unit("a", ["a/"], ["zzz"])]), ("self dependency", [unit("a", ["a/"], ["a"])]), ("duplicate ids", [unit("a", ["a/"]), unit("a", ["b/"])]),
                      ("cycle", [unit("a", ["a/"], ["b"]), unit("b", ["b/"], ["a"])])):
        try:

        except ValueError as e:
            print(f"{label:20} rejected: {e}")
    print("ownership and dependencies are separate checks: two units can own different files and still be unable to run, and the cycle was reported with the names of the units that blocked it")

    section("5. Genuinely computing: when parallel delegation is slower (ILLUSTRATIVE numbers)")

    for label, crit, coord, integ_t, rework in (("tidy split", 4, 1, 2, 0), ("some conflicts", 4, 1, 2, 3), ("heavy conflicts", 4, 2, 3, 6)):

ಮತ್ತು ಟ್ರ್ಯಾಕ್ ಮಾಡದ ಫೈಲ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು ಸೇರಿಸಿ rename ಪತ್ತೆ ಆರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. owned path ಘಟಕಗಳನ್ನು ಹೋಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ ಮತ್ತು audit ಮಾಲೀಕತ್ವದ paths ಹೊರಗಿನ ಪ್ರತಿ ಬದಲಾವಣೆ ಪಟ್ಟಿ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def git(repo, *a):
    return subprocess.run(GIT + list(a), cwd=repo, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()


def committed_changes(repo, base):
    return sorted(git(repo, "diff", "--name-only", f"{base}..HEAD").splitlines())


def all_changes(repo, base):
    names = set(git(repo, "diff", "--name-only", "--no-renames", base).splitlines())
    names |= set(git(repo, "ls-files", "--others", "--exclude-standard").splitlines())
    return sorted(names)


def owned(path, owned_paths):
    c = PurePosixPath(path).parts
    return any(c[: len(PurePosixPath(o).parts)] == PurePosixPath(o).parts for o in owned_paths)


def audit(changed, owned_paths):
    bad = [f for f in changed if not owned(f, owned_paths)]
    return {"accepted": not bad, "unauthorized": bad}"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"dg_2.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() creates two worktrees and edits one, audits committed-only and full change lists, moves a file out of app/, overwrites a shared results file and loses an update in a shared state file.","descKn":"main() ಎರಡು worktrees ರಚಿಸಿ ಒಂದನ್ನು ಸಂಪಾದಿಸಿ, commit ಮಾಡಿದ-ಮಾತ್ರ ಮತ್ತು ಪೂರ್ಣ ಬದಲಾವಣೆ ಪಟ್ಟಿಗಳನ್ನು ಲೆಕ್ಕಪರಿಶೋಧಿಸಿ, app/ ಯಿಂದ ಫೈಲ್ ಸರಿಸಿ, ಹಂಚಿಕೆಯ ಫಲಿತಾಂಶ ಫೈಲ್ ಮೇಲ್ಬರೆದು ಹಂಚಿಕೆಯ ಸ್ಥಿತಿ ಫೈಲ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ನವೀಕರಣ ಕಳೆಯುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        root = Path(d)
        repo = root / "project"
        repo.mkdir()
        git(repo, "init", "-q", "-b", "main")
        for rel, txt in (("app/accounts.py", "v1" + chr(10)), ("app/settings.py", "s1" + chr(10)), ("docs/accounts.md", "d1" + chr(10)), ("app/old.py", "legacy" + chr(10) * 1)):
            (repo / rel).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            (repo / rel).write_text(txt, encoding="utf-8")
        git(repo, "add", "-A")
        git(repo, "commit", "-q", "-m", "base")
        base = git(repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD")

        section("1. Genuinely running: two worktrees give two physical checkouts")
        api_wt, docs_wt = root / "project-api", root / "project-docs"
        git(repo, "worktree", "add", "-q", "-b", "worker/api", str(api_wt), base)
        git(repo, "worktree", "add", "-q", "-b", "worker/docs", str(docs_wt), base)
        (api_wt / "app/accounts.py").write_text("v2 by api worker" + chr(10), encoding="utf-8")
        print("main checkout app/accounts.py :", (repo / "app/accounts.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip())
        print("api worktree app/accounts.py  :", (api_wt / "app/accounts.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip())
        print("docs worktree app/accounts.py :", (docs_wt / "app/accounts.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip())
        print("worktrees registered:", len(git(repo, "worktree", "list").splitlines()))
        print("the api worker's edit exists only in its own folder; the other checkouts still hold v1, which is what stops two workers from editing one working directory at once, and nothing in it limits which files each worker may touch")

        section("2. Genuinely measuring: a committed-only change list misses uncommitted and new files")
        (api_wt / "app/settings.py").write_text("s2 changed without permission" + chr(10), encoding="utf-8")
        (api_wt / "app/extra.py").write_text("brand new" + chr(10), encoding="utf-8")
        git(api_wt, "add", "app/accounts.py")
        git(api_wt, "commit", "-q", "-m", "api work")
        print("committed changes since the base:", committed_changes(api_wt, base))
        print("all changes (committed, uncommitted, untracked):", all_changes(api_wt, base))
        print("audit of the committed list :", audit(committed_changes(api_wt, base), ["app/accounts.py"]))
        print("audit of the full list      :", audit(all_changes(api_wt, base), ["app/accounts.py"]))
        print("the edit to settings.py and the new file were not committed, so the committed-only list passed the audit and the full list rejected two files; the integrator has to look at the whole working tree")

        section("3. Genuinely measuring: a rename out of an owned path")
        git(docs_wt, "mv", "app/old.py", "docs/old.py")
        print("diff with rename detection  :", sorted(git(docs_wt, "diff", "--name-only", "--cached", base).splitlines()))
        print("diff without rename detection:", sorted(git(docs_wt, "diff", "--name-only", "--cached", "--no-renames", base).splitlines()))
        print("audit for a docs-only owner :", audit(sorted(git(docs_wt, "diff", "--name-only", "--cached", "--no-renames", base).splitlines()), ["docs"]))
        print("the move out of app/ into docs/ appears under its new name only when renames are detected, and listing both ends showed that the docs worker also removed a file in app/ it does not own")

        section("4. Genuinely running: separate worktrees still share the output path they are told to write")
        shared = root / "outputs" / "results.json"
        shared.parent.mkdir()
        shared.write_text(json.dumps({"worker": "api", "passed": 12}), encoding="utf-8")
        shared.write_text(json.dumps({"worker": "docs", "passed": 3}), encoding="utf-8")
        print("shared results.json now says:", json.loads(shared.read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
        per = {w: root / "evidence" / w / "results.json" for w in ("api", "docs")}
        for w, p in per.items():
            p.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
            p.write_text(json.dumps({"worker": w}), encoding="utf-8")
        print("per-worker evidence files:", sorted(str(p.relative_to(root)).replace(chr(92), "/") for p in per.values()), "| both survive:", all(p.exists() for p in per.values()))
        print("the second worker overwrote the first worker's evidence in the shared location and nothing noticed; separate worktrees isolated the source files and not the output path, so every worker needs its own evidence directory")

        section("5. Genuinely running: a shared state file loses a worker's update")
        state = root / "shared-state.json"
        state.write_text(json.dumps({"api": "pending", "docs": "pending"}), encoding="utf-8")
        a_view = json.loads(state.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        b_view = json.loads(state.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        a_view["api"] = "done"
        state.write_text(json.dumps(a_view), encoding="utf-8")
        b_view["docs"] = "done"
        state.write_text(json.dumps(b_view), encoding="utf-8")
        print("state after both workers wrote:", json.loads(state.read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
        print("both workers read the file before either wrote, so the api update was lost when the docs worker wrote its older copy back; a database, a port or a cache shared between worktrees fails the same way, and giving each worker its own state avoids it")"}},{"type":"output","data":{"output":"

    return subprocess.run(GIT + list(a), cwd=repo, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()


def committed_changes(repo, base):
    return sorted(git(repo, "diff", "--name-only", f"{base}..HEAD").splitlines())


def all_changes(repo, base):
    names = set(git(repo, "diff", "--name-only", "--no-renames", base).splitlines())
    names |= set(git(repo, "ls-files", "--others", "--exclude-standard").splitlines())
    return sorted(names)


def owned(path, owned_paths):
    c = PurePosixPath(path).parts
    return any(c[: len(PurePosixPath(o).parts)] == PurePosixPath(o).parts for o in owned_paths)


def audit(changed, owned_paths):
    bad = [f for f in changed if not owned(f, owned_paths)]
    return {"accepted": not bad, "unauthorized": bad}"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"dg_2.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() creates two worktrees and edits one, audits committed-only and full change lists, moves a file out of app/, overwrites a shared results file and loses an update in a shared state file.","descKn":"main() ಎರಡು worktrees ರಚಿಸಿ ಒಂದನ್ನು ಸಂಪಾದಿಸಿ, commit ಮಾಡಿದ-ಮಾತ್ರ ಮತ್ತು ಪೂರ್ಣ ಬದಲಾವಣೆ ಪಟ್ಟಿಗಳನ್ನು ಲೆಕ್ಕಪರಿಶೋಧಿಸಿ, app/ ಯಿಂದ ಫೈಲ್ ಸರಿಸಿ, ಹಂಚಿಕೆಯ ಫಲಿತಾಂಶ ಫೈಲ್ ಮೇಲ್ಬರೆದು ಹಂಚಿಕೆಯ ಸ್ಥಿತಿ ಫೈಲ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ನವೀಕರಣ ಕಳೆಯುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():

            (repo / rel).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            (repo / rel).write_text(txt, encoding="utf-8")
        git(repo, "add", "-A")
        git(repo, "commit", "-q", "-m", "base")
        base = git(repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD")

        section("1. Genuinely running: two worktrees give two physical checkouts")
        api_wt, docs_wt = root / "project-api", root / "project-docs"
        git(repo, "worktree", "add", "-q", "-b", "worker/api", str(api_wt), base)
        git(repo, "worktree", "add", "-q", "-b", "worker/docs", str(docs_wt), base)
        (api_wt / "app/accounts.py").write_text("v2 by api worker" + chr(10), encoding="utf-8")
        print("main checkout app/accounts.py :", (repo / "app/accounts.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip())
        print("api worktree app/accounts.py  :", (api_wt / "app/accounts.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip())
        print("docs worktree app/accounts.py :", (docs_wt / "app/accounts.py").read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip())
        print("worktrees registered:", len(git(repo, "worktree", "list").splitlines()))
        print("the api worker's edit exists only in its own folder; the other checkouts still hold v1, which is what stops two workers from editing one working directory at once, and nothing in it limits which files each worker may touch")

        section("2. Genuinely measuring: a committed-only change list misses uncommitted and new files")
        (api_wt / "app/settings.py").write_text("s2 changed without permission" + chr(10), encoding="utf-8")
        (api_wt / "app/extra.py").write_text("brand new" + chr(10), encoding="utf-8")
        git(api_wt, "add", "app/accounts.py")
        git(api_wt, "commit", "-q", "-m", "api work")
        print("committed changes since the base:", committed_changes(api_wt, base))
        print("all changes (committed, uncommitted, untracked):", all_changes(api_wt, base))
        print("audit of the committed list :", audit(committed_changes(api_wt, base), ["app/accounts.py"]))
        print("audit of the full list      :", audit(all_changes(api_wt, base), ["app/accounts.py"]))
        print("the edit to settings.py and the new file were not committed, so the committed-only list passed the audit and the full list rejected two files; the integrator has to look at the whole working tree")

        section("3. Genuinely measuring: a rename out of an owned path")
        git(docs_wt, "mv", "app/old.py", "docs/old.py")
        print("diff with rename detection  :", sorted(git(docs_wt, "diff", "--name-only", "--cached", base).splitlines()))
        print("diff without rename detection:", sorted(git(docs_wt, "diff", "--name-only", "--cached", "--no-renames", base).splitlines()))
        print("audit for a docs-only owner :", audit(sorted(git(docs_wt, "diff", "--name-only", "--cached", "--no-renames", base).splitlines()), ["docs"]))
        print("the move out of app/ into docs/ appears under its new name only when renames are detected, and listing both ends showed that the docs worker also removed a file in app/ it does not own")

ಬಂಧಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.","code":"def git(repo, *a, check=True):
    p = subprocess.run(GIT + list(a), cwd=repo, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if check and p.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(p.stderr.strip() or p.stdout.strip())
    return p


def commit_file(repo, rel, text, msg):
    (Path(repo) / rel).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (Path(repo) / rel).write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    git(repo, "add", "-A")
    git(repo, "commit", "-q", "-m", msg)


def merge_in_order(repo, branches):
    merged = []
    if git(repo, "status", "--porcelain").stdout.strip():
        return merged, "integration checkout is not clean"
    for b in branches:
        p = git(repo, "merge", "--no-ff", "-q", "-m", f"merge {b}", b, check=False)
        if p.returncode != 0:
            git(repo, "merge", "--abort", check=False)
            return merged, f"conflict while merging {b}; merge aborted"
        merged.append(b)
    return merged, "all merged"


def gate(scope_ok, proof_ok, review_ok, tests_ok, approval_required, approved):
    reasons = [n for n, v in (("scope", scope_ok), ("proof", proof_ok), ("review", review_ok), ("integration tests", tests_ok)) if not v]
    if approval_required and not approved:
        reasons.append("human approval missing")
    return ("PASS" if not reasons else "BLOCK"), reasons


@dataclass
class ApprovalFlag:
    action: str
    approved: bool = False


def sign(action, approver):
    return hmac.new(KEY, f"{action}|{approver}".encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()


def verify_approval(record, action):
    if record.get("action") != action:
        return False
    return hmac.compare_digest(sign(record["action"], record["approver"]), record.get("sig", ""))"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"dg_3.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() merges two clean branches, compares code and docs for a semantic conflict, merges two conflicting branches, runs the gate four ways and tries a boolean flag against a signed record.","descKn":"main() ಎರಡು ಸ್ವಚ್ಛ branches ವಿಲೀನಿಸಿ, ಅರ್ಥಗತ ಸಂಘರ್ಷಕ್ಕೆ ಕೋಡ್ ಮತ್ತು docs ಹೋಲಿಸಿ, ಎರಡು ಸಂಘರ್ಷಿಸುವ branches ವಿಲೀನಿಸಿ, gate ನಾಲ್ಕು ರೀತಿ ಓಡಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು boolean ಧ್ವಜವನ್ನು ಸಹಿ ದಾಖಲೆಗೆ ವಿರುದ್ಧ ಪ್ರಯತ್ನಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
