ಬಂಧಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.","code":"def git(repo, *a, check=True):
    p = subprocess.run(GIT + list(a), cwd=repo, capture_output=True, text=True)
    if check and p.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(p.stderr.strip() or p.stdout.strip())
    return p


def commit_file(repo, rel, text, msg):
    (Path(repo) / rel).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (Path(repo) / rel).write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    git(repo, "add", "-A")
    git(repo, "commit", "-q", "-m", msg)


def merge_in_order(repo, branches):
    merged = []
    if git(repo, "status", "--porcelain").stdout.strip():
        return merged, "integration checkout is not clean"
    for b in branches:
        p = git(repo, "merge", "--no-ff", "-q", "-m", f"merge {b}", b, check=False)
        if p.returncode != 0:
            git(repo, "merge", "--abort", check=False)
            return merged, f"conflict while merging {b}; merge aborted"
        merged.append(b)
    return merged, "all merged"


def gate(scope_ok, proof_ok, review_ok, tests_ok, approval_required, approved):
    reasons = [n for n, v in (("scope", scope_ok), ("proof", proof_ok), ("review", review_ok), ("integration tests", tests_ok)) if not v]
    if approval_required and not approved:
        reasons.append("human approval missing")
    return ("PASS" if not reasons else "BLOCK"), reasons


@dataclass
class ApprovalFlag:
    action: str
    approved: bool = False


def sign(action, approver):
    return hmac.new(KEY, f"{action}|{approver}".encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()


def verify_approval(record, action):
    if record.get("action") != action:
        return False
    return hmac.compare_digest(sign(record["action"], record["approver"]), record.get("sig", ""))"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"dg_3.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() merges two clean branches, compares code and docs for a semantic conflict, merges two conflicting branches, runs the gate four ways and tries a boolean flag against a signed record.","descKn":"main() ಎರಡು ಸ್ವಚ್ಛ branches ವಿಲೀನಿಸಿ, ಅರ್ಥಗತ ಸಂಘರ್ಷಕ್ಕೆ ಕೋಡ್ ಮತ್ತು docs ಹೋಲಿಸಿ, ಎರಡು ಸಂಘರ್ಷಿಸುವ branches ವಿಲೀನಿಸಿ, gate ನಾಲ್ಕು ರೀತಿ ಓಡಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು boolean ಧ್ವಜವನ್ನು ಸಹಿ ದಾಖಲೆಗೆ ವಿರುದ್ಧ ಪ್ರಯತ್ನಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():

ಕಾರಣ ಮತ್ತು ಶುದ್ಧ target ಅನ್ನು ಮಾತ್ರ hash ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def normalize_text(text):
    return " ".join(str(text).lower().replace("’", "'").split()).strip(" .!")


def resolve_cause(message):
    m = normalize_text(message)
    for cause, (layer, phrases) in CAUSES.items():
        if any(p in m for p in phrases):
            return cause, layer
    return "unclassified", "human_decision"


def validate(c):
    for name in ("event_id", "message", "symptom", "target"):
        if not isinstance(getattr(c, name), str) or not getattr(c, name).strip():
            raise ValueError(f"Expected a non-empty {name}")
    return c


def classify(c):
    validate(c)
    c.cause, c.layer = resolve_cause(c.message)
    return c


def fingerprint(cause, target, include_time=None):
    payload = {"cause": cause, "target": target.replace(chr(92), "/").strip("/")}
    if include_time is not None:
        payload["time"] = include_time
    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()[:12]


def naive_fingerprint(message):
    return hashlib.sha256(message.encode()).hexdigest()[:12]"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"fr_1.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() resolves one correction, tries six wordings, compares what goes into a fingerprint, counts recurrences with and without the target and rejects three malformed records.","descKn":"main() ಒಂದು ತಿದ್ದುಪಡಿ ಪರಿಹರಿಸಿ, ಆರು ಪದಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳನ್ನು ಪ್ರಯತ್ನಿಸಿ, fingerprint ನಲ್ಲಿ ಏನು ಹೋಗುತ್ತದೆ ಹೋಲಿಸಿ, target ಸಹಿತ ಮತ್ತು ರಹಿತ ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ ಎಣಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ಮೂರು ದೋಷಪೂರ್ಣ ದಾಖಲೆಗಳನ್ನು ತಿರಸ್ಕರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    section("1. Genuinely running: a symptom is not a cause")
    c = classify(Correction("e1", "Do not edit README.md. Only change files related to registration validation.", "agent edited README.md", "README.md"))
    print("symptom:", c.symptom, "| resolved cause:", c.cause, "| earliest layer:", c.layer)
    print("the correction says what to avoid in one conversation; the cause names the missing control (an executable scope), and the layer says where prevention belongs")

    section("2. Genuinely measuring: differently worded corrections reach the same cause")
    msgs = [("Do not modify README.md.", "README.md"), ("Please do NOT edit   README.md!", "README.md"), ("Don’t touch README.md", "README.md"),
            ("The response is missing a required field: user_id", "api/response.py"), ("The result is wrong; the total is off by one", "app/totals.py"), ("Which behaviour do we want for expired carts?", "app/cart.py")]
    for i, (m, t) in enumerate(msgs):
        k = classify(Correction(f"m{i}", m, "s", t))
        print(f"{m!r:62} -> {k.cause:20} {k.layer:16} {fingerprint(k.cause, k.target)}")
    print("the first two wordings matched a phrase and shared a fingerprint, while the third (\"Don't touch\") matched no phrase and fell to unclassified; a phrase table is only as good as its phrases, and unclassified items go to a human instead of being guessed")

    section("3. Genuinely measuring: what goes into a fingerprint")
    a = fingerprint("off_scope_edit", "README.md")
    print("same cause and target, different message text :", a == fingerprint("off_scope_edit", "README.md"))
    print("backslash path and leading slash               :", a == fingerprint("off_scope_edit", chr(92) + "README.md"))
    print("different target (LICENSE)                     :", a == fingerprint("off_scope_edit", "LICENSE"))
    print("different cause on the same target             :", a == fingerprint("missing_field", "README.md"))
    print("timestamp included (two runs a second apart)   :", fingerprint("off_scope_edit", "README.md", "10:00:01") == fingerprint("off_scope_edit", "README.md", "10:00:02"))

ಕಾರಣ ಮತ್ತು ಶುದ್ಧ target ಅನ್ನು ಮಾತ್ರ hash ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def normalize_text(text):
    return " ".join(str(text).lower().replace("’", "'").split()).strip(" .!")


def resolve_cause(message):
    m = normalize_text(message)
    for cause, (layer, phrases) in CAUSES.items():
        if any(p in m for p in phrases):
            return cause, layer
    return "unclassified", "human_decision"


def validate(c):
    for name in ("event_id", "message", "symptom", "target"):
        if not isinstance(getattr(c, name), str) or not getattr(c, name).strip():
            raise ValueError(f"Expected a non-empty {name}")
    return c


def classify(c):
    validate(c)
    c.cause, c.layer = resolve_cause(c.message)
    return c


def fingerprint(cause, target, include_time=None):
    payload = {"cause": cause, "target": target.replace(chr(92), "/").strip("/")}
    if include_time is not None:
        payload["time"] = include_time
    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()[:12]


def naive_fingerprint(message):
    return hashlib.sha256(message.encode()).hexdigest()[:12]"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"fr_1.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() resolves one correction, tries six wordings, compares what goes into a fingerprint, counts recurrences with and without the target and rejects three malformed records.","descKn":"main() ಒಂದು ತಿದ್ದುಪಡಿ ಪರಿಹರಿಸಿ, ಆರು ಪದಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳನ್ನು ಪ್ರಯತ್ನಿಸಿ, fingerprint ನಲ್ಲಿ ಏನು ಹೋಗುತ್ತದೆ ಹೋಲಿಸಿ, target ಸಹಿತ ಮತ್ತು ರಹಿತ ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ ಎಣಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ಮೂರು ದೋಷಪೂರ್ಣ ದಾಖಲೆಗಳನ್ನು ತಿರಸ್ಕರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    section("1. Genuinely running: a symptom is not a cause")
    c = classify(Correction("e1", "Do not edit README.md. Only change files related to registration validation.", "agent edited README.md", "README.md"))
    print("symptom:", c.symptom, "| resolved cause:", c.cause, "| earliest layer:", c.layer)
    print("the correction says what to avoid in one conversation; the cause names the missing control (an executable scope), and the layer says where prevention belongs")

    section("2. Genuinely measuring: differently worded corrections reach the same cause")
    msgs = [("Do not modify README.md.", "README.md"), ("Please do NOT edit   README.md!", "README.md"), ("Don’t touch README.md", "README.md"),
            ("The response is missing a required field: user_id", "api/response.py"), ("The result is wrong; the total is off by one", "app/totals.py"), ("Which behaviour do we want for expired carts?", "app/cart.py")]
    for i, (m, t) in enumerate(msgs):
        k = classify(Correction(f"m{i}", m, "s", t))
        print(f"{m!r:62} -> {k.cause:20} {k.layer:16} {fingerprint(k.cause, k.target)}")
    print("the first two wordings matched a phrase and shared a fingerprint, while the third (\"Don't touch\") matched no phrase and fell to unclassified; a phrase table is only as good as its phrases, and unclassified items go to a human instead of being guessed")

    section("3. Genuinely measuring: what goes into a fingerprint")
    a = fingerprint("off_scope_edit", "README.md")
    print("same cause and target, different message text :", a == fingerprint("off_scope_edit", "README.md"))
    print("backslash path and leading slash               :", a == fingerprint("off_scope_edit", chr(92) + "README.md"))
    print("different target (LICENSE)                     :", a == fingerprint("off_scope_edit", "LICENSE"))
    print("different cause on the same target             :", a == fingerprint("missing_field", "README.md"))
    print("timestamp included (two runs a second apart)   :", fingerprint("off_scope_edit", "README.md", "10:00:01") == fingerprint("off_scope_edit", "README.md", "10:00:02"))
    print("hash of the raw message for two wordings       :", naive_fingerprint("Do not modify README.md.") == naive_fingerprint("Please do NOT edit README.md!"))
    print("the fingerprint covers the cause and the target only; adding a timestamp or hashing the raw wording made equal failures look different, and dropping the target would have merged README.md with LICENSE")

    section("4. Genuinely running: recurrence counting with and without false merges")
    log = [("README.md", "Do not edit README.md"), ("README.md", "Do not modify README.md"), ("LICENSE", "Do not edit LICENSE"), ("api/response.py", "The response is missing a required field"), ("README.md", "Do not change files outside the task")]
    counts, ids = {}, {}
    for i, (t, m) in enumerate(log):
        k = classify(Correction(f"r{i}", m, "s", t))
        fp = fingerprint(k.cause, k.target)
        counts[fp] = counts.get(fp, 0) + 1
        ids[fp] = (k.cause, k.target)
    for fp, n in sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1]):
        print(f"{fp} {ids[fp][0]:16} {ids[fp][1]:16} recurrence={n}")
    cause_only = {}
    for t, m in log:
        k = classify(Correction("x", m, "s", t))
        cause_only[k.cause] = cause_only.get(k.cause, 0) + 1
    print("if the target is ignored, off_scope_edit would count", cause_only.get("off_scope_edit"), "events as one problem")
    print("with the target in the fingerprint README.md has 3 recurrences and LICENSE has 1, so a control is justified for README.md and LICENSE is not lumped in; a recurrence count only means something if equal causes are merged and unequal ones are not")

    section("5. Genuinely running: malformed corrections are rejected before they become records")
    for label, kw in (("empty message", dict(message="  ")), ("missing target", dict(target="")), ("non-string symptom", dict(symptom=None))):
        base = dict(event_id="b1", message="Do not edit README.md", symptom="s", target="README.md")
        base.update(kw)
        try:
            classify(Correction(**base))
            print(f"{label:20} accepted")
        except ValueError as e:
            print(f"{label:20} rejected: {e}")
    print("a record without a message or a target cannot be fingerprinted, so the ingest step refuses it instead of storing something that will never match")"}},{"type":"output","data":{"output":"

    allowed_parts = [PurePosixPath(a.replace(chr(92), "/")).parts for a in allowed]
    bad = [c for c in changed if not any(PurePosixPath(c.replace(chr(92), "/")).parts[: len(p)] == p for p in allowed_parts)]
    return {"ok": not bad, "violations": bad}


def check_response(resp):
    missing = [k for k in ("status", "user_id") if not isinstance(resp, dict) or k not in resp]
    return {"ok": not missing, "missing": missing}


def run_unittest(code, test):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        Path(d, "totals.py").write_text(code, encoding="utf-8")
        Path(d, "test_totals.py").write_text(test, encoding="utf-8")
        p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-B", "-m", "unittest", "-q", "test_totals"], cwd=d, capture_output=True, text=True)
        return p.returncode, (p.stderr.strip().splitlines() or [""])[-1]


BUGGY = "def total(items):" + chr(10) + "    return sum(items) - 1" + chr(10)
FIXED = "def total(items):" + chr(10) + "    return sum(items)" + chr(10)
TEST = textwrap.dedent("""
    import unittest
    from totals import total
    class T(unittest.TestCase):
        def test_total(self):
            self.assertEqual(total([1, 2, 3]), 6)
    """)
TEST_NO_ASSERT = textwrap.dedent("""
    import unittest
    from totals import total
    class T(unittest.TestCase):
        def test_total(self):
            total([1, 2, 3])
    """)
TEST_NOT_COLLECTED = textwrap.dedent("""
    import unittest
    from totals import total
    class T(unittest.TestCase):
        def check_total(self):
            self.assertEqual(total([1, 2, 3]), 6)
    """)


def verify_control(control_fails_on_bad, control_passes_on_good):
    return "verified" if control_fails_on_bad and control_passes_on_good else "unverified"


class Ingest:
    def __init__(self):
        self.seen, self.records = set(), []

    def add(self, event):
        if event["event_id"] in self.seen:
            return False
        self.seen.add(event["event_id"])
        self.records.append(event)
        return True


def validate_report(text):
    data = json.loads(text)
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or not isinstance(data.get("corrections"), list):
        raise ValueError("Expected a corrections list")
    for i, c in enumerate(data["corrections"]):
        for k in ("fingerprint", "cause", "layer", "owner", "review_by", "verified"):
            if k not in c:
                raise ValueError(f"corrections[{i}] is missing {k}")
    return data"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"fr_2.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() runs the two checks, runs the regression test on both code versions, runs the two fake controls, ingests a duplicate event and validates four reports.","descKn":"main() ಎರಡು ಪರಿಶೀಲನೆ ಓಡಿಸಿ, ಎರಡೂ ಕೋಡ್ ಆವೃತ್ತಿಗಳ ಮೇಲೆ regression test ಓಡಿಸಿ, ಎರಡು ನಕಲಿ ನಿಯಂತ್ರಣ ಓಡಿಸಿ, ನಕಲು event ಸೇರಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ನಾಲ್ಕು ವರದಿ ಮಾನ್ಯಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    section("1. Genuinely running: a scope control and a schema control")
    print("changed README.md only        :", check_scope(["README.md"], ["app/registration"]))
    print("changed registration file     :", check_scope(["app/registration/validate.py"], ["app/registration"]))
    print("app/registration_old.py       :", check_scope(["app/registration_old.py"], ["app/registration"]))
    print("response with user_id         :", check_response({"status": "success", "user_id": 42}))
    print("response without user_id      :", check_response({"status": "success"}))
    print("the controls turned two conversational corrections into checks that run on the output, and the third line shows component matching keeping a sibling directory outside the allowed path")

    section("2. Genuinely running: a regression test is run against bad and good code")
    r_bad, last_bad = run_unittest(BUGGY, TEST)
    r_good, last_good = run_unittest(FIXED, TEST)
    print("test against buggy code exit:", r_bad, "|", last_bad)
    print("test against fixed code exit:", r_good, "|", last_good)
    print("status:", verify_control(r_bad == 1, r_good == 0))
    print("a control counts as verified here because it failed on the code that had the defect and passed on the corrected code; passing alone says nothing about whether it can detect the failure")

    section("3. Genuinely running: controls that look like protection and are not")
    r1, _ = run_unittest(BUGGY, TEST_NO_ASSERT)
    r2, l2 = run_unittest(BUGGY, TEST_NOT_COLLECTED)
    print("test with no assertion against buggy code exit :", r1, "->", verify_control(r1 == 1, True))
    print("test never collected against buggy code exit   :", r2, "|", l2, "->", verify_control(r2 == 1, True))
    print("the first exited 0 on code that was wrong because it never compared anything; the second was not named test_ so no test ran and the runner exited 5, which is not the exit 1 of a real test failure, so only an exit of 1 counts as the control catching the defect; running a control against the known-bad case is what exposes both")

    section("4. Genuinely running: duplicate events are ingested once")
    ing = Ingest()
    evs = [{"event_id": "a1", "cause": "off_scope_edit"}, {"event_id": "a1", "cause": "off_scope_edit"}, {"event_id": "a2", "cause": "off_scope_edit"}]
    print("accepted:", [ing.add(e) for e in evs], "| stored records:", len(ing.records))
    print("without the event id check the same webhook delivered twice would have counted as two recurrences and promoted a control early; a retry is not a new failure")

    section("5. Genuinely running: a report is validated when it is read")
    good = json.dumps({"corrections": [{"fingerprint": "1ad37322ca49", "cause": "off_scope_edit", "layer": "scope_policy", "owner": "platform", "review_by": "2027-02-01", "verified": True}]})
    no_owner = json.dumps({"corrections": [{"fingerprint": "1ad37322ca49", "cause": "off_scope_edit", "layer": "scope_policy", "review_by": "2027-02-01", "verified": True}]})
    for label, text in (("complete record", good), ("record without owner", no_owner), ("not a list", json.dumps({"corrections": {}})), ("not json", "{")):

            print(f"{label:22} accepted")

def verify_control(control_fails_on_bad, control_passes_on_good):
    return "verified" if control_fails_on_bad and control_passes_on_good else "unverified"


class Ingest:
    def __init__(self):
        self.seen, self.records = set(), []

    def add(self, event):
        if event["event_id"] in self.seen:
            return False
        self.seen.add(event["event_id"])
        self.records.append(event)
        return True


def validate_report(text):
    data = json.loads(text)
    if not isinstance(data, dict) or not isinstance(data.get("corrections"), list):
        raise ValueError("Expected a corrections list")
    for i, c in enumerate(data["corrections"]):
        for k in ("fingerprint", "cause", "layer", "owner", "review_by", "verified"):
            if k not in c:

    def __init__(self, cid, cause, owner, review_by):
        self.cid, self.cause, self.owner, self.review_by, self.state, self.history = cid, cause, owner, review_by, "proposed", ["proposed"]

    def move(self, new, evidence=None):
        if new not in ALLOWED[self.state]:
            raise ValueError(f"Illegal transition {self.state} -> {new}")
        if new == "active" and not evidence:
            raise ValueError("Activation needs verification evidence")
        self.state = new
        self.history.append(new)


def overdue(controls, today):
    return sorted(c.cid for c in controls if c.state in ("active", "under_review") and date.fromisoformat(c.review_by) < today)


def effectiveness(events, control_start):
    before = [e for e in events if e["day"] < control_start]
    after = [e for e in events if e["day"] >= control_start]
    return len(before), len(after)


def can_retire(c, recent_events, replacement_active, today):
    reasons = []
    if recent_events:
        reasons.append("failure still occurring")
    if not replacement_active:
        reasons.append("no replacement protects the same cause")
    return (not reasons), reasons


def sign_change(cid, new_text, approver):
    return hmac.new(KEY, f"{cid}|{hashlib.sha256(new_text.encode()).hexdigest()}|{approver}".encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()


def apply_change(registry, cid, new_text, approver, sig):
    if not hmac.compare_digest(sign_change(cid, new_text, approver), sig):
        return False
    registry[cid] = new_text
    return True"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"fr_3.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() walks transitions, registers three controls and queries overdue review, compares an invented log at three start days, evaluates three retirement cases and tries three rule edits.","descKn":"main() ಪರಿವರ್ತನೆಗಳ ಮೇಲೆ ನಡೆದು, ಮೂರು ನಿಯಂತ್ರಣ ನೋಂದಾಯಿಸಿ ಮೀರಿದ ವಿಮರ್ಶೆ ಪ್ರಶ್ನಿಸಿ, ಮೂರು ಆರಂಭ ದಿನಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಕಲ್ಪಿತ ದಾಖಲೆ ಹೋಲಿಸಿ, ಮೂರು ನಿವೃತ್ತಿ ಸಂದರ್ಭ ಮೌಲ್ಯಮಾಪನ ಮಾಡಿ ಮತ್ತು ಮೂರು ನಿಯಮ ಸಂಪಾದನೆ ಪ್ರಯತ್ನಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():

class OutcomeFrame:
    user: str
    situation: str
    current_behavior: str
    desired_outcome: str
    constraints: tuple
    non_goals: tuple


def validate_structure(f):
    errors = []
    for name in ("user", "situation", "current_behavior", "desired_outcome"):
        if not str(getattr(f, name)).strip():
            errors.append(f"{name} is required")
    for name in ("constraints", "non_goals"):
        if not getattr(f, name):
            errors.append(f"{name} needs at least one entry")
    return errors


def leaks_naive(text):
    t = text.lower()
    return [s for s in SOLUTION_TERMS if s in t]


def leaks_words(text):
    t = text.lower()
    return [s for s in SOLUTION_TERMS if re.search(r"\b" + re.escape(s) + r"\b", t)]


def validate_leakage(f):
    return {"desired_outcome": leaks_words(f.desired_outcome), "current_behavior": leaks_words(f.current_behavior)}"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"oc_1.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() compares two outputs with two outcomes, validates a good and an empty frame, compares substring and word matching, names PostgreSQL as a constraint and tries wording that hides a solution.","descKn":"main() ಎರಡು ಔಟ್‌ಪುಟ್ ಮತ್ತು ಎರಡು ಫಲಿತಾಂಶ ಹೋಲಿಸಿ, ಒಳ್ಳೆಯ ಮತ್ತು ಖಾಲಿ ಚೌಕಟ್ಟು ಮಾನ್ಯಗೊಳಿಸಿ, ಉಪಸ್ಟ್ರಿಂಗ್ ಮತ್ತು ಪದ ಹೊಂದಾಣಿಕೆ ಹೋಲಿಸಿ, PostgreSQL ಅನ್ನು ನಿರ್ಬಂಧವಾಗಿ ಹೆಸರಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ಪರಿಹಾರ ಮರೆಮಾಡುವ ಪದಗಳನ್ನು ಪ್ರಯತ್ನಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    section("1. Genuinely running: output versus outcome")
    for out, outcome in (("Build an AI incident assistant", "Identify the failing service and a safe next action within two minutes"),
                         ("Add an automated code reviewer", "High-severity defects are found before merge, with evidence, without write permission")):
        print(f"output : {out}\noutcome: {outcome}\n  solution terms in the output : {leaks_words(out)}\n  solution terms in the outcome: {leaks_words(outcome)}")
    print("the output names a thing to build and the outcome names a change somebody should see; the word list flagged ai and assistant in the first output and nothing in either outcome, but it also missed the second output because reviewer is not on the list, so the list is a starting point and section 5 shows the same gap again")

    section("2. Genuinely running: a complete frame and structural validation")
    print("good frame errors:", validate_structure(GOOD))
    empty = OutcomeFrame("", "a production alert has arrived", "slow", " ", (), ())
    print("incomplete frame errors:", validate_structure(empty))
    print("six fields are required before a frame is accepted, and the two list fields need at least one entry; the check is structural, so it says the fields exist and nothing about whether they are good")

    section("3. Genuinely measuring: solution leakage with a substring check and a word check")
    leaky = OutcomeFrame("on-call engineer", "an alert arrives", "manual", "Build an AI-powered incident dashboard", ("read-only",), ("remediation",))
    print("leaky desired_outcome (words):", validate_leakage(leaky))
    for text in ("Engineers maintain a balanced email rotation", "Analysts retrain the model of demand each week", "Engineers can paraphrase the failing service quickly"):
        print(f"{text[:52]:54} substring={leaks_naive(text)} words={leaks_words(text)}")
    print("the substring check reported ai inside maintain, balanced, email and paraphrase, which are not solutions, while the word-boundary check did not; the second row shows a limit of the word check too, since model there is a legitimate noun and is still flagged, so a flag is a prompt for a person to look and not a verdict")

    section("4. Genuinely running: a technology name that is a real constraint")
    with_constraint = OutcomeFrame("billing analyst", "month-end close", "exports are copied by hand", "reconcile the ledger export within one hour", ("must use the existing PostgreSQL database and its audit table", "read-only"), ("new reports",))
    print("leakage in desired outcome:", validate_leakage(with_constraint)["desired_outcome"], "| technology named in constraints:", [c for c in with_constraint.constraints if "postgresql" in c.lower()])
    print("naming PostgreSQL as a constraint is legitimate because the organisation really is bound to it, and it did not trip the check because only the desired outcome and the current behaviour are scanned; where the technology appears matters more than that it appears")

    section("5. Genuinely measuring: wording that hides a solution from the word list")
    for text in ("Engineers get a smart helper that watches the alerts", "Engineers get a conversational tool that answers on-call questions", "Identify the failing service within two minutes"):
        print(f"{text[:60]:62} flagged={leaks_words(text)}")
    print("the first two phrases still describe a thing to build and the list did not flag them, while the third is a real outcome; this is a false negative, and the word list cannot be made complete, so the review step has to ask what change a user would see and not just what words are present")"}},{"type":"output","data":{"output":"

ಮರಳಿಸುತ್ತದೆ, gate ಪ್ರತಿ ಕಾರಣ ಸಂಗ್ರಹಿಸುತ್ತದೆ ಮತ್ತು may_revise_target ಸಾಕ್ಷ್ಯ ಮತ್ತು ಅನುಮೋದಕ ಬಯಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def make_evidence(metric, baseline, target, sample_min):
    return {"metric": metric, "baseline": baseline, "target": target, "sample_min": sample_min}


def measure(samples, ev):
    if len(samples) < ev["sample_min"]:
        return {"status": "insufficient_data", "n": len(samples)}
    med = statistics.median(samples)
    return {"status": "met" if med <= ev["target"] else "not_met", "n": len(samples), "median": med, "baseline": ev["baseline"]}


def gate(tests_pass, constraints_ok, outcome):
    reasons = []
    if not tests_pass:
        reasons.append("tests failing")
    if not constraints_ok:
        reasons.append("constraint violated")
    if outcome["status"] == "insufficient_data":
        reasons.append("outcome not measured")
    elif outcome["status"] == "not_met":
        reasons.append("outcome target not met")
    return ("PASS" if not reasons else "BLOCK"), reasons


def review(builder, reviewer):
    return "independent" if builder != reviewer else "not independent"


def approval_needed(action):
    return action in {"change_alert_routing", "enable_auto_remediation", "write_production_data"}


def may_revise_target(old_target, new_target, evidence_note, approver):
    if not evidence_note or not approver:
        return False, "a revision needs evidence and an approver"
    if new_target > old_target and "baseline" not in evidence_note:
        return False, "loosening the target must cite the baseline"
    return True, "revision recorded""}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"oc_3.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() fixes evidence, gates a build that missed the target and one that met it, blocks on too few samples, mixes constraint and test failures, then tries review, approval and revision rules.","descKn":"main() ಸಾಕ್ಷ್ಯ ನಿಗದಿಪಡಿಸಿ, ಗುರಿ ತಪ್ಪಿದ ಮತ್ತು ಸಾಧಿಸಿದ ನಿರ್ಮಾಣವನ್ನು gate ಮಾಡಿ, ಕಡಿಮೆ ಮಾದರಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ತಡೆದು, ನಿರ್ಬಂಧ ಮತ್ತು ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ ವೈಫಲ್ಯ ಮಿಶ್ರಣ ಮಾಡಿ, ನಂತರ ವಿಮರ್ಶೆ, ಅನುಮೋದನೆ ಮತ್ತು ಪರಿಷ್ಕರಣೆ ನಿಯಮ ಪ್ರಯತ್ನಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    ev = make_evidence("minutes to identify the failing service", baseline=12, target=2, sample_min=8)
    section("1. Genuinely running: evidence is defined before building")
    print("evidence:", ev)
    print("the metric, the baseline, the target and the minimum sample size were written down before any implementation existed, so the result cannot be argued into success afterwards; these numbers are invented for the lab")

    section("2. Genuinely computing: tests passing is not the outcome (ILLUSTRATIVE samples, minutes)")
    after_build = [9, 10, 8, 9, 11, 9, 10, 8, 9]
    after_fix = [2, 1.5, 3, 1.8, 2, 1.2, 2.5, 1.9, 1.6]
    for label, s, t in (("assistant built, tests pass", after_build, True), ("after fixing metadata labels", after_fix, True)):
        out = measure(s, ev)
        print(f"{label:30} measure={out} gate={gate(t, True, out)}")
    print("the first build passed every test and the gate still blocked because the median of nine minutes missed the two-minute target, while the second sample met it; the same tests were green both times, so they could not tell the two apart")

    section("3. Genuinely running: a missing measurement blocks")
    out = measure([2, 2, 3], ev)
    print("three samples:", out, "->", gate(True, True, out))
    print("a gate that treats no data as success would pass a change nobody measured, so too few samples is its own reason to block")

    section("4. Genuinely running: constraints and the gate")
    out = measure(after_fix, ev)
    print("outcome met, constraint violated:", gate(True, False, out))
    print("outcome met, tests failing      :", gate(False, True, out))
    print("everything holds                :", gate(True, True, out))
    print("a speed gain bought by breaking the read-only rule still blocks, because the outcome is one condition among several")

    section("5. Genuinely running: independent review, approval and target revision")
    print("builder and reviewer the same agent :", review("agent-a", "agent-a"))
    print("builder and reviewer different       :", review("agent-a", "agent-b"))
    for a in ("read_logs", "enable_auto_remediation"):
        print(f"approval needed for {a:26}: {approval_needed(a)}")
    print("revise target without evidence      :", may_revise_target(2, 4, "", "owner"))
    print("loosen target without citing baseline:", may_revise_target(2, 4, "the team prefers it", "owner"))
    print("loosen target citing baseline        :", may_revise_target(2, 4, "baseline measured at 12 minutes; 2 not reachable with current logs", "owner"))
    print("the builder cannot be its own independent reviewer, risky actions need a human, and a target moves only with evidence and an approver; here 'cites the baseline' is a keyword check on the note, which a careless note could satisfy")"}},{"type":"output","data":{"output":"

    return {"metric": metric, "baseline": baseline, "target": target, "sample_min": sample_min}


def measure(samples, ev):
    if len(samples) < ev["sample_min"]:
        return {"status": "insufficient_data", "n": len(samples)}
    med = statistics.median(samples)
    return {"status": "met" if med <= ev["target"] else "not_met", "n": len(samples), "median": med, "baseline": ev["baseline"]}


def gate(tests_pass, constraints_ok, outcome):
    reasons = []
    if not tests_pass:
        reasons.append("tests failing")
    if not constraints_ok:
        reasons.append("constraint violated")
    if outcome["status"] == "insufficient_data":
        reasons.append("outcome not measured")
    elif outcome["status"] == "not_met":
        reasons.append("outcome target not met")
    return ("PASS" if not reasons else "BLOCK"), reasons


def review(builder, reviewer):
    return "independent" if builder != reviewer else "not independent"


def approval_needed(action):
    return action in {"change_alert_routing", "enable_auto_remediation", "write_production_data"}


def may_revise_target(old_target, new_target, evidence_note, approver):
    if not evidence_note or not approver:
        return False, "a revision needs evidence and an approver"
    if new_target > old_target and "baseline" not in evidence_note:
        return False, "loosening the target must cite the baseline"
    return True, "revision recorded""}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"oc_3.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() fixes evidence, gates a build that missed the target and one that met it, blocks on too few samples, mixes constraint and test failures, then tries review, approval and revision rules.","descKn":"main() ಸಾಕ್ಷ್ಯ ನಿಗದಿಪಡಿಸಿ, ಗುರಿ ತಪ್ಪಿದ ಮತ್ತು ಸಾಧಿಸಿದ ನಿರ್ಮಾಣವನ್ನು gate ಮಾಡಿ, ಕಡಿಮೆ ಮಾದರಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ತಡೆದು, ನಿರ್ಬಂಧ ಮತ್ತು ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆ ವೈಫಲ್ಯ ಮಿಶ್ರಣ ಮಾಡಿ, ನಂತರ ವಿಮರ್ಶೆ, ಅನುಮೋದನೆ ಮತ್ತು ಪರಿಷ್ಕರಣೆ ನಿಯಮ ಪ್ರಯತ್ನಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    ev = make_evidence("minutes to identify the failing service", baseline=12, target=2, sample_min=8)
    section("1. Genuinely running: evidence is defined before building")
    print("evidence:", ev)
    print("the metric, the baseline, the target and the minimum sample size were written down before any implementation existed, so the result cannot be argued into success afterwards; these numbers are invented for the lab")

    section("2. Genuinely computing: tests passing is not the outcome (ILLUSTRATIVE samples, minutes)")
    after_build = [9, 10, 8, 9, 11, 9, 10, 8, 9]
    after_fix = [2, 1.5, 3, 1.8, 2, 1.2, 2.5, 1.9, 1.6]
    for label, s, t in (("assistant built, tests pass", after_build, True), ("after fixing metadata labels", after_fix, True)):
        out = measure(s, ev)
        print(f"{label:30} measure={out} gate={gate(t, True, out)}")
    print("the first build passed every test and the gate still blocked because the median of nine minutes missed the two-minute target, while the second sample met it; the same tests were green both times, so they could not tell the two apart")

    section("3. Genuinely running: a missing measurement blocks")
    out = measure([2, 2, 3], ev)
    print("three samples:", out, "->", gate(True, True, out))
    print("a gate that treats no data as success would pass a change nobody measured, so too few samples is its own reason to block")

    section("4. Genuinely running: constraints and the gate")
    out = measure(after_fix, ev)
    print("outcome met, constraint violated:", gate(True, False, out))
    print("outcome met, tests failing      :", gate(False, True, out))
    print("everything holds                :", gate(True, True, out))
    print("a speed gain bought by breaking the read-only rule still blocks, because the outcome is one condition among several")

    section("5. Genuinely running: independent review, approval and target revision")
    print("builder and reviewer the same agent :", review("agent-a", "agent-a"))
    print("builder and reviewer different       :", review("agent-a", "agent-b"))
    for a in ("read_logs", "enable_auto_remediation"):
        print(f"approval needed for {a:26}: {approval_needed(a)}")
    print("revise target without evidence      :", may_revise_target(2, 4, "", "owner"))
    print("loosen target without citing baseline:", may_revise_target(2, 4, "the team prefers it", "owner"))
    print("loosen target citing baseline        :", may_revise_target(2, 4, "baseline measured at 12 minutes; 2 not reachable with current logs", "owner"))
    print("the builder cannot be its own independent reviewer, risky actions need a human, and a target moves only with evidence and an approver; here 'cites the baseline' is a keyword check on the note, which a careless note could satisfy")"}},{"type":"output","data":{"output":"

class Evidence:
    category: str
    source: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Step:
    step_id: int
    actor: str
    action: str
    inputs: tuple = ()
    outputs: tuple = ()
    friction: str = ""
    handoff_to: str = ""
    needs_authority: str = ""
    evidence: tuple = field(default_factory=tuple)


def validate_step(s):
    if s.step_id < 1:
        raise ValueError("Step ID must be positive")
    if not s.actor.strip() or not s.action.strip():
        raise ValueError("Actor and action are required")
    if not s.evidence:
        raise ValueError(f"Step {s.step_id} has no evidence")
    for e in s.evidence:
        if e.category not in CATEGORIES:
            raise ValueError(f"Step {s.step_id} has unknown evidence category: {e.category}")
    return s


def hidden_inputs(steps, available=()):
    produced, hidden = set(available), []
    for s in steps:
        for i in s.inputs:
            if i not in produced:
                hidden.append((s.step_id, i))
        produced.update(s.outputs)
    return hidden"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"wd_1.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() prints documented against observed steps, computes the direct-evidence ratio, finds hidden inputs, lists handoffs and authority boundaries and rejects three bad steps.","descKn":"main() ದಾಖಲಿತ ಮತ್ತು ವೀಕ್ಷಿತ ಹಂತಗಳನ್ನು ಮುದ್ರಿಸಿ, ನೇರ-ಸಾಕ್ಷ್ಯ ಅನುಪಾತ ಲೆಕ್ಕ ಹಾಕಿ, ಗುಪ್ತ ಒಳಹರಿವು ಹುಡುಕಿ, ಹಸ್ತಾಂತರ ಮತ್ತು ಅಧಿಕಾರ ಗಡಿ ಪಟ್ಟಿ ಮಾಡಿ ಮತ್ತು ಮೂರು ಕೆಟ್ಟ ಹಂತ ತಿರಸ್ಕರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    section("1. Genuinely running: the documented workflow versus the observed one")
    print("documented steps:", len(DOCUMENTED), "->", DOCUMENTED)
    print("observed steps  :", len(OBSERVED))
    for s in OBSERVED:
        validate_step(s)
        print(f"  {s.step_id}. {s.action:55} evidence={[e.category for e in s.evidence]}")
    print("the official procedure has six lines and the observed workflow has seven recorded steps, among them a manual search, a question to a colleague, a copy into chat and a wait for authorization that the procedure never mentions; the lab's steps and sources are invented")

    section("2. Genuinely measuring: how much of the workflow is directly evidenced")
    counts = {c: sum(1 for s in OBSERVED for e in s.evidence if e.category == c) for c in CATEGORIES}
    total = sum(counts.values())
    print("evidence by category:", counts)
    print(f"direct-evidence ratio: {counts['direct']}/{total} = {counts['direct'] / total:.2f}")
    print("steps resting only on reported or assumed evidence:", [s.step_id for s in OBSERVED if all(e.category in ('reported', 'assumed') for e in s.evidence)])
    print("three of seven pieces of evidence were direct observation, and steps 4, 6 and 7 rest only on what someone said or on inference; those are the steps to confirm before anything is built on them")

    section("3. Genuinely running: hidden state that no step produces")
    print("inputs with no producer:", hidden_inputs(OBSERVED))
    print("with approval token supplied by a person:", hidden_inputs(OBSERVED, available=("approval token",)))
    print("the workflow consumes an approval token that none of the recorded steps creates, which is the shape of hidden state: somebody holds it outside the system, and an automation that starts from step 6 would have nothing to hand over")

    section("4. Genuinely running: handoffs and authority")
    print("handoffs:", [(s.step_id, s.handoff_to) for s in OBSERVED if s.handoff_to])
    print("authority boundaries:", [(s.step_id, s.needs_authority) for s in OBSERVED if s.needs_authority])
    print("friction notes:", len([s for s in OBSERVED if s.friction]), "of", len(OBSERVED), "steps")
    print("three handoffs and one authority boundary appear only in the observed list; a workflow summary that leaves them out will describe a process that can be automated end to end when it cannot")

    section("5. Genuinely running: a step without evidence is refused")
    for label, s in (("no evidence", Step(8, "engineer", "close the incident")), ("bad category", Step(9, "engineer", "x", evidence=(Evidence("hunch", "me"),))), ("zero id", Step(0, "engineer", "x", evidence=(Evidence("direct", "a"),)))):
        try:
            validate_step(s)
            print(f"{label:14} accepted")
        except ValueError as e:
            print(f"{label:14} rejected: {e}")
    print("each step has to carry its own evidence from a known category, so an assumed step is visible as assumed instead of being mixed into a clean list")"}},{"type":"output","data":{"output":"

confidence ಲ್ಯಾಬ್‌ನ ಸ್ವಂತ ಮಿತಿ ಅನ್ವಯಿಸುತ್ತದೆ ಮತ್ತು summarize ಅಂಕದ ಪಕ್ಕ ದೃಢೀಕರಿಸದ ಹಂತ ಪಟ್ಟಿ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def validate_order(ids):
    if not ids:
        raise ValueError("Workflow must contain steps")
    if len(ids) != len(set(ids)):
        raise ValueError("Duplicate step IDs")
    if ids != sorted(ids):
        raise ValueError("Steps must be in ascending order")
    gaps = [b for a, b in zip(ids, ids[1:]) if b != a + 1]
    return {"ok": True, "gaps_before": gaps}


def direct_ratio(categories):
    if not categories:
        return None
    return sum(1 for c in categories if c == "direct") / len(categories)


def confidence(ratio, has_assumed):
    if ratio is None:
        return "unknown"
    if has_assumed:
        return "low" if ratio < 0.8 else "medium"
    return "high" if ratio >= 0.8 else ("medium" if ratio >= 0.5 else "low")


def summarize(steps):
    cats = [c for s in steps for c in s["evidence"]]
    r = direct_ratio(cats)
    return {"steps": len(steps), "direct_ratio": None if r is None else round(r, 2), "confidence": confidence(r, "assumed" in cats),
            "unconfirmed": [s["id"] for s in steps if not any(c == "direct" for c in s["evidence"])]}"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"wd_2.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() tries five id lists, scores four evidence sets, compares two workflows, checks a reported claim, compares workflow-level and per-step evidence and builds an artifact.","descKn":"main() ಐದು id ಪಟ್ಟಿ ಪ್ರಯತ್ನಿಸಿ, ನಾಲ್ಕು ಸಾಕ್ಷ್ಯ ಸೆಟ್‌ಗೆ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡಿ, ಎರಡು ಕಾರ್ಯಪ್ರವಾಹ ಹೋಲಿಸಿ, reported ಹೇಳಿಕೆ ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಿ, ಕಾರ್ಯಪ್ರವಾಹ-ಮಟ್ಟ ಮತ್ತು ಹಂತ-ಮಟ್ಟದ ಸಾಕ್ಷ್ಯ ಹೋಲಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ಕಲಾಕೃತಿ ನಿರ್ಮಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    section("1. Genuinely running: ordering rules")
    for label, ids in (("1,2,3,4", [1, 2, 3, 4]), ("1,3,4 (gap)", [1, 3, 4]), ("1,3,2", [1, 3, 2]), ("1,2,2", [1, 2, 2]), ("empty", [])):
        try:
            print(f"{label:14} accepted {validate_order(ids)}")
        except ValueError as e:
            print(f"{label:14} rejected: {e}")
    print("a gap in the numbering was accepted and reported, while out-of-order, duplicate and empty lists were refused; a gap may mean a step was removed on purpose, so it is surfaced for a person and not rejected")

    section("2. Genuinely computing: the direct-evidence ratio and its edge cases")
    for label, cats in (("all direct", ["direct"] * 4), ("half direct", ["direct", "direct", "reported", "document"]), ("one in four", ["direct", "reported", "reported", "assumed"]), ("no evidence at all", [])):
        r = direct_ratio(cats)
        print(f"{label:20} ratio={r} confidence={confidence(r, 'assumed' in cats)}")
    print("an empty list returned None and 'unknown' instead of a ratio of zero or a division error, because no evidence is different from evidence that was all indirect")

    section("3. Genuinely measuring: a ratio can hide where the weak steps are")
    wf_a = [{"id": i, "evidence": ["direct"]} for i in range(1, 5)] + [{"id": 5, "evidence": ["assumed"]}]
    wf_b = [{"id": 1, "evidence": ["direct", "direct", "direct", "direct"]}, {"id": 2, "evidence": ["reported"]}, {"id": 3, "evidence": ["reported"]}, {"id": 4, "evidence": ["reported"]}, {"id": 5, "evidence": ["reported"]}]
    for name, wf in (("workflow A", wf_a), ("workflow B", wf_b)):
        print(name, summarize(wf))
    print("A scored a ratio of 0.8 and B scored 0.5, and both received the same label, medium, even though A has one step that was only assumed and B has four steps that rest on talk alone; the label hid that difference, which is why the list of unconfirmed steps is reported next to it, and the thresholds in confidence() are this lab's own choice")

    section("3b. Genuinely running: reported behaviour is not upgraded")
    claim = {"id": 6, "evidence": ["reported"], "text": "engineers always wait for approval"}
    print("claim:", claim["text"], "| evidence:", claim["evidence"], "| counted as confirmed:", any(c == "direct" for c in claim["evidence"]))
    print("a statement that people always do something stays labelled reported until someone has watched it or read a record of it, so it appears in the unconfirmed list instead of the confirmed one")

    section("4. Genuinely running: per-step evidence versus a workflow-level claim")
    wf_level = {"workflow": "incident triage", "evidence": ["direct"]}
    print("workflow-level claim:", wf_level, "| steps it covers: unknown")
    print("per-step evidence for the same workflow:", [(s["id"], s["evidence"]) for s in wf_a])
    print("one line of evidence attached to the whole workflow cannot show that step 5 was only assumed; attaching evidence to each step is what makes the weak step visible")

    section("5. Genuinely running: the JSON artifact")
    art = {"workflow": "incident triage", "summary": summarize(wf_a), "steps": wf_a}
    text = json.dumps(art, sort_keys=True)
    print("artifact keys:", sorted(art), "| bytes:", len(text), "| round trip equal:", json.loads(text) == art)

confidence ಲ್ಯಾಬ್‌ನ ಸ್ವಂತ ಮಿತಿ ಅನ್ವಯಿಸುತ್ತದೆ ಮತ್ತು summarize ಅಂಕದ ಪಕ್ಕ ದೃಢೀಕರಿಸದ ಹಂತ ಪಟ್ಟಿ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def validate_order(ids):
    if not ids:
        raise ValueError("Workflow must contain steps")
    if len(ids) != len(set(ids)):
        raise ValueError("Duplicate step IDs")
    if ids != sorted(ids):
        raise ValueError("Steps must be in ascending order")
    gaps = [b for a, b in zip(ids, ids[1:]) if b != a + 1]
    return {"ok": True, "gaps_before": gaps}


def direct_ratio(categories):
    if not categories:
        return None
    return sum(1 for c in categories if c == "direct") / len(categories)


def confidence(ratio, has_assumed):
    if ratio is None:
        return "unknown"
    if has_assumed:
        return "low" if ratio < 0.8 else "medium"
    return "high" if ratio >= 0.8 else ("medium" if ratio >= 0.5 else "low")


def summarize(steps):
    cats = [c for s in steps for c in s["evidence"]]
    r = direct_ratio(cats)
    return {"steps": len(steps), "direct_ratio": None if r is None else round(r, 2), "confidence": confidence(r, "assumed" in cats),
            "unconfirmed": [s["id"] for s in steps if not any(c == "direct" for c in s["evidence"])]}"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"wd_2.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() tries five id lists, scores four evidence sets, compares two workflows, checks a reported claim, compares workflow-level and per-step evidence and builds an artifact.","descKn":"main() ಐದು id ಪಟ್ಟಿ ಪ್ರಯತ್ನಿಸಿ, ನಾಲ್ಕು ಸಾಕ್ಷ್ಯ ಸೆಟ್‌ಗೆ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡಿ, ಎರಡು ಕಾರ್ಯಪ್ರವಾಹ ಹೋಲಿಸಿ, reported ಹೇಳಿಕೆ ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಿ, ಕಾರ್ಯಪ್ರವಾಹ-ಮಟ್ಟ ಮತ್ತು ಹಂತ-ಮಟ್ಟದ ಸಾಕ್ಷ್ಯ ಹೋಲಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ಕಲಾಕೃತಿ ನಿರ್ಮಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    section("1. Genuinely running: ordering rules")
    for label, ids in (("1,2,3,4", [1, 2, 3, 4]), ("1,3,4 (gap)", [1, 3, 4]), ("1,3,2", [1, 3, 2]), ("1,2,2", [1, 2, 2]), ("empty", [])):
        try:
            print(f"{label:14} accepted {validate_order(ids)}")
        except ValueError as e:
            print(f"{label:14} rejected: {e}")
    print("a gap in the numbering was accepted and reported, while out-of-order, duplicate and empty lists were refused; a gap may mean a step was removed on purpose, so it is surfaced for a person and not rejected")

    section("2. Genuinely computing: the direct-evidence ratio and its edge cases")
    for label, cats in (("all direct", ["direct"] * 4), ("half direct", ["direct", "direct", "reported", "document"]), ("one in four", ["direct", "reported", "reported", "assumed"]), ("no evidence at all", [])):
        r = direct_ratio(cats)
        print(f"{label:20} ratio={r} confidence={confidence(r, 'assumed' in cats)}")
    print("an empty list returned None and 'unknown' instead of a ratio of zero or a division error, because no evidence is different from evidence that was all indirect")

    section("3. Genuinely measuring: a ratio can hide where the weak steps are")
    wf_a = [{"id": i, "evidence": ["direct"]} for i in range(1, 5)] + [{"id": 5, "evidence": ["assumed"]}]
    wf_b = [{"id": 1, "evidence": ["direct", "direct", "direct", "direct"]}, {"id": 2, "evidence": ["reported"]}, {"id": 3, "evidence": ["reported"]}, {"id": 4, "evidence": ["reported"]}, {"id": 5, "evidence": ["reported"]}]
    for name, wf in (("workflow A", wf_a), ("workflow B", wf_b)):
        print(name, summarize(wf))
    print("A scored a ratio of 0.8 and B scored 0.5, and both received the same label, medium, even though A has one step that was only assumed and B has four steps that rest on talk alone; the label hid that difference, which is why the list of unconfirmed steps is reported next to it, and the thresholds in confidence() are this lab's own choice")

    section("3b. Genuinely running: reported behaviour is not upgraded")
    claim = {"id": 6, "evidence": ["reported"], "text": "engineers always wait for approval"}

    print("a statement that people always do something stays labelled reported until someone has watched it or read a record of it, so it appears in the unconfirmed list instead of the confirmed one")

    section("4. Genuinely running: per-step evidence versus a workflow-level claim")
    wf_level = {"workflow": "incident triage", "evidence": ["direct"]}
    print("workflow-level claim:", wf_level, "| steps it covers: unknown")
    print("per-step evidence for the same workflow:", [(s["id"], s["evidence"]) for s in wf_a])
    print("one line of evidence attached to the whole workflow cannot show that step 5 was only assumed; attaching evidence to each step is what makes the weak step visible")

    section("5. Genuinely running: the JSON artifact")
    art = {"workflow": "incident triage", "summary": summarize(wf_a), "steps": wf_a}
    text = json.dumps(art, sort_keys=True)
    print("artifact keys:", sorted(art), "| bytes:", len(text), "| round trip equal:", json.loads(text) == art)

ನೀಡಿದವರೊಂದಿಗೆ ಉಳಿಸುತ್ತದೆ, approval_steps keyword ಮೂಲಕ ಹಂತ ಗುರುತಿಸುತ್ತದೆ ಮತ್ತು combined ಪ್ರತಿ ಶಾಖೆ ದೋಷ ಸಂಗ್ರಹಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def validate_branch(b):
    if b["from_step"] not in NORMAL:
        raise ValueError(f"Branch {b['id']} starts at unknown step {b['from_step']}")
    if not b.get("condition", "").strip():
        raise ValueError(f"Branch {b['id']} has no activating condition")
    if not b.get("evidence"):
        raise ValueError(f"Branch {b['id']} has no evidence")
    return b


def finding(record):
    if record is None:
        return "missing: not recorded (unknown)"
    if record is False:
        return "negative: checked and nothing was found"
    return f"found: {record}"


def merge_variants(reports):
    by = {}
    for who, answer in reports:
        by.setdefault(answer, []).append(who)
    return {"agreed": len(by) == 1, "variants": by}


def approval_steps(steps):
    return [k for k, v in steps.items() if "approval" in v or "execute" in v]


def combined(normal, branches):
    errors = []
    for b in branches:
        try:
            validate_branch(b)
        except ValueError as e:
            errors.append(str(e))
    return {"steps": len(normal), "branches": len(branches), "errors": errors}"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"wd_3.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() attaches three branches, rejects three bad ones, compares missing and negative findings, merges two sets of answers and runs the combined check with and without a bad branch.","descKn":"main() ಮೂರು ಶಾಖೆ ಜೋಡಿಸಿ, ಮೂರು ಕೆಟ್ಟವನ್ನು ತಿರಸ್ಕರಿಸಿ, ಕಾಣೆಯಾದ ಮತ್ತು ಋಣಾತ್ಮಕ ಶೋಧನೆ ಹೋಲಿಸಿ, ಎರಡು ಉತ್ತರ ಸೆಟ್ ವಿಲೀನಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ಕೆಟ್ಟ ಶಾಖೆ ಸಹಿತ ಮತ್ತು ರಹಿತ ಸಂಯೋಜಿತ ಪರಿಶೀಲನೆ ಓಡಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    section("1. Genuinely running: exception branches attach to a step")
    branches = [{"id": "B1", "from_step": 3, "condition": "deployment record is missing", "evidence": ["interview A", "deploy log gap"]},
                {"id": "B2", "from_step": 4, "condition": "service owner is unavailable", "evidence": ["chat transcript"]},
                {"id": "B3", "from_step": 6, "condition": "remediation needs the incident commander", "evidence": ["interview B"]}]
    for b in branches:
        validate_branch(b)
        print(f"{b['id']} starts after step {b['from_step']} ({NORMAL[b['from_step']]}) when {b['condition']}")
    print("each branch names the step it leaves, the condition that activates it and its evidence, and the normal sequence stays one clean list; the branches are invented for the lab")

    section("2. Genuinely running: invalid branches are rejected")
    for label, b in (("unknown step", {"id": "X1", "from_step": 12, "condition": "c", "evidence": ["e"]}), ("no condition", {"id": "X2", "from_step": 3, "condition": " ", "evidence": ["e"]}), ("no evidence", {"id": "X3", "from_step": 3, "condition": "c", "evidence": []})):
        try:
            validate_branch(b)
            print(f"{label:14} accepted")
        except ValueError as e:
            print(f"{label:14} rejected: {e}")
    print("a branch that hangs off a step that does not exist, or that cannot say when it applies or why it is believed, would make the combined workflow impossible to follow")

    section("3. Genuinely running: missing information is not a negative finding")
    for label, rec in (("deployment record not exported", None), ("searched the log, no deployment in the window", False), ("deployment d-881 at 14:02", "d-881 at 14:02")):
        print(f"{label:46} -> {finding(rec)}")
    print("None and False look alike in a loose check, and the lab keeps them apart: not knowing whether a deployment happened and knowing that none happened lead to different next steps")
    print("a falsy test treats them the same:", [bool(x) for x in (None, False)])

    section("4. Genuinely running: stakeholders who disagree")
    print(merge_variants([("engineer A", "asks a colleague for the owner"), ("engineer B", "asks a colleague for the owner"), ("manager", "looks the owner up in the service catalogue")]))
    print(merge_variants([("engineer A", "waits for approval"), ("engineer B", "waits for approval")]))
    print("two answers about the owner step were kept side by side with who gave each, instead of being averaged or replaced by the manager's version; the disagreement is itself a finding, since the catalogue may exist and not be used")

    section("5. Genuinely running: approval boundaries and the combined check")
    print("steps that need approval or act on production:", approval_steps(NORMAL))
    print("combined report:", combined(NORMAL, branches))
    print("combined with a bad branch:", combined(NORMAL, branches + [{"id": "X1", "from_step": 12, "condition": "c", "evidence": ["e"]}]))
    print("steps 6 and 7 are marked because of the words approval and execute in their names, which is a keyword rule and would miss a step called 'confirm with commander'; the combined check reports every error at once and does not stop at the first")"}},{"type":"output","data":{"output":"

    if b["from_step"] not in NORMAL:
        raise ValueError(f"Branch {b['id']} starts at unknown step {b['from_step']}")
    if not b.get("condition", "").strip():
        raise ValueError(f"Branch {b['id']} has no activating condition")
    if not b.get("evidence"):
        raise ValueError(f"Branch {b['id']} has no evidence")
    return b


def finding(record):
    if record is None:
        return "missing: not recorded (unknown)"
    if record is False:
        return "negative: checked and nothing was found"
    return f"found: {record}"


def merge_variants(reports):
    by = {}
    for who, answer in reports:
        by.setdefault(answer, []).append(who)
    return {"agreed": len(by) == 1, "variants": by}


def approval_steps(steps):
    return [k for k, v in steps.items() if "approval" in v or "execute" in v]


def combined(normal, branches):
    errors = []
    for b in branches:
        try:
            validate_branch(b)
        except ValueError as e:
            errors.append(str(e))
    return {"steps": len(normal), "branches": len(branches), "errors": errors}"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"wd_3.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() attaches three branches, rejects three bad ones, compares missing and negative findings, merges two sets of answers and runs the combined check with and without a bad branch.","descKn":"main() ಮೂರು ಶಾಖೆ ಜೋಡಿಸಿ, ಮೂರು ಕೆಟ್ಟವನ್ನು ತಿರಸ್ಕರಿಸಿ, ಕಾಣೆಯಾದ ಮತ್ತು ಋಣಾತ್ಮಕ ಶೋಧನೆ ಹೋಲಿಸಿ, ಎರಡು ಉತ್ತರ ಸೆಟ್ ವಿಲೀನಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ಕೆಟ್ಟ ಶಾಖೆ ಸಹಿತ ಮತ್ತು ರಹಿತ ಸಂಯೋಜಿತ ಪರಿಶೀಲನೆ ಓಡಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    section("1. Genuinely running: exception branches attach to a step")

    for b in branches:

        print(f"{b['id']} starts after step {b['from_step']} ({NORMAL[b['from_step']]}) when {b['condition']}")
    print("each branch names the step it leaves, the condition that activates it and its evidence, and the normal sequence stays one clean list; the branches are invented for the lab")

    section("2. Genuinely running: invalid branches are rejected")
    for label, b in (("unknown step", {"id": "X1", "from_step": 12, "condition": "c", "evidence": ["e"]}), ("no condition", {"id": "X2", "from_step": 3, "condition": " ", "evidence": ["e"]}), ("no evidence", {"id": "X3", "from_step": 3, "condition": "c", "evidence": []})):
        try:
            validate_branch(b)
            print(f"{label:14} accepted")
        except ValueError as e:
            print(f"{label:14} rejected: {e}")
    print("a branch that hangs off a step that does not exist, or that cannot say when it applies or why it is believed, would make the combined workflow impossible to follow")

    section("3. Genuinely running: missing information is not a negative finding")
    for label, rec in (("deployment record not exported", None), ("searched the log, no deployment in the window", False), ("deployment d-881 at 14:02", "d-881 at 14:02")):
        print(f"{label:46} -> {finding(rec)}")
    print("None and False look alike in a loose check, and the lab keeps them apart: not knowing whether a deployment happened and knowing that none happened lead to different next steps")
    print("a falsy test treats them the same:", [bool(x) for x in (None, False)])

    section("4. Genuinely running: stakeholders who disagree")
    print(merge_variants([("engineer A", "asks a colleague for the owner"), ("engineer B", "asks a colleague for the owner"), ("manager", "looks the owner up in the service catalogue")]))
    print(merge_variants([("engineer A", "waits for approval"), ("engineer B", "waits for approval")]))
    print("two answers about the owner step were kept side by side with who gave each, instead of being averaged or replaced by the manager's version; the disagreement is itself a finding, since the catalogue may exist and not be used")

    section("5. Genuinely running: approval boundaries and the combined check")
    print("steps that need approval or act on production:", approval_steps(NORMAL))
    print("combined report:", combined(NORMAL, branches))
    print("combined with a bad branch:", combined(NORMAL, branches + [{"id": "X1", "from_step": 12, "condition": "c", "evidence": ["e"]}]))

class Assumption:
    aid: str
    claim: str
    impact: int
    uncertainty: int
    irreversibility: int
    status: str = "open"


def validate(a):
    for n in ("impact", "uncertainty", "irreversibility"):
        v = getattr(a, n)
        if not isinstance(v, int) or isinstance(v, bool) or not 1 <= v <= 5:
            raise ValueError(f"{a.aid}: {n} must be an integer from 1 to 5")
    if not a.claim.strip():
        raise ValueError(f"{a.aid}: claim is required")
    return a


def falsifiable(claim):
    c = claim.lower()
    has_number = bool(re.search(r"\d", c)) or any(w in c for w in ("at least", "at most", "fewer", "more than", "without"))
    vague = [w for w in ("good", "useful", "intelligent", "easy", "trust") if re.search(r"\b" + w + r"\b", c)]
    return {"has_threshold_or_condition": has_number, "vague_words": vague}


def score_product(a):
    return a.impact * a.uncertainty * a.irreversibility


def score_sum(a):
    return a.impact + a.uncertainty + a.irreversibility


def rank(items, key):
    return [a.aid for a in sorted((x for x in items if x.status == "open"), key=lambda a: (-key(a), -a.irreversibility, a.aid))]"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"am_1.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() scores five assumptions, ranks them two ways, breaks a three-way tie, checks four claims for falsifiability and rejects five bad records.","descKn":"main() ಐದು ಊಹೆಗಳಿಗೆ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡಿ, ಎರಡು ರೀತಿ ಶ್ರೇಣೀಕರಿಸಿ, ಮೂರು-ಮಾರ್ಗ tie ಮುರಿದು, ನಾಲ್ಕು ಹೇಳಿಕೆಗಳನ್ನು ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ಐದು ಕೆಟ್ಟ ದಾಖಲೆ ತಿರಸ್ಕರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    section("1. Genuinely running: the assumption map and its scores (ratings are invented)")
    for a in MAP:
        validate(a)
        print(f"{a.aid} impact={a.impact} uncertainty={a.uncertainty} irreversibility={a.irreversibility} product={score_product(a):3} sum={score_sum(a):2}  {a.claim[:60]}")
    print("each hidden belief became a record with three ratings, and the ratings are the team's own judgement on a 1 to 5 scale, not measurements")

    section("2. Genuinely running: ranking by product and by sum")
    print("by product:", rank(MAP, score_product))
    print("by sum    :", rank(MAP, score_sum))
    print("the rules disagree about the top item: the product put A1 first with 60 against 50 for A3 and A4, while the sum scored A1, A3 and A4 all at 12 and the tie-break on irreversibility put A3 first; A2 and A5 kept their places in both")
    print("the rule is a choice the team makes and should state, since the same ratings ranked differently; the lab uses the product so that one low rating pulls a risk down")

    section("3. Genuinely running: ties are broken by irreversibility")
    tie = [Assumption("T1", "Claim one at least 3", 4, 3, 2), Assumption("T2", "Claim two at least 3", 3, 4, 2), Assumption("T3", "Claim three at least 3", 2, 3, 4)]
    print("products:", {a.aid: score_product(a) for a in tie})
    print("ranked:", rank(tie, score_product))
    print("three assumptions scored 24 each and the order came from the tie-break, which puts the least reversible one first and then falls back to the id; without a stated tie-break the order would depend on how the list was written")

    section("4. Genuinely measuring: is the claim falsifiable")
    for c in ("The assistant is intelligent and useful", "At least 90 percent of alerts name the failing service", "Engineers trust the tool", "The tool runs without write permission to production"):
        print(f"{c[:56]:58} {falsifiable(c)}")
    print("a claim with a threshold or a condition can be shown wrong by an observation, and one made of words like intelligent and trust cannot; the check is a keyword heuristic, so a claim like 'works well enough' would also slip through without being flagged")

    section("5. Genuinely running: invalid ratings are rejected")
    for label, kw in (("rating 0", dict(impact=0)), ("rating 6", dict(uncertainty=6)), ("float rating", dict(irreversibility=2.5)), ("bool rating", dict(impact=True)), ("blank claim", dict(claim=" "))):
        base = dict(aid="X", claim="c", impact=3, uncertainty=3, irreversibility=3)

tie-break ನೊಂದಿಗೆ ವಿಂಗಡಿಸುತ್ತದೆ, ಮತ್ತು falsifiable ಮಿತಿ ಅಥವಾ ಷರತ್ತು ಮತ್ತು ಅಸ್ಪಷ್ಟ ಪದಗಳನ್ನು ಹುಡುಕುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Assumption:
    aid: str
    claim: str
    impact: int
    uncertainty: int
    irreversibility: int
    status: str = "open"


def validate(a):
    for n in ("impact", "uncertainty", "irreversibility"):
        v = getattr(a, n)
        if not isinstance(v, int) or isinstance(v, bool) or not 1 <= v <= 5:
            raise ValueError(f"{a.aid}: {n} must be an integer from 1 to 5")
    if not a.claim.strip():
        raise ValueError(f"{a.aid}: claim is required")
    return a


def falsifiable(claim):
    c = claim.lower()
    has_number = bool(re.search(r"\d", c)) or any(w in c for w in ("at least", "at most", "fewer", "more than", "without"))
    vague = [w for w in ("good", "useful", "intelligent", "easy", "trust") if re.search(r"\b" + w + r"\b", c)]
    return {"has_threshold_or_condition": has_number, "vague_words": vague}


def score_product(a):
    return a.impact * a.uncertainty * a.irreversibility


def score_sum(a):
    return a.impact + a.uncertainty + a.irreversibility


def rank(items, key):
    return [a.aid for a in sorted((x for x in items if x.status == "open"), key=lambda a: (-key(a), -a.irreversibility, a.aid))]"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"am_1.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() scores five assumptions, ranks them two ways, breaks a three-way tie, checks four claims for falsifiability and rejects five bad records.","descKn":"main() ಐದು ಊಹೆಗಳಿಗೆ ಅಂಕ ನೀಡಿ, ಎರಡು ರೀತಿ ಶ್ರೇಣೀಕರಿಸಿ, ಮೂರು-ಮಾರ್ಗ tie ಮುರಿದು, ನಾಲ್ಕು ಹೇಳಿಕೆಗಳನ್ನು ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ಐದು ಕೆಟ್ಟ ದಾಖಲೆ ತಿರಸ್ಕರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    section("1. Genuinely running: the assumption map and its scores (ratings are invented)")
    for a in MAP:
        validate(a)
        print(f"{a.aid} impact={a.impact} uncertainty={a.uncertainty} irreversibility={a.irreversibility} product={score_product(a):3} sum={score_sum(a):2}  {a.claim[:60]}")
    print("each hidden belief became a record with three ratings, and the ratings are the team's own judgement on a 1 to 5 scale, not measurements")

    section("2. Genuinely running: ranking by product and by sum")
    print("by product:", rank(MAP, score_product))
    print("by sum    :", rank(MAP, score_sum))
    print("the rules disagree about the top item: the product put A1 first with 60 against 50 for A3 and A4, while the sum scored A1, A3 and A4 all at 12 and the tie-break on irreversibility put A3 first; A2 and A5 kept their places in both")
    print("the rule is a choice the team makes and should state, since the same ratings ranked differently; the lab uses the product so that one low rating pulls a risk down")

    section("3. Genuinely running: ties are broken by irreversibility")
    tie = [Assumption("T1", "Claim one at least 3", 4, 3, 2), Assumption("T2", "Claim two at least 3", 3, 4, 2), Assumption("T3", "Claim three at least 3", 2, 3, 4)]
    print("products:", {a.aid: score_product(a) for a in tie})
    print("ranked:", rank(tie, score_product))
    print("three assumptions scored 24 each and the order came from the tie-break, which puts the least reversible one first and then falls back to the id; without a stated tie-break the order would depend on how the list was written")

    section("4. Genuinely measuring: is the claim falsifiable")
    for c in ("The assistant is intelligent and useful", "At least 90 percent of alerts name the failing service", "Engineers trust the tool", "The tool runs without write permission to production"):
        print(f"{c[:56]:58} {falsifiable(c)}")
    print("a claim with a threshold or a condition can be shown wrong by an observation, and one made of words like intelligent and trust cannot; the check is a keyword heuristic, so a claim like 'works well enough' would also slip through without being flagged")

    section("5. Genuinely running: invalid ratings are rejected")
    for label, kw in (("rating 0", dict(impact=0)), ("rating 6", dict(uncertainty=6)), ("float rating", dict(irreversibility=2.5)), ("bool rating", dict(impact=True)), ("blank claim", dict(claim=" "))):
        base = dict(aid="X", claim="c", impact=3, uncertainty=3, irreversibility=3)
        base.update(kw)
        try:
            validate(Assumption(**base))
            print(f"{label:14} accepted")
        except ValueError as e:
            print(f"{label:14} rejected: {e}")
    print("ratings must be whole numbers from 1 to 5, and a bool was refused explicitly because True would otherwise pass as 1")"}},{"type":"output","data":{"output":"

ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ ಮತ್ತು EvidenceLog ನಮೂದುಗಳನ್ನು ಸೇರಿಸಿ ಮಾತ್ರ supersession ದಾಖಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def wilson(successes, n, z=1.96):
    if n == 0:
        return (0.0, 1.0)
    p = successes / n
    d = 1 + z * z / n
    centre = (p + z * z / (2 * n)) / d
    half = z * math.sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + z * z / (4 * n * n)) / d
    return (max(0.0, centre - half), min(1.0, centre + half))


def verdict(successes, n, threshold):
    lo, hi = wilson(successes, n)
    if lo >= threshold:
        return "supports", (round(lo, 3), round(hi, 3))
    if hi < threshold:
        return "rejects", (round(lo, 3), round(hi, 3))
    return "ambiguous", (round(lo, 3), round(hi, 3))


def lock(experiment):
    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(experiment, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()[:10]


class EvidenceLog:
    def __init__(self):
        self.entries = []

    def add(self, exp_hash, successes, n, note):
        self.entries.append({"exp": exp_hash, "successes": successes, "n": n, "note": note})

    def supersede(self, index, note):
        self.entries.append({"supersedes": index, "note": note})"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"am_2.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() locks an experiment, computes six verdicts, moves a threshold, compares a biased and a mixed sample and appends evidence.","descKn":"main() ಪ್ರಯೋಗ ಲಾಕ್ ಮಾಡಿ, ಆರು ತೀರ್ಪು ಲೆಕ್ಕ ಹಾಕಿ, ಮಿತಿ ಸರಿಸಿ, ಪಕ್ಷಪಾತ ಮತ್ತು ಮಿಶ್ರ ಮಾದರಿ ಹೋಲಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ಸಾಕ್ಷ್ಯ ಸೇರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    exp = {"claim": "at least 90 percent of alerts identify the failing service", "threshold": 0.90, "population": "alerts from the last 30 days", "min_sample": 50}
    section("1. Genuinely running: the experiment is fixed before the data (made-up alert counts)")
    h = lock(exp)
    print("experiment:", exp, "| lock:", h)
    print("the claim, the threshold, the population and the sample minimum were written down and hashed before any alert was looked at, so a changed threshold shows up as a different hash")

    section("2. Genuinely computing: the same observed rate gives different verdicts at different sample sizes")
    for ok, n in ((46, 50), (92, 100), (460, 500), (475, 500), (45, 50), (400, 500)):
        v, ci = verdict(ok, n, exp["threshold"])
        print(f"{ok:4}/{n:<4} rate={ok / n:.2f}  95% Wilson interval={ci}  verdict={v}")
    print("the same 92 percent was ambiguous at 50, 100 and even 500 alerts because the lower end of the interval stayed under 0.90 (0.893 at 500), and only 475/500 = 95 percent cleared the threshold; 400/500 = 80 percent was the one far enough below for the whole interval to sit under 0.90; a point estimate alone would have said supports for the first four rows")

    section("3. Genuinely running: moving the threshold after the data is detectable")
    after = dict(exp, threshold=0.80)
    print("original lock:", lock(exp), "| lock after edit:", lock(after), "| same:", lock(exp) == lock(after))
    print("verdict at 0.90 for 46/50:", verdict(46, 50, 0.90)[0], "| at the edited 0.80:", verdict(46, 50, 0.80)[0])
    print("lowering the threshold from 0.90 to 0.80 turned the same 46 of 50 from ambiguous into supports, which is exactly the move the lock exposes; the lab compares hashes and a team would have to check them in review")

    section("4. Genuinely measuring: a sample that does not represent the population")
    population = [("payments", 0.70)] * 40 + [("search", 0.97)] * 60
    overall = sum(p for _, p in population) / len(population)
    biased = [p for s, p in population if s == "search"]
    print(f"rate over all alerts (service mix 40 payments, 60 search): {overall:.3f}")
    print(f"rate over a sample drawn only from search: {sum(biased) / len(biased):.3f}")
    print("an experiment that only looked at the well-behaved service reported 0.97 while the mixed population was 0.862, so the population definition has to say which alerts count; the numbers are invented for the lab")

    section("5. Genuinely running: evidence is appended and never overwritten")
    log = EvidenceLog()
    log.add(h, 46, 50, "first pass")
    log.add(h, 460, 500, "full 30 days")
    log.supersede(0, "first pass used only the first week")
    for e in log.entries:
        print(e)
    print("the first result is still in the log with a note saying it was superseded, so a reader can see what was believed at each point; an update in place would have lost the earlier reading")"}},{"type":"output","data":{"output":"

ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ ಮತ್ತು EvidenceLog ನಮೂದುಗಳನ್ನು ಸೇರಿಸಿ ಮಾತ್ರ supersession ದಾಖಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def wilson(successes, n, z=1.96):
    if n == 0:
        return (0.0, 1.0)
    p = successes / n
    d = 1 + z * z / n
    centre = (p + z * z / (2 * n)) / d
    half = z * math.sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n + z * z / (4 * n * n)) / d
    return (max(0.0, centre - half), min(1.0, centre + half))


def verdict(successes, n, threshold):
    lo, hi = wilson(successes, n)
    if lo >= threshold:
        return "supports", (round(lo, 3), round(hi, 3))
    if hi < threshold:
        return "rejects", (round(lo, 3), round(hi, 3))
    return "ambiguous", (round(lo, 3), round(hi, 3))


def lock(experiment):
    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(experiment, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()[:10]


class EvidenceLog:
    def __init__(self):
        self.entries = []

    def add(self, exp_hash, successes, n, note):
        self.entries.append({"exp": exp_hash, "successes": successes, "n": n, "note": note})

    def supersede(self, index, note):
        self.entries.append({"supersedes": index, "note": note})"}},{"type":"code","data":{"filename":"am_2.py","headingEn":"main(): five experiments","headingKn":"main(): ಐದು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು","descEn":"main() locks an experiment, computes six verdicts, moves a threshold, compares a biased and a mixed sample and appends evidence.","descKn":"main() ಪ್ರಯೋಗ ಲಾಕ್ ಮಾಡಿ, ಆರು ತೀರ್ಪು ಲೆಕ್ಕ ಹಾಕಿ, ಮಿತಿ ಸರಿಸಿ, ಪಕ್ಷಪಾತ ಮತ್ತು ಮಿಶ್ರ ಮಾದರಿ ಹೋಲಿಸಿ ಮತ್ತು ಸಾಕ್ಷ್ಯ ಸೇರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.","code":"def main():
    exp = {"claim": "at least 90 percent of alerts identify the failing service", "threshold": 0.90, "population": "alerts from the last 30 days", "min_sample": 50}
    section("1. Genuinely running: the experiment is fixed before the data (made-up alert counts)")
    h = lock(exp)
    print("experiment:", exp, "| lock:", h)
    print("the claim, the threshold, the population and the sample minimum were written down and hashed before any alert was looked at, so a changed threshold shows up as a different hash")

    section("2. Genuinely computing: the same observed rate gives different verdicts at different sample sizes")
    for ok, n in ((46, 50), (92, 100), (460, 500), (475, 500), (45, 50), (400, 500)):
        v, ci = verdict(ok, n, exp["threshold"])
        print(f"{ok:4}/{n:<4} rate={ok / n:.2f}  95% Wilson interval={ci}  verdict={v}")
    print("the same 92 percent was ambiguous at 50, 100 and even 500 alerts because the lower end of the interval stayed under 0.90 (0.893 at 500), and only 475/500 = 95 percent cleared the threshold; 400/500 = 80 percent was the one far enough below for the whole interval to sit under 0.90; a point estimate alone would have said supports for the first four rows")

    section("3. Genuinely running: moving the threshold after the data is detectable")
    after = dict(exp, threshold=0.80)
    print("original lock:", lock(exp), "| lock after edit:", lock(after), "| same:", lock(exp) == lock(after))
    print("verdict at 0.90 for 46/50:", verdict(46, 50, 0.90)[0], "| at the edited 0.80:", verdict(46, 50, 0.80)[0])
    print("lowering the threshold from 0.90 to 0.80 turned the same 46 of 50 from ambiguous into supports, which is exactly the move the lock exposes; the lab compares hashes and a team would have to check them in review")

    section("4. Genuinely measuring: a sample that does not represent the population")
    population = [("payments", 0.70)] * 40 + [("search", 0.97)] * 60
    overall = sum(p for _, p in population) / len(population)
    biased = [p for s, p in population if s == "search"]
    print(f"rate over all alerts (service mix 40 payments, 60 search): {overall:.3f}")
    print(f"rate over a sample drawn only from search: {sum(biased) / len(biased):.3f}")
    print("an experiment that only looked at the well-behaved service reported 0.97 while the mixed population was 0.862, so the population definition has to say which alerts count; the numbers are invented for the lab")

    section("5. Genuinely running: evidence is appended and never overwritten")
    log = EvidenceLog()
    log.add(h, 46, 50, "first pass")
    log.add(h, 460, 500, "full 30 days")
    log.supersede(0, "first pass used only the first week")
